title.zh: 结核病
title.en: Tuberculosis

summary.zh: 从传播、感染到就医，读懂结核病。
summary.en: Understand transmission, infection and seeking care.

body.zh:
## 认识疾病
结核病由结核分枝杆菌引起，最常影响肺部，也可能影响其他器官。它可以预防，也可以治愈。

## 传播与感染
肺结核患者可通过空气传播结核菌。结核感染与结核病不同：感染者通常没有症状，也不具有传染性；只有一部分人会发病。

## 识别与行动
持续咳嗽、发热、盗汗或不明原因的体重下降，需要及时就医。症状不能单独确诊。是否需要检查和治疗，应由医务人员评估。

## 感染就一定会生病？
不是。感染与发病是不同状态，不能仅凭接触经历给人贴标签。

## 日常做法
不凭症状自行判断，出现持续症状时就医。
body.en:
## Understanding TB
TB is caused by bacteria. It usually affects the lungs but can involve other organs. It is preventable and curable.

## Transmission and infection
Lung TB can spread through the air. TB infection differs from TB disease: infected people generally have no symptoms and are not contagious. Only some develop disease.

## Recognize and act
Seek medical care for a prolonged cough, fever, night sweats or unexplained weight loss. Symptoms alone do not establish a diagnosis. A health professional assesses testing and treatment.

## Does infection always mean illness?
No. Infection and disease are different states; exposure alone does not justify labelling someone.

## In practice
Seek care for persistent symptoms instead of self-diagnosing.

sources.title: WHO · Tuberculosis

imageAlt: Laboratory microscope, illustrative photograph

title.zh: 结核病传播：需要关注的是共同呼吸的空气
title.en: TB transmission: focus on the air we share

summary.zh: 握手不是结核病的传播途径。了解空气传播，才能把预防措施用在关键处。
summary.en: Handshakes do not transmit TB. Understanding airborne spread helps us focus prevention where it matters.

body.zh:
## 传播发生在哪里？
具有传染性的肺部或喉部结核病患者咳嗽、说话或唱歌时，可将结核菌释放到空气中。其他人吸入后可能感染。室内空气流通差、共同停留时间长，会增加接触机会。

## 哪些担心需要纠正？
结核病不是通过握手、分享食物或接触马桶座传播的。但与患者在同一房间共处，可能涉及空气暴露。不能把餐具当作风险判断的重点，也不能凭一次接触认定自己已感染。

## 把知识用于生活
关注教室和宿舍的空气流通。如果收到密切接触者筛查通知，按学校和当地卫生部门安排接受评估。保护患者隐私，配合检查，比给人贴标签更有帮助。
body.en:
## Where does exposure happen?
Infectious TB in the lungs or throat can release bacteria into the air during coughing, speaking or singing. Others may inhale them. Poor airflow and prolonged time together increase opportunities for exposure.

## Correct the misconception
TB does not spread through handshakes, shared food or toilet seats. Sharing a room can involve airborne exposure, however. Neither cutlery nor a single encounter tells you whether you are infected.

## Put it into practice
Pay attention to classroom and dormitory airflow. Follow school and local health authority instructions for contact screening. Protect privacy and support assessment rather than labelling classmates.

sources.title: CDC · Tuberculosis: Causes and How It Spreads

imageAlt: Illustrated classroom with open windows; educational illustration

title.zh: 结核筛查阳性，就代表会传染吗？
title.en: Does a positive TB screening test mean you are contagious?

summary.zh: 分清感染与发病，读懂皮肤试验和血液检测能告诉我们什么。
summary.en: Separate infection from disease and understand what skin and blood tests can tell us.

body.zh:
## 检测阳性不等于确诊活动性结核病
结核皮肤试验和血液检测主要用于判断结核感染。结果阳性后，医务人员还需要结合症状、胸部影像，有时还包括痰液检查，判断是潜伏感染还是活动性结核病。

## 感染与传染不是一回事
潜伏结核感染者没有结核病症状，不向他人传播结核菌，但以后可能发病。医生会评估是否需要预防性治疗。不能仅凭筛查结果排斥同学。

## 检查前告诉医生什么？
说明是否接种过卡介苗、有无相关症状及接触史。卡介苗可能影响皮肤试验，结核血液检测不受它影响。具体选哪种检查、如何解读结果，应由医务人员决定。
body.en:
## A positive screen is not an active-TB diagnosis
TB skin and blood tests assess infection. After a positive result, clinicians use symptoms, chest imaging and sometimes sputum tests to distinguish latent infection from active disease.

## Infection is not contagiousness
People with latent TB infection have no TB symptoms and cannot transmit TB bacteria, but may develop disease later. A clinician assesses preventive treatment. A screening result alone is no reason to exclude a classmate.

## What should you tell the clinician?
Report BCG vaccination, symptoms and exposure history. BCG can affect a skin test; TB blood tests are unaffected. Test selection and interpretation require professional assessment.

sources.title: CDC · Testing for Tuberculosis
CDC · About Tuberculosis

title.zh: 洗手的 20 秒，应该洗到哪些地方？
title.en: What should those 20 seconds of handwashing cover?

summary.zh: 从洗手时机到指缝、指甲，学会比简单冲水更有效的手卫生。
summary.en: Learn when to wash and why fingers and nails need more than a quick rinse.

body.zh:
## 为什么不只是冲一下？
手上的病原体可能在触摸眼、鼻、口或进食时进入身体。用肥皂搓洗能帮助去除病原体。打湿双手、涂肥皂后，搓洗至少 20 秒，覆盖手背、指缝和指甲下方，再用流动水冲净、擦干。

## 把握关键时机
饭前、如厕后、擤鼻涕或咳嗽后，尤其应洗手。用纸巾或肘部遮挡咳嗽，可减少直接污染双手。

## 洗手液和免洗消毒剂怎么选？
没有肥皂和水时，可使用酒精含量至少 60% 的免洗手消毒剂，按产品说明揉搓至干。双手明显脏污或油腻时优先用肥皂和水；免洗消毒剂不能清除所有类型的病原体。
body.en:
## More than a rinse
Germs on hands can enter through your eyes, nose or mouth, or during eating. Wet your hands, add soap and scrub for at least 20 seconds, including backs, between fingers and under nails. Rinse with running water and dry.

## Choose the right moments
Wash before eating, after using the toilet and after blowing your nose or coughing. Cough into a tissue or elbow to avoid contaminating your hands.

## When water is unavailable
Use sanitizer with at least 60% alcohol and follow its directions until hands are dry. Soap and water are preferable for visibly dirty or greasy hands; sanitizer does not remove every type of germ.

sources.title: CDC · About Handwashing
CDC · Hand Sanitizer Guidelines and Recommendations

imageAlt: Illustrated hands washing with soap at a sink; educational illustration

title.zh: 预防呼吸道感染，为什么也要关心空气？
title.en: Why cleaner air matters for respiratory infections

summary.zh: 擦干净桌面之外，空气流通也是减少部分病原体暴露的重要环节。
summary.en: Beyond clean surfaces, airflow can help reduce exposure to some respiratory pathogens.

body.zh:
## 病原体不只停留在物体表面
一些呼吸道病毒可随感染者呼出的颗粒进入空气。在拥挤、通风不足的室内，颗粒更容易积聚。因此，擦桌子不能替代改善空气流通。

## 怎样改善室内空气？
在安全、室外空气质量允许时，开窗或开门引入新鲜空气。场所管理者也可维护通风系统，使用适合房间大小的空气净化设备。室外活动通常比空气流通差的室内活动更有利于减少空气中的病毒暴露。

## 多种措施共同起作用
通风能降低风险，却不能保证完全不感染。手卫生、按当地建议接种疫苗、生病时减少与他人接触，以及按风险使用口罩，都有各自作用。具体措施应结合学校通知和当地卫生建议。
body.en:
## Germs are not only on surfaces
Some respiratory viruses enter the air in particles exhaled by infected people. They can accumulate in crowded, poorly ventilated rooms. Cleaning desks cannot replace better airflow.

## Improve the air
Open windows or doors when safe and outdoor air quality permits. Building managers can maintain ventilation and use appropriately sized air cleaners. Outdoor activities generally reduce airborne virus exposure compared with poorly ventilated indoor settings.

## Combine protections
Ventilation reduces risk without eliminating it. Hand hygiene, locally recommended vaccinations, limiting contact when ill and risk-based mask use each have a role. Follow school and local health guidance.

sources.title: CDC · Taking Steps for Cleaner Air for Respiratory Virus Prevention

imageAlt: Illustrated hand opening a window in a bright room; educational illustration

title.zh: 一顿饭的均衡，从食物种类开始
title.en: A balanced meal starts with variety

summary.zh: 不用追逐“超级食物”，先看看餐盘里有哪些不同食物。
summary.en: Before chasing superfoods, look at the different foods on your plate.

body.zh:
## 没有一种食物能包办营养
不同食物提供不同营养成分。均衡饮食关注整体模式：摄入充足、搭配平衡、适量并保持多样。只吃某种“健康食物”，也可能遗漏身体需要的营养。

## 用一顿饭练习观察
例如米饭、豆腐和青菜的组合，包含主食、蛋白质来源和蔬菜。可在日常搭配中轮换全谷物、豆类、鱼、蛋、奶及不同蔬果。这个例子是观察方法，不是适合所有人的固定份量方案。

## 从小调整开始
如果午餐只有面条和肉，可以加一份蔬菜；如果饮食长期很单一，先增加一种可获得的食物。具体食量取决于年龄、活动量和健康情况。食物多样性不需要依赖昂贵保健品。
body.en:
## No food supplies everything
Different foods provide different nutrients. A healthy dietary pattern combines adequacy, balance, moderation and variety. Eating only one supposedly healthy food can leave nutritional gaps.

## Inspect one meal
Rice, tofu and vegetables include a staple, a protein source and vegetables. Rotate whole grains, pulses, fish, eggs, dairy and varied produce across meals. This is an observation exercise, not a universal portion prescription.

## Make one adjustment
Add vegetables to a noodle-and-meat lunch, or one accessible food to a repetitive diet. Needs vary with age, activity and health. Variety does not require expensive supplements.

sources.title: WHO · Healthy diet

imageAlt: Illustrated everyday meal with rice, tofu, vegetables and fruit; educational illustration

title.zh: 不咸的食物，也可能含有不少钠
title.en: Food need not taste salty to contain sodium

summary.zh: 酱料、零食和包装食品里的钠，怎样用标签比较？
summary.en: Learn to compare sodium in sauces, snacks and packaged foods.

body.zh:
## 盐和钠有什么关系？
食盐含有钠，但钠也存在于部分食品添加剂中。吃起来不明显咸，并不代表钠含量低。钠摄入过多会升高血压，增加心血管疾病风险。

## 看标签，要先统一比较单位
比较同类食品时，先确认标注的是每 100 克还是每份。假设某食品每 100 克含钠 600 毫克，吃 50 克就摄入 300 毫克钠。这个计算例子不对应特定产品。

## 给味道留一些其他选择
可以减少酱油、调味酱和汤料的用量，用香料、蒜或柠檬增加风味。WHO 对成人建议每天少于 2000 毫克钠，相当于少于 5 克盐；儿童建议需按能量需求向下调整，不能直接照搬成人上限。
body.en:
## Salt is not the only source
Salt contains sodium, but some food additives do too. Mild taste does not guarantee low sodium. Excess sodium raises blood pressure and cardiovascular risk.

## Compare the same units
Check whether labels use 100 grams or one serving. A hypothetical food containing 600 mg sodium per 100 g supplies 300 mg in a 50 g portion. This example is not a specific product.

## Add flavour differently
Use less salty sauce or stock and try herbs, garlic or lemon. WHO recommends adults consume under 2,000 mg sodium daily, equivalent to under 5 g salt. Children's limits require downward adjustment for energy needs.

sources.title: WHO · Sodium reduction

imageAlt: Illustrated soy sauce, salt and unbranded packaged food; educational illustration

title.zh: 每天 60 分钟活动，不一定是一整节训练
title.en: Sixty active minutes need not be one training session

summary.zh: 理解青少年活动建议，把运动放进通学、课间和课后。
summary.en: Understand youth activity recommendations and make room for movement throughout the day.

body.zh:
## 先弄清建议适用的年龄
WHO 建议 5 至 17 岁儿童青少年，一周内平均每天至少进行 60 分钟中高强度、以有氧为主的身体活动。轻松散步和中高强度活动并不完全等同。

## 活动可以分散安排
快走通学、体育课和课后球类活动，都可能贡献活动时间，取决于实际强度。可尝试在一天不同时间安排活动，不必把目标理解为一次连续训练。

## 还需要不同类型的活动
一周至少 3 天应包含较高强度有氧活动，以及增强肌肉和骨骼的活动，例如适龄的攀爬、跳跃。刚开始活动少也有价值，逐渐增加更容易坚持；有健康限制时让专业人员帮助调整。
body.en:
## Know the age group
WHO recommends ages 5–17 average at least 60 minutes daily of moderate-to-vigorous, mostly aerobic activity across the week. An easy stroll is not equivalent to higher-intensity activity.

## Spread movement across the day
Brisk walking to school, PE and after-school games can contribute, depending on intensity. Activity can be distributed rather than treated as one continuous training session.

## Include different types
At least three days weekly should include vigorous aerobic activity and muscle- and bone-strengthening activity, such as age-appropriate climbing and jumping. Start gradually; seek tailored advice for health limitations.

sources.title: WHO · Physical activity
CDC · Child Activity: An Overview

imageAlt: Illustrated basketball, skipping rope and shoes on a school sports court; educational illustration

title.zh: 出汗多少，不能单独判断运动强度
title.en: Sweat alone does not tell you exercise intensity

summary.zh: 观察呼吸和说话的变化，比只看有没有流汗更实用。
summary.en: Changes in breathing and speech are more useful than sweat alone.

body.zh:
## 看身体有多用力
判断活动强度可以观察心跳和呼吸的变化。CDC 为儿童青少年提供的 0 至 10 主观用力尺度中，坐着不动接近 0，中等强度约为 5 至 6，高强度约为 7 至 8。出汗还受天气和个人差异影响，不能单独当作运动量指标。

## 试试说话测试
中等强度时，一般还能说话，但不容易唱歌；高强度时，往往说几个词就需要换气。同样是走路，速度、坡度和个人体能不同，强度也可能不同。

## 选择能持续参与的活动
从自己喜欢且能力适合的活动开始，逐步增加强度。课间走动能打断久坐，但不一定替代中高强度活动。不要为了达到某个数字忽视身体不适。
body.en:
## Notice effort
Heart rate and breathing help indicate intensity. CDC's youth effort scale runs from 0 at rest to 10 at maximum effort: moderate activity is around 5–6 and vigorous around 7–8. Weather and individual differences affect sweat, so it is not a standalone measure.

## Try the talk test
At moderate intensity, talking is possible but singing is difficult. Vigorous activity usually allows only a few words before a breath. Walking intensity varies with speed, slope and fitness.

## Choose sustainable activity
Start with enjoyable, suitable activities and build gradually. Walking breaks interrupt sitting but may not replace higher-intensity activity. Do not ignore discomfort to hit a number.

sources.title: CDC · Child Activity: An Overview
CDC · Measuring Physical Activity Intensity

title.zh: 感冒为什么通常不需要抗生素？
title.en: Why a cold usually does not need antibiotics

summary.zh: 抗生素针对某些细菌感染，不是所有发热和咳嗽的通用药。
summary.en: Antibiotics treat certain bacterial infections, not every fever or cough.

body.zh:
## 病毒和细菌不是一回事
普通感冒和流感由病毒引起，抗生素不能治疗病毒感染。发热、咳嗽，甚至黄绿色鼻涕，都不能单独证明需要抗生素。医生会结合病情判断是否存在需要治疗的细菌感染。

## 不需要时用药，也会有代价
不必要的抗生素不会让病毒感染好得更快，却仍可能带来腹泻、皮疹等不良反应，并推动耐药问题。不要因为想尽快返校就要求医生开抗生素。

## 已经拿到处方怎么办？
按医生或药师说明服用，不自行改变疗程，不与别人分享，也不把剩药留给下一次类似症状。出现不良反应或病情变化时联系专业人员，重新评估比自行加药更可靠。
body.en:
## Viruses differ from bacteria
Colds and flu are viral; antibiotics do not treat them. Fever, cough or yellow-green mucus alone does not establish a need for antibiotics. A clinician assesses whether a bacterial infection needs treatment.

## Unnecessary treatment has costs
Unneeded antibiotics do not speed recovery from viruses but can cause adverse effects such as diarrhoea or rash and contribute to resistance. Do not request them just to return to school sooner.

## Follow the prescription
Follow the clinician's or pharmacist's instructions. Do not change the course, share medicines or save leftovers for similar symptoms. Contact a professional about adverse effects or changes in illness.

sources.title: CDC · Healthy Habits: Antibiotic Do's and Don'ts

imageAlt: Illustrated tissues and thermometer with a closed generic tablet pack; educational illustration

title.zh: 耐药的是病原体，不是你的身体
title.en: Resistance belongs to microbes, not your body

summary.zh: 理解耐药如何影响治疗，也理解为什么它是共同的公共卫生问题。
summary.en: Understand why resistance affects treatment and matters beyond one medicine user.

body.zh:
## 耐药到底指什么？
细菌、病毒、真菌或寄生虫发生变化，不再对相应抗微生物药物作出反应，就可能出现耐药。不是人的身体“习惯了药”。抗生素耐药属于其中针对细菌的一部分。

## 为什么影响不止一个人？
耐药病原体能够传播。即使一个人很少用药，也可能感染耐药病原体。感染会更难治疗，有时需要其他药物或更复杂的医疗照护。药物误用和过度使用会加速这个问题。

## 日常能做的事
合理用药和预防感染都重要：不自行购买或借用抗生素，按处方用药，落实手卫生和疫苗接种等适用措施。清洁用水、卫生设施和可获得的诊断服务也很关键，不能把责任全归于某个患者。
body.en:
## What changes?
Resistance occurs when bacteria, viruses, fungi or parasites no longer respond to the relevant antimicrobial medicines. It is not your body getting used to a drug. Antibiotic resistance concerns bacteria within this broader problem.

## Why does it affect others?
Resistant pathogens can spread, including to people who rarely take medicines. Infections become harder to treat and may need alternative drugs or more complex care. Misuse and overuse accelerate the problem.

## What helps?
Use medicines as prescribed, avoid borrowing antibiotics and prevent infections through appropriate hand hygiene and vaccination. Clean water, sanitation and access to diagnosis matter too; responsibility does not rest on individual patients alone.

sources.title: WHO · Antimicrobial resistance

title.zh: 转发健康消息前，先问三个问题
title.en: Three questions before sharing a health claim

summary.zh: 谁写的、依据是什么、何时更新：让来源比转发量更重要。
summary.en: Who wrote it, what supports it, and when was it reviewed? Trace evidence before popularity.

body.zh:
## 谁在提供信息？
找到作者、负责机构及其联系方式。查看内容是为了教育公众，还是推销某种产品。穿白大褂的照片和专业排版，不能替代可核查的身份与依据。

## 证据在哪里？
点开原始链接，确认它是否真的支持消息中的说法。个人体验、销量和转发量不能证明疗效。“所有人适用”“保证治愈”等绝对承诺，值得进一步核查。

## 日期新，就一定正确吗？
发布日期和审核日期有助于判断内容是否过时，但新日期本身不是可靠证据。转发前，记录作者、依据和日期；如果建议涉及你自己的诊断或用药，把原文带给医务人员讨论其适用性。
body.en:
## Who is providing the information?
Find the author, responsible organization and contact details. Is the purpose education or selling a product? A white-coat photograph and polished layout are not verifiable credentials or evidence.

## Where is the evidence?
Open the original link and check whether it supports the claim. Personal stories, sales and shares do not establish effectiveness. Absolute promises such as guaranteed cures deserve scrutiny.

## Is recent always reliable?
Publication and review dates help identify outdated advice, but a new date alone proves nothing. Note the author, evidence and date before sharing. Discuss personal diagnostic or medication advice with a clinician using the original source.

sources.title: MedlinePlus · Evaluating Health Information

imageAlt: Illustrated smartphone, blank notebook and pen before sharing information; educational illustration

title.zh: “研究发现”之后，还需要知道什么？
title.en: What should come after 'a study found'?

summary.zh: 看研究对象、规模与设计，避免把一个标题当成生活指南。
summary.en: Check participants, size and design before turning a headline into advice.

body.zh:
## 先问研究了谁
细胞、动物和人的研究，不具有相同的直接适用性。即使研究对象是人，也要看年龄、健康状况等是否与你相近。动物实验的结果不能直接变成个人用药建议。

## 研究是怎样做的？
样本有多大、持续多久、有没有比较组，会影响结论的解释。小样本结果往往需要更多研究验证。随机对照试验有助于评估治疗效果和安全性，但仍要结合研究质量与其他证据。

## 不只读一句结论
一项研究可能只回答一个特定问题。不同研究的对象与方法不同，结果也可能不同。看到“颠覆常识”的标题时，先寻找原文和可靠机构的解释，不凭一篇新闻改变治疗方案。
body.en:
## Who was studied?
Cell, animal and human studies have different implications. In human research, check whether participants' ages and health resemble yours. Animal findings cannot directly become personal medication advice.

## How was the study conducted?
Sample size, duration and comparison groups affect interpretation. Small studies often need confirmation. Randomized trials help assess treatment effectiveness and safety, but quality and other evidence still matter.

## Read beyond one conclusion
One study answers a particular question. Different populations and methods can produce different results. For a supposedly revolutionary headline, seek the original research and reliable explanations rather than changing treatment based on a news story.

sources.title: MedlinePlus · Understanding Medical Research

imageAlt: Illustrated research papers with a magnifying glass and pencil; educational illustration

title.zh: 咳嗽两周还没好，为什么应该排查结核病？
title.en: Why a cough lasting two weeks deserves a TB assessment

summary.zh: 认识需要就医的线索，并在看诊前整理好症状、接触史和既往用药。
summary.en: Recognize signs that need assessment and prepare your symptoms, exposure history and medicines before a visit.

body.zh:
## 两周是就医提醒，不是自我诊断标准
中国疾控的科普提醒：咳嗽、咳痰持续两周及以上，或出现咯血、痰中带血，应及时到结核病定点医疗机构检查。它们也可能由其他疾病引起，不能凭症状认定自己得了结核病。

## 不只注意咳嗽
低热、夜间出汗、乏力、食欲下降和不明原因的体重减轻，也值得告诉医生。不要把“两周”理解成必须等满两周才能就医；症状明显、加重或出现咯血时应及时寻求医疗帮助。

## 就诊前准备一份小记录
记下症状开始时间、是否接触过结核病患者、既往结核病史，以及已经用过的药。医生会综合病史、影像和必要的病原学检查作判断；不应靠反复自行吃“消炎药”拖延评估。
body.en:
## A prompt for assessment, not self-diagnosis
China CDC advises assessment for cough or sputum lasting at least two weeks, or blood in sputum. Seek a designated TB service. Other illnesses can cause these symptoms too.

## Look beyond the cough
Report fever, night sweats, fatigue, appetite loss and unexplained weight loss. Two weeks is not a required waiting period: worsening symptoms or coughing blood warrant prompt medical help.

## Prepare for the visit
Record when symptoms began, TB contacts, previous TB and medicines taken. Clinicians combine history, imaging and appropriate tests. Repeated self-medication should not delay assessment.

sources.title: 中国疾控中心 · 肺结核防治核心知识
CDC · Signs and Symptoms of Tuberculosis

credit: CDC / Charles Farmer · PHIL #2466 · Public domain
imageAlt: CDC historical photograph of a physician and nurse examining a chest X-ray; not a YSPH activity

title.zh: 打过卡介苗，为什么仍要关注结核病？
title.en: Why TB still matters after a BCG vaccination

summary.zh: 卡介苗能提供重要保护，但接种史不等于终身不会感染或发病。
summary.en: BCG offers important protection, but vaccination does not guarantee lifelong protection from infection or disease.

body.zh:
## 保护有重点，也有边界
卡介苗（BCG）对预防儿童严重结核病，如结核性脑膜炎，具有重要作用。但它不能保证每个人都不感染结核菌或不发病，保护也可能随时间减弱。接种过仍需留意症状与接触史。

## 为什么检查前要说清接种史？
卡介苗可能影响结核皮肤试验结果，造成假阳性；结核血液检测（IGRA）不受卡介苗影响。检查结果应交由医务人员结合实际情况解读，不能把所有阳性都简单归因于疫苗。

## 接种过，也要配合筛查
接到学校或卫生部门的接触者筛查通知时，不要以“小时候打过针”为由忽略检查。是否需要某种检测或其他处理，应由当地医务人员决定；不要自行补种来替代暴露后的医学评估。
body.en:
## Protection has limits
BCG helps protect children against severe TB, including TB meningitis. It does not guarantee protection from infection or disease, and protection may weaken over time. Symptoms and exposure still matter.

## Tell the clinician about vaccination
BCG can cause a false-positive TB skin test; IGRA blood tests are unaffected. A clinician should interpret results in context rather than attributing every positive result to vaccination.

## Screening can still be necessary
Follow school or health-authority contact-screening advice even if vaccinated. Local clinicians determine suitable tests and care. Do not use self-directed revaccination as a substitute for assessment after exposure.

sources.title: CDC · Tuberculosis Vaccine

credit: CDC / Dr. Carolyn Sein · PHIL #17985 · Public domain

title.zh: 同学确诊结核病后，接到筛查通知怎么办？
title.en: A classmate has TB: what does a screening notice mean?

summary.zh: 被列为接触者不代表已经感染；配合评估、保护隐私，比猜测更有帮助。
summary.en: Being named as a contact does not mean you are infected. Assessment and privacy matter more than speculation.

body.zh:
## 接触、感染、发病是不同的事
与有传染性的肺部或喉部结核病患者共同停留，可能构成暴露，但不等于一定感染，更不等于已经发病。疾控人员会根据接触的场所、时间等信息判断谁需要检查。

## 没有不舒服，也可能需要检查
潜伏结核感染通常没有症状，因此“我感觉很好”不能替代筛查。按通知接受评估，并如实说明同住、同班等接触情况。具体检查及后续随访由当地医务人员安排；若出现症状，应主动说明，不必等下一次通知。

## 让支持代替标签
不要在群聊转发患者姓名、病历或猜测名单。配合必要的公共卫生调查，同时尊重个人隐私。可以帮助同学联系校医、整理学习资料，让科学防护与同伴支持同时发生。
body.en:
## Exposure is not infection or disease
Sharing air with someone who has infectious lung or throat TB may constitute exposure. It does not establish infection or illness. Health workers assess who needs testing using the setting and duration of contact.

## Feeling well does not replace screening
Latent infection usually causes no symptoms. Follow screening and follow-up instructions, report household or classroom contact accurately, and mention new symptoms promptly. Local clinicians determine tests and timing.

## Support without labelling
Do not circulate names, medical records or speculative lists in group chats. Cooperate with necessary health investigations while respecting privacy. Help classmates reach the school health service and keep up with learning.

sources.title: CDC · Exposure to Tuberculosis
中国疾控中心结核病控制中心 · 学校结核病防控科普

imageAlt: CDC health worker explaining TB chest X-ray screening results in Micronesia in 2024; not a YSPH activity

title.zh: 结核病治疗：感觉好了，为什么还不能自行停药？
title.en: TB treatment: why feeling better is not a reason to stop

summary.zh: 理解联合用药、定期复查和治疗支持，让完成疗程更有把握。
summary.en: Understand combination treatment, follow-up and support for completing a prescribed course.

body.zh:
## 症状缓解，不代表结核菌已经清除
治疗后可能先感觉好转，但体内仍可能有存活的结核菌。过早停药或不按方案服药，会增加再次生病和耐药的风险。是否结束疗程，需要医务人员评估，不能只看是否还咳嗽。

## 为什么常常需要多种药？
联合用药有助于清除结核菌并减少耐药风险。具体药物、剂量和疗程取决于病情及检查结果，不应套用别人的处方。定期复诊和必要的痰液、血液等检查，可帮助评估疗效与药物安全性。

## 遇到困难，要尽早求助
漏服、出现不适或难以按时复诊时，联系医生或药师，不自行补双倍剂量或改药。可使用提醒、服药记录和亲友支持；医护人员也可能安排面对面或视频服药支持。治疗是需要协作的过程，不是个人意志的考试。
body.en:
## Improvement is not proof that treatment is complete
You may feel better while TB bacteria remain alive. Stopping early or taking medicines incorrectly can lead to illness returning and resistance. A clinician determines when treatment is complete.

## Why several medicines?
Combination treatment helps kill bacteria and prevent resistance. Medicines, doses and duration depend on the individual assessment. Follow-up tests help monitor effectiveness and safety; another person's prescription is not a template.

## Ask for support early
Report missed doses, adverse effects or appointment difficulties. Do not double doses or change medicines yourself. Reminders, treatment records, family support and supervised or video-supported treatment can help.

sources.title: CDC · Treating Active Tuberculosis Disease
中国疾控中心结核病预防控制中心 · 关于结核病，我们都了解多少？

credit: CDC / Dr. George Kubica · PHIL #16464 · Public domain

title.zh: 结核病不只在肺部：认识肺外结核
title.en: TB is not only a lung disease: understanding extrapulmonary TB

summary.zh: 淋巴结、脊柱和其他部位也可能受影响；症状与传染性需要分别判断。
summary.en: TB can affect lymph nodes, the spine and other sites. Symptoms and infectiousness require separate assessment.

body.zh:
## 为什么名字里没有“肺”也可能是结核病？
结核菌最常影响肺部，但也可能影响淋巴结、肾脏、脊柱或脑膜等部位，称为肺外结核。同一个人也可能同时有肺部和肺外病变，因此没有咳嗽不能排除所有类型的结核病。

## 症状与受累部位有关
淋巴结结核可能出现肿块，脊柱结核可能表现为背痛。它们也有许多其他原因，不能看到一个症状就对号入座。持续或不明原因的症状需要专业评估；医生根据受累部位决定需要哪些影像或样本检查。

## 肺外结核都能传染吗？
多数肺外结核通常不具有传染性，但合并肺部或喉部结核等情况可能不同。是否需要防护、接触者筛查或暂缓返校，应由医务人员结合具体病情判断。不能仅凭“结核”两个字给他人贴上危险标签。
body.en:
## TB can occur outside the lungs
TB most often affects the lungs, but can involve lymph nodes, kidneys, the spine or the tissues around the brain. Lung and other disease can occur together. Absence of cough does not exclude every form of TB.

## Symptoms depend on the site
A lump or back pain may occur, but has many other possible causes. Persistent unexplained symptoms need professional assessment, not self-diagnosis. Tests depend on the site involved.

## Is it always contagious?
Most extrapulmonary TB is usually not infectious, but accompanying lung or throat disease can change that. Clinicians assess precautions, contact screening and return to school individually.

sources.title: CDC · About Active Tuberculosis Disease
CDC · Tuberculosis: Causes and How It Spreads

credit: CDC / Janice Haney Carr / Ray Butler · PHIL #8438 · Public domain
imageAlt: Scanning electron micrograph of Mycobacterium tuberculosis, CDC, 2006; a laboratory image, not a patient's scan

title.zh: 给睡眠留出八到十小时
title.en: Make room for sleep

summary.zh: 睡够多久、怎样睡好，以及什么时候需要专业评估。
summary.en: How much sleep teenagers need, what quality means and when to seek help.

body.zh:
## 先算清真正的睡眠时间
CDC 给 13 至 17 岁青少年的参考建议是每天睡 8 至 10 小时。躺在床上刷手机的时间不等于睡眠时间；制定作息时，也要为入睡留出余地。充足睡眠有助于注意力、记忆与情绪调节。

## 让作息比偶尔补觉更规律
尽量在相近时间入睡和起床，保持卧室安静、舒适。睡前至少半小时放下电子设备，下午和晚上避免摄入咖啡因。可以先从固定起床时间这一个小调整开始。

## 时间够了，却仍然困怎么办？
睡眠质量同样重要。经常难以入睡、夜间多次醒来，或睡够后仍明显困倦，应向医务人员咨询。记录一周的入睡、起床和白天困倦情况，比只说“最近睡不好”更有助于沟通。
body.en:
## Count sleep, not time in bed
CDC recommends 8–10 hours daily for ages 13–17. Scrolling in bed is not sleep; allow time to fall asleep. Adequate sleep supports attention, memory and emotional well-being.

## Make the routine consistent
Keep similar sleep and wake times and a quiet, comfortable bedroom. Switch off devices at least half an hour before bed and avoid afternoon or evening caffeine. Start with one manageable change, such as a consistent wake time.

## Quality matters too
Regular difficulty falling asleep, repeated waking or tiredness despite enough sleep deserves professional advice. A sleep diary can make that conversation more useful.

sources.title: CDC · About Sleep

imageAlt: A red mechanical alarm clock against a white background, photographed by Wilfredor; an illustrative sleep-schedule object photo, not a YSPH event.

title.zh: 压力大时，先照顾日常生活
title.en: When stress builds, start with the everyday

summary.zh: 识别压力的身体信号，把求助视为一种可行的行动。
summary.en: Notice stress in the body and treat asking for help as a practical step.

body.zh:
## 压力不只是一种想法
面对考试或冲突时，感到紧张是常见反应。压力也可能表现为难以集中注意力、烦躁、头痛、胃部不适或睡眠变化。不同人的表现不同，不能只凭“看起来很平静”判断对方是否需要支持。

## 给生活保留几个稳定的支点
安排规律的吃饭、睡眠和活动时间，和信任的人保持联系。如果不断刷消息让自己更焦虑，可以主动减少这部分时间。散步、休息和交流可以成为日常支持，不需要等一切任务完成才允许自己休息。

## 何时不宜只靠自己扛？
如果压力持续存在，已经影响学习、睡眠或日常生活，向信任的家人、学校心理老师或医务人员求助。自助方法不能替代必要的专业评估；需要帮助不代表不够努力。
body.en:
## Stress can show up physically
Exams or conflict can bring tension, irritability, difficulty concentrating, headaches, stomach discomfort or sleep changes. People respond differently; appearing calm does not establish that someone is coping well.

## Keep a few steady routines
Protect regular meals, sleep, activity and contact with trusted people. Reduce news or social-media exposure if it increases stress. Walking, breaks and conversation can support everyday coping.

## Know when to ask for help
Persistent stress affecting school, sleep or daily functioning deserves support from a trusted adult, school counsellor or health professional. Self-help does not replace appropriate assessment.

sources.title: WHO · Stress

credit: Debora Cartagena / CDC PHIL · Public domain
imageAlt: CDC colleagues taking part in the April 2010 Earth Walk at the Century Center campus; archival photo, not a YSPH event.

title.zh: 护牙，先从每天两次刷牙开始
title.en: Healthy teeth start with a daily routine

summary.zh: 了解糖、牙菌斑与含氟牙膏之间的关系。
summary.en: Understand the connection between sugars, plaque and fluoride toothpaste.

body.zh:
## 蛀牙并不是突然出现的洞
牙菌斑中的细菌可把食物和饮料中的游离糖转化为酸，逐渐损伤牙齿。含糖饮料、蜂蜜和果汁中的糖也在其中；“天然”不意味着对牙齿没有影响。

## 刷牙和减少糖摄入，各有作用
WHO 建议鼓励每天两次使用含氟牙膏刷牙。刷牙帮助清除牙菌斑，适当的氟暴露有助于预防龋齿。选择水作为主要饮品、减少游离糖，是另一项重要措施，不能仅靠刷牙抵消高糖饮食。

## 不要把不适一直拖下去
牙痛、牙龈出血或肿胀值得向牙科专业人员咨询。多数口腔问题在早期更容易处理；具体清洁方式、牙膏选择和复查安排，可根据年龄与个人情况询问牙医。
body.en:
## Decay develops over time
Plaque bacteria turn free sugars into acids that damage teeth. Sugar in honey and fruit juice counts too; natural does not mean harmless to teeth.

## Brushing and diet work together
WHO encourages twice-daily brushing with fluoride toothpaste. Brushing removes plaque, while adequate fluoride exposure helps prevent decay. Make water the main drink and reduce free sugars; brushing does not cancel a high-sugar diet.

## Act on symptoms
Toothache, bleeding or swollen gums deserve dental advice. Many oral problems are easier to treat early. Ask a dentist about age-appropriate products, cleaning and check-ups.

title.zh: 看屏幕久了，给眼睛一次休息
title.en: Give your eyes a screen break

summary.zh: 把远眺、保护眼睛和必要检查放进日常习惯。
summary.en: Build distance breaks, eye protection and appropriate examinations into daily life.

body.zh:
## 远眺是一种休息，不是治疗
长时间看电脑可能让眼睛疲劳。美国国家眼科研究所建议一种简单做法：每看屏幕约 20 分钟，看看约 20 英尺（约 6 米）外的东西，持续约 20 秒。它是休息提醒，不是治愈近视或其他眼病的方法。

## 保护视力，也要注意屏幕之外
从事可能伤眼的运动或操作时，使用合适的护目装备；户外选择能阻挡 UVA 与 UVB 的太阳镜。佩戴隐形眼镜的人，应先洗手，再按要求清洁、更换镜片。

## 看得清，不代表不需要评估
一些眼病早期没有明显症状。是否需要眼科检查，应结合年龄、症状和风险因素咨询专业人员；持续不适不要只依赖休息或网上的“护眼偏方”。
body.en:
## A break is not a treatment
Long computer sessions can tire the eyes. The National Eye Institute suggests looking about 20 feet away for about 20 seconds every 20 minutes. This is a rest reminder, not a cure for myopia or other eye disease.

## Protect eyes beyond screens
Use appropriate protective eyewear for risky activities and sunglasses that block UVA and UVB. Wash hands before handling contact lenses and follow cleaning and replacement instructions.

## Clear vision is not the whole picture
Some eye diseases begin without symptoms. Ask a professional about examinations suited to your age, symptoms and risks. Persistent discomfort deserves assessment.

sources.title: National Eye Institute · Keep Your Eyes Healthy

credit: Amanda Mills / CDC PHIL · Public domain
imageAlt: A physician examining a seated patient's right eye with a handheld ophthalmoscope in a 2011 CDC archive photograph; not a YSPH clinic.

title.zh: 保护听力，不只看音量大小
title.en: Listening safely is about volume and time

summary.zh: 声音有多响、听了多久，共同决定噪声暴露。
summary.en: Loudness and listening duration both contribute to sound exposure.

body.zh:
## 声音越响，安全暴露时间越短
强噪声或长时间噪声暴露可能造成永久性听力损伤。耳机上的音量百分比不是统一的分贝刻度：设备、耳机和环境不同，同一百分比也可能意味着不同声强。

## 不要靠加大音量对抗环境噪声
在嘈杂环境中，优先离开声源、缩短停留时间，或使用合适的听力保护。听音乐时降低音量并安排安静的休息；设备的声暴露提醒也可以提供参考。

## 留意听力的变化
耳鸣、听不清高频声音，或越来越需要别人重复说话，值得进行听力评估。不要因为暂时没有疼痛，就认为长时间大音量一定安全。
body.en:
## Louder sound leaves less safe listening time
Intense or prolonged noise can permanently damage hearing. Volume percentages are not standardized decibel readings: devices, headphones and surroundings differ.

## Do not compete with background noise
Move away from loud sources, limit exposure and use suitable hearing protection. Lower listening volume, take quiet breaks and pay attention to sound-exposure alerts where available.

## Notice changes
Ringing ears, difficulty hearing high-pitched sounds or repeatedly asking people to repeat themselves deserve a hearing assessment. Lack of pain does not make prolonged loud listening safe.

sources.title: WHO · Deafness and hearing loss: Safe listening

imageAlt: A pair of wired Koss Porta Pro headphones in an independent Wikimedia Commons photograph; an illustrative object photo, not a YSPH endorsement.

title.zh: 厨房里，生熟分开为什么重要？
title.en: Why raw and cooked food need separate paths

summary.zh: 认识交叉污染，把食品安全变成几个可重复的小动作。
summary.en: Understand cross-contamination and make food safety a repeatable routine.

body.zh:
## 煮熟之后，还可能再次被污染
生食材上的微生物可能通过手、刀具、砧板或容器，转移到已经煮熟或可直接食用的食品上。这种交叉污染不一定会改变食物的外观，不能仅凭“看起来干净”判断。

## 给生熟食物分开安排工具
处理生肉、禽类和海鲜的工具，与直接入口食品的工具分开使用；操作之间清洁双手和工作表面。盛过生肉的盘子，不应未经清洗就重新盛放熟食。

## 记住五个环节
WHO 的食品安全五要点包括保持清洁、生熟分开、彻底做熟、保持安全温度，以及使用安全的水和原料。分开工具只是其中一步，不能替代其他环节。
body.en:
## Cooked food can be contaminated again
Microbes from raw ingredients can move through hands, knives, boards or containers onto cooked or ready-to-eat food. Appearance alone does not reveal this cross-contamination.

## Separate tools and tasks
Use separate equipment for raw meat, poultry or seafood and ready-to-eat food. Clean hands and surfaces between tasks. Do not return cooked food to an unwashed plate that held raw meat.

## Think in five steps
WHO's five keys are cleanliness, separating raw and cooked food, thorough cooking, safe temperatures, and safe water and ingredients. Separation supports, rather than replaces, the other steps.

sources.title: WHO · Five keys to safer food manual

credit: Lauren Bishop / CDC PHIL · Public domain

title.zh: 疫苗为什么要在生病之前接种？
title.en: Why vaccination comes before illness

summary.zh: 理解免疫记忆、接种记录和补种咨询的意义。
summary.en: Understand immune memory, vaccination records and catch-up advice.

body.zh:
## 让免疫系统提前认识目标
疫苗帮助免疫系统识别特定病原体的抗原并形成保护。它们可以使用病原体的一部分、经过处理的病原体，或让细胞产生抗原的遗传指令；不同疫苗的原理并不完全相同。

## 保护并不是按下按钮立即出现
建立保护需要时间，一些疫苗需要多剂次或加强接种。等到疫情发生、即将暴露时才考虑接种，可能来不及获得预期保护。是否接种、何时接种，应参考当地接种建议与个人情况。

## 先找接种记录，再咨询补种
保存纸质或电子接种记录，记录已经完成的剂次。发现遗漏时向接种门诊咨询补种安排，不凭记忆随意重打，也不要把某种疫苗的安排套用到所有疫苗。
body.en:
## Let immunity recognize the target early
Vaccines train immunity to recognize particular antigens. They may use parts of a pathogen, modified pathogens or genetic instructions for making an antigen; technologies differ.

## Protection takes time
Some vaccines need multiple doses or boosters. Waiting until an outbreak or imminent exposure may not leave enough time for protection. Follow local recommendations and individual clinical advice.

## Keep the record
Retain paper or electronic vaccination records. Ask a vaccination service about missed doses rather than repeating doses from memory or assuming every vaccine follows the same schedule.

sources.title: WHO · Vaccines and immunization: What is vaccination?

credit: Becky Rentz / CDC PHIL · Public domain
imageAlt: Anne Schuchat receiving an influenza vaccination from a healthcare worker at CDC's 2014 Flu Immunization Open House; archival photograph, not a YSPH event.

title.zh: 防蚊，也要留意白天和积水
title.en: Mosquito prevention starts with standing water

summary.zh: 从伊蚊的活动特点出发，组合环境清理与个人防护。
summary.en: Combine source reduction and personal protection with an understanding of Aedes mosquitoes.

body.zh:
## 不是所有蚊子都只在夜里活动
传播登革热的伊蚊主要在白天活动。因此，只在夜间使用蚊帐，不能覆盖所有暴露情境；风险还与当地蚊媒和疾病流行情况有关。

## 先检查身边的小容器
花盆托盘、闲置桶和其他能蓄水的容器，都值得定期检查、清空和清洁。储水容器加盖，有助于减少蚊虫孳生。清理环境需要家庭、学校与社区共同参与。

## 把个人防护也加进来
穿着能覆盖皮肤的衣物、使用纱窗，并按产品说明选择和使用驱蚊剂。外出或旅行前留意当地卫生提醒，不因为“只叮了一口”就忽视暴露后的持续不适。
body.en:
## Daytime matters too
Aedes mosquitoes that transmit dengue are mainly active during the day. Night-time bed nets alone do not cover every exposure; local mosquito and disease patterns matter.

## Check small water-holding containers
Inspect plant saucers, unused buckets and similar containers. Empty and clean them regularly and cover stored water. Families, schools and communities all contribute to source reduction.

## Add personal protection
Use covering clothing, window screens and repellents according to their instructions. Check local health advice before travel and seek advice for persistent illness following exposure.

title.zh: 热天活动，别把降温只理解为喝水
title.en: In hot weather, water is only part of the plan

summary.zh: 把时间、环境、休息和补水一起纳入高温防护。
summary.en: Plan activity timing, cooling, rest and hydration together.

body.zh:
## 热会影响身体散热
高温下，身体需要更努力地维持体温。户外活动、密闭炎热空间以及一些健康状况，都可能增加风险。不是只有运动员或户外工作者才需要防暑。

## 先调整安排，再准备补水
留意天气和高温提醒，尽量把活动安排在较凉爽时段，增加阴凉处或凉爽室内的休息。随身带水、规律补水，同时降低不必要的高强度暴露；喝水不能抵消所有热风险。

## 不舒服时，不要硬撑
头晕、头痛、乏力、恶心或异常大量出汗，都可能提示过热。停止活动，转移到凉爽环境，并根据情况及时寻求医疗帮助。需要限制饮水或服用特定药物的人，应提前咨询个人防暑安排。
body.en:
## Heat challenges temperature control
High temperatures make the body work harder to stay cool. Outdoor exertion, hot indoor spaces and some health conditions increase risk. Heat protection is not only for athletes or outdoor workers.

## Adjust plans as well as fluids
Follow heat alerts, use cooler activity times and take breaks in shade or a cool room. Carry water and hydrate regularly, while reducing unnecessary strenuous exposure. Drinking water does not remove every heat risk.

## Do not push through symptoms
Dizziness, headache, weakness, nausea or unusually heavy sweating can signal overheating. Stop, cool down and seek appropriate care. Ask about tailored plans if medicines or fluid restrictions affect you.

sources.title: WHO · Heat and health
CDC · About Heat and Your Health

title.zh: 电子烟的气溶胶，不是普通水蒸气
title.en: Vape aerosol is not just water vapour

summary.zh: 别让口味、包装或“无烟”的说法代替风险判断。
summary.en: Flavours, packaging and smoke-free claims are not a measure of safety.

body.zh:
## 先分清水蒸气与气溶胶
电子烟通过加热液体产生供吸入的气溶胶，不能把它简单看成水蒸气。WHO 明确指出电子烟有害健康，并不安全。产品的甜味或较淡的气味，不能证明吸入物无害。

## “换一种产品”不等于没有风险
传统卷烟、加热烟草与电子烟的工作方式不同，但不能仅凭“没有燃烧”或“无烟”就判定安全。含尼古丁产品还涉及成瘾风险，尤其不应把面向青少年的宣传当成健康建议。

## 给拒绝留下简单的表达
不使用的人没有必要为了尝试而开始。可以直接说“我不吸”，并选择远离烟雾或气溶胶的环境。已经使用且想停止时，向医务人员寻求适合自己的戒用支持，不依赖广告推荐的替代品。
body.en:
## Aerosol is not ordinary steam
E-cigarettes heat liquid to create an inhaled aerosol. WHO states that e-cigarettes are harmful and unsafe. Sweet flavours or a mild smell do not establish harmlessness.

## Different does not mean risk-free
Cigarettes, heated tobacco and e-cigarettes work differently, but no combustion or smoke-free claims do not prove safety. Nicotine products also carry addiction risks; youth-oriented promotion is not health advice.

## Keep refusal simple
Non-users need not start to experiment. A direct refusal and avoiding smoke or aerosol are practical choices. People wanting to stop can ask health professionals for suitable support rather than relying on advertising.

title.zh: 突然发烧、浑身酸痛，是流感吗？
title.en: Fever and body aches: could it be flu?

summary.zh: 症状能提供线索，却不能单独确定是哪一种病毒。
summary.en: Symptoms offer clues, but do not identify the virus on their own.

body.zh:
## 症状有重叠
流感由流感病毒引起，常见表现包括突然发热、咳嗽、肌肉酸痛和明显乏力。其他呼吸道感染也可能有相似表现，单凭发烧高低无法确诊。医生会结合症状和必要的检测判断。

## 生病后，先减少接触
症状较轻时，在家休息、补充水分，避免把感染带到教室。咳嗽时用纸巾遮住口鼻，及时洗手。症状加重，或本身有慢性病等重症风险时，应就医。流感疫苗是重要的预防手段；具体接种安排向当地接种门诊咨询。
body.en:
## Symptoms overlap
Influenza viruses can cause sudden fever, cough, muscle aches and pronounced tiredness. Other respiratory infections can look similar. The height of a fever cannot confirm flu; clinicians use the clinical picture and testing where needed.

## Stay home while ill
For mild illness, rest, drink fluids and avoid bringing the infection into class. Cover coughs with a tissue and wash your hands. Seek care if symptoms worsen or you have a condition that increases the risk of severe illness. Vaccination helps prevent flu; ask your local vaccination clinic about arrangements.

sources.title: WHO · Influenza (seasonal), 28 February 2025

credit: James Gathany / CDC PHIL #11162 · Public domain
imageAlt: A man sneezing with visible expelled droplets in a 2009 CDC photograph; illustrates respiratory spread, not a confirmed influenza case or YSPH activity.

title.zh: 空气污染为什么也会伤到心脏？
title.en: Air pollution affects the heart, too

summary.zh: 从呼吸道以外的影响，理解清洁空气的公共卫生意义。
summary.en: The health effects extend beyond the lungs.

body.zh:
## 影响不止咳嗽
室外空气污染会增加呼吸系统和心血管疾病风险。WHO将细颗粒物暴露与心脏病、卒中及肺部疾病联系起来。没有咳嗽，并不能说明污染对健康没有影响。

## 清洁空气需要共同治理
交通、工业和燃料燃烧都是治理对象。更清洁的交通与能源、合理的城市规划，可以减少污染来源。个人很难控制这些排放；讨论空气质量时，也需要关注学校周边道路、社区能源和公共交通，而不能把责任全留给每个呼吸空气的人。
body.en:
## The effects go beyond coughing
Outdoor air pollution increases respiratory and cardiovascular risks. WHO links fine-particle exposure with heart disease, stroke and lung disease. Not coughing does not establish that polluted air is harmless.

## Cleaner air needs shared action
Transport, industry and fuel combustion are targets for pollution control. Cleaner transport and energy, alongside urban planning, can reduce emissions. Most sources are outside an individual's control. Roads around schools, community energy supplies and public transport belong in the conversation about health, alongside personal precautions.

sources.title: WHO · Ambient (outdoor) air pollution, 24 October 2024

imageAlt: Industrial stacks releasing visible plumes beside the river in Quebec City, photographed by Wilfredor on 23 October 2023; illustrates industrial emissions, not a measurement of pollutant concentration or a local YSPH observation.

title.zh: 低钠盐，适合家里所有人吗？
title.en: Is lower-sodium salt suitable for everyone at home?

summary.zh: 含钾替代盐有适用范围，换盐前先了解家人的健康情况。
summary.en: Potassium-containing salt substitutes have limits on who should use them.

body.zh:
## 替代掉一部分钠，也增加了钾
一些低钠盐用钾替代一部分钠。WHO在2025年的指南中，有条件地建议选择使用食盐的成年人，考虑以含钾的低钠替代盐取代普通食盐。这个建议有明确的适用范围。

## 一家人共用盐罐之前
这项建议不适用于儿童和孕妇，也排除了肾功能受损或存在其他影响钾排泄情况的人。家里有人需要限制钾摄入时，不宜自行给全家换用含钾低钠盐，应先询问医务人员。换了盐也仍需控制用量，低钠不意味着可以任意多放。
body.en:
## Less sodium can mean more potassium
Some lower-sodium salts replace part of the sodium with potassium. WHO's 2025 guideline conditionally suggests that adults who choose to use table salt replace it with a potassium-containing lower-sodium substitute. The recommendation has a defined scope.

## Check before changing the shared salt jar
It does not apply to children or pregnant women, and excludes people with kidney impairment or other circumstances that compromise potassium excretion. If someone at home needs to limit potassium, seek professional advice before switching the household supply. A lower-sodium product still needs to be used in limited amounts.

sources.title: WHO · Use of lower-sodium salt substitutes, 27 January 2025
WHO · Salt substitutes guideline: recommendation and scope (2025)

credit: Amanda Mills / CDC PHIL #13547 · Public domain
imageAlt: An open glass salt shaker lying beside spilled table salt in a 2011 CDC photograph; ordinary salt, not a verified potassium-enriched salt substitute.

title.zh: 果汁里的糖，也算游离糖吗？
title.en: Does the sugar in juice count as free sugar?

summary.zh: 读懂游离糖的范围，避免把“不额外加糖”当成没有糖。
summary.en: No added sugar does not mean no free sugar.

body.zh:
## 果汁和完整水果，分类不同
WHO所说的游离糖，包括食品制作时加入的糖，以及蜂蜜、糖浆、果汁和浓缩果汁中的糖。完整水果中的糖不属于这一范围。因此，一杯没有额外加糖的果汁，仍含有游离糖。

## 建议看的是全天饮食
WHO建议成人和儿童把游离糖控制在全天总能量的10%以下，并有条件地建议进一步降到5%以下，以获得额外健康益处。这不是每杯饮料的含糖比例。日常可以用白水替换一部分甜饮料，不必把整个饮食问题简化成某一杯饮料的好坏。
body.en:
## Juice counts differently from whole fruit
WHO's definition of free sugars includes sugars added during preparation and those in honey, syrups, fruit juice and juice concentrates. Sugars within whole fruit are outside this definition. Juice can therefore contain free sugars without any being added.

## The recommendation covers the whole diet
WHO recommends keeping free sugars below 10% of daily energy intake for adults and children, with a conditional recommendation to go below 5% for additional benefits. These percentages describe daily energy, not the sugar concentration of one drink. Replacing some sweet drinks with water is one practical adjustment.

sources.title: WHO · Sugars intake for adults and children (2015)
WHO · Sugars guideline: recommendations and definitions (2015)

title.zh: 量血压时，手臂该放在哪里？
title.en: Where should your arm be during a blood pressure check?

summary.zh: 姿势和袖带大小，会影响测量结果。
summary.en: Position and cuff size can affect the reading.

body.zh:
## 先把姿势摆好
坐着测量时，让背部和双脚有支撑，双腿不要交叉。把手臂支撑在与心脏同高的位置，测量时不交谈。手臂悬空、双脚不着地或边量边说话，都可能影响读数。

## 袖带要合适，也要贴着皮肤
袖带尺寸过小可能使读数偏高，不要隔着衣服绑袖带。测量前先排空膀胱，并请医务人员确认袖带是否适合自己的臂围。复测时保持相同的规范姿势，有助于减少测量条件带来的差异。
body.en:
## Support your body and arm
For a seated check, support your back and feet and keep your legs uncrossed. Rest your arm at heart level and do not talk during measurement. An unsupported arm, dangling feet or conversation can affect the reading.

## Check the cuff
A cuff that is too small can produce a higher reading. Place it on bare skin, not over clothing. Empty your bladder beforehand and ask the person taking the measurement to check the fit. Using the same correct position for repeat measurements reduces variation caused by the setup.

sources.title: CDC / Million Hearts · 7 Simple Tips to Get an Accurate Blood Pressure Reading (2024)

credit: Yvonne Green / CDC PHIL #14867 (content provider: Nasheka Powell) · Public domain
imageAlt: Amy Valderrama measuring Shonia Zollicoffer's blood pressure with an upper-arm cuff and stethoscope at a 2012 CDC employee screening; archival photograph, not a YSPH clinic.

title.zh: 总觉得累，需要补铁吗？
title.en: Always tired: do you need iron?

summary.zh: 疲劳有多种原因，贫血也不全是缺铁。
summary.en: Fatigue has many causes, and not all anaemia is iron deficiency.

body.zh:
## 疲劳不能代替检查
血红蛋白帮助血液把氧送到身体各处。贫血时，可能出现乏力、头晕或活动后气短，但这些表现并不特异。判断贫血需要血液检查，并结合年龄等因素解释结果。

## 先查原因，再决定怎么补
缺铁是常见原因，感染、慢性疾病和遗传性红细胞疾病也可能导致贫血。月经过多的人应把出血情况告诉医生。日常保持食物多样，吃富含铁的食物；是否需要补充剂，由医务人员根据原因决定，不要仅凭“最近很累”开始长期补铁。
body.en:
## Tiredness is not a diagnosis
Haemoglobin helps carry oxygen around the body. Anaemia can cause fatigue, dizziness or breathlessness on exertion, but these symptoms are not specific. Diagnosis requires blood testing, interpreted with factors such as age.

## Find the cause before taking supplements
Iron deficiency is common, but infections, chronic disease and inherited red-cell disorders can also cause anaemia. Tell your clinician about heavy periods. Eat a varied diet with iron-rich foods, and use supplements when a qualified professional recommends them for your situation. Feeling tired alone is not a reason to start long-term iron treatment.

sources.title: WHO · Anaemia, 10 February 2025

credit: Amanda Mills / CDC PHIL #13492 · Public domain
imageAlt: Gloved hands collecting a venous blood sample from a patient's arm in a 2011 CDC photograph; illustrates blood sampling, not a confirmed anaemia diagnosis or YSPH clinic.

title.zh: 学校里，月经健康需要哪些支持？
title.en: What does menstrual support at school look like?

summary.zh: 用品、厕所和可以安心提问的环境，都会影响在校体验。
summary.en: Products, facilities and the freedom to ask questions all matter at school.

body.zh:
## 有用品，还需要能更换的地方
管理月经需要合适的用品，也需要清洁用水、能保护隐私的厕所和丢弃废弃用品的设施。选择用品时，应考虑个人舒适度，以及清洗、晾干或处理它们的条件。

## 让求助不用遮遮掩掩
WHO把月经健康放在身体、心理和社会健康的范围内。校园可以提供清楚的信息和必要的用品，让同学知道有问题时向谁求助。嘲笑、羞辱或把月经当成不能提的事，会妨碍人们获取支持。需要专业照护的人，也应能方便地获得服务。
body.en:
## Products need usable facilities
Managing a period takes suitable products, clean water, private toilets and a way to dispose of used materials. Product choices also depend on comfort and whether washing, drying or disposal is practical.

## Make asking for help ordinary
WHO describes menstrual health as physical, psychological and social health. Schools can provide clear information and supplies, and make it clear who students can approach with questions. Ridicule and silence get in the way of support. People who need professional care should be able to access it.

sources.title: WHO · Statement on menstrual health and rights, 22 June 2022
UNICEF / WHO · Menstrual health in schools, May 2024

imageAlt: A clean reusable cloth menstrual pad with patterned fabric, red wings and snap fasteners on a pale background, photographed by Sonjaaa in 2006; neutral product illustration, not an endorsement.

title.zh: 哮喘没发作的时候，还需要管理吗？
title.en: Does asthma need attention between attacks?

summary.zh: 了解气道、诱因和个人行动计划的作用。
summary.en: Understand the airways, triggers and the purpose of an action plan.

body.zh:
## 症状可以时轻时重
哮喘是一种影响肺部气道的慢性疾病。气道发炎、变窄时，呼吸会变得困难。花粉、冷空气、病毒感染或运动可能诱发症状，不同人的诱因并不相同。

## 和医生一起写清楚怎么应对
治疗和个人哮喘行动计划有助于控制病情。计划可包括症状监测、减少诱因接触和用药安排。按自己的方案管理，不要借用别人的吸入器或照搬别人的用药。反复出现呼吸不适，应就诊评估；医生可能安排肺功能检查，不能只凭一次咳嗽给自己诊断哮喘。
body.en:
## Symptoms can come and go
Asthma is a chronic condition affecting the lung's airways. When they become inflamed and narrow, breathing becomes harder. Pollen, cold air, viral infections or exercise can trigger symptoms, though triggers differ between people.

## Make a plan with your clinician
Treatment and a personal asthma action plan help manage the condition. A plan may cover symptom monitoring, triggers and medicines. Follow your own plan rather than borrowing an inhaler or copying someone else's prescription. Recurrent breathing problems need assessment. Clinicians may use lung-function tests; a cough alone does not establish asthma.

sources.title: NHLBI / NIH · What is asthma?, 17 April 2024
NHLBI / NIH · Asthma diagnosis, 17 April 2024

credit: Ben Dalton / Wikimedia Commons · CC BY 2.0
imageAlt: A blue metered-dose inhaler photographed by Ben Dalton on 30 July 2009; an illustrative object photograph, not a product endorsement or a treatment recommendation.

title.zh: 头盔戴上了，还要检查什么？
title.en: Helmet on: what else needs checking?

summary.zh: 合适、合规、正确佩戴，才能让头盔发挥保护作用。
summary.en: Fit, standards and correct fastening affect protection.

body.zh:
## 戴上以后，也要扣好
头盔能在碰撞时减少头部损伤风险，但需要适合使用者并正确佩戴。出发前检查尺寸、位置和扣带，按产品说明固定。购买时选择符合适用安全标准的产品，不能只凭外观判断保护能力。

## 头盔不会消除道路风险
WHO的头盔手册同时讨论安全标准、法律执行和公众教育。更安全的出行还需要合理车速和道路环境。头盔主要帮助减轻碰撞后的伤害，无法保证不发生碰撞；把佩戴检查放进出发前的习惯，也要遵守交通规则。
body.en:
## Fasten it properly
Helmets reduce the risk of head injury in a crash when they fit and are worn correctly. Before setting off, check the size, position and straps and follow the product instructions. Choose a product that meets the applicable safety standard; appearance cannot tell you how well it protects.

## Protection has limits
WHO's helmet manual also addresses standards, enforcement and public education. Safer travel depends on speed and the road environment as well. A helmet helps reduce injuries if a collision happens; it cannot guarantee that a collision will not happen. Check it before leaving and follow traffic rules.

sources.title: WHO · Helmets: a road safety manual, second edition (2023)

credit: Amanda Mills / CDC PHIL #14070 · Public domain

title.zh: 天不热，也需要防晒吗？
title.en: Can a cool day still call for sun protection?

summary.zh: 温度不是紫外线强弱的刻度，出门前可以看紫外线指数。
summary.en: Temperature does not measure UV exposure. Check the UV index.

body.zh:
## 紫外线看不见，也感觉不到
阴天仍可能有较强的紫外线，凉爽不等于暴露少。WHO建议紫外线指数达到3及以上时采取防护。指数越高，皮肤和眼睛受到损伤的风险越大。

## 先找遮阴，再考虑裸露部位
安排户外活动时，避开正午强烈日晒，利用树荫、衣物和宽檐帽遮挡。无法被衣物覆盖的皮肤可使用广谱防晒产品，眼睛也需要防紫外线的太阳镜。涂了防晒并不适合因此延长暴晒时间。春季出游时，也可以把查看紫外线指数列入准备事项。
body.en:
## You cannot feel ultraviolet radiation
UV levels can still be high under cloud cover. Cool weather does not establish low exposure. WHO recommends protection when the UV index reaches 3 or above. A higher index means greater potential for damage to skin and eyes.

## Plan for shade and cover
Limit midday sun and use shade, clothing and a broad-brimmed hat. Use broad-spectrum sunscreen on exposed skin and sunglasses with UV protection. Sunscreen is not a reason to spend longer in strong sun. Checking the UV index can be part of preparing for a spring outing, too.

sources.title: WHO · Ultraviolet radiation, 21 June 2022

credit: Amanda Mills / CDC PHIL #14062 · Public domain
imageAlt: An adult applying sunscreen to a child's cheek at a playground in a 2011 CDC photograph; archival illustration, not a YSPH activity or brand endorsement.

title.zh: 一出门就打喷嚏，是花粉过敏吗？
title.en: Sneezing outdoors: could pollen be the cause?

summary.zh: 留意鼻痒、眼痒和接触环境，别只凭喷嚏判断。
summary.en: Itchy eyes, an itchy nose and exposure patterns can offer clues.

body.zh:
## 把环境和症状一起记下来
花粉过敏可能引起连续打喷嚏、鼻塞、流鼻涕，以及眼睛发痒、流泪。症状可以持续数周，但这些表现也会与其他疾病重叠。记录外出时间、接触环境和不适变化，有助于向医生说明情况。

## 减少把花粉带回家
花粉较多时，外出可用合适的口罩和包覆式眼镜减少接触；回家后换衣、洗澡。症状影响上课或睡眠时，可咨询医生或药师。部分抗组胺药会让人困倦，选药时应说明自己的日常安排。当地花粉情况要看当地信息，不能仅凭天气暖和就判断。
body.en:
## Notice where symptoms happen
Pollen allergy can cause sneezing, a blocked or runny nose, and itchy, watery eyes. Symptoms may last for weeks, but they overlap with other conditions. A note of when you were outside and how symptoms changed can help a clinician assess them.

## Leave less pollen indoors
When pollen levels are high, a suitable mask and wraparound glasses can reduce contact. Change clothes and shower after being outside. Ask a clinician or pharmacist if symptoms disrupt school or sleep. Some antihistamines cause drowsiness, so mention your daily activities. Check local pollen information rather than assuming warm weather means high exposure.

sources.title: NHS · Hay fever, reviewed March 2024

credit: Janice Haney Carr; Betsy Crane / CDC PHIL #8720 · Public domain
imageAlt: Scanning electron micrograph of yellow sundrops pollen grains, CDC archive, 2006; a pollen illustration, not an allergic rhinitis diagnosis or local pollen measurement.

title.zh: 踏青回来，除了洗手还该检查什么？
title.en: Back from a walk: check for ticks, too

summary.zh: 草地和灌木中的蜱虫，可能随衣物和背包进入家中。
summary.en: Ticks can travel home on clothing and outdoor gear.

body.zh:
## 尽量走在步道中间
蜱虫可出现在草丛、灌木和林地。出行时减少穿过高草和落叶堆，选择步道中间行走；如使用驱避产品，按标签要求选择和使用，不把衣物专用处理剂直接涂在皮肤上。

## 回家后检查衣物，也检查身体
留意背包、外套和身上的蜱虫，尤其是耳后、发际、腋下、腰部和膝后等不容易看见的地方，可借助镜子检查。洗澡有助于冲走尚未附着的蜱虫，但不能替代全身检查。若发现已经附着、自己不会安全处理的蜱虫，应尽快寻求专业帮助。
body.en:
## Stay near the centre of the trail
Ticks can live in grass, brush and wooded areas. Avoid high grass and leaf litter where practical. Follow the label when choosing and using repellents; products intended only for treating clothing should not be applied to skin.

## Check after coming indoors
Inspect bags, outer clothing and your body. Look around the ears and hairline, under the arms, around the waist and behind the knees; a mirror can help. A shower may wash off unattached ticks, but it does not replace a body check. Seek prompt professional help if a tick is attached and you cannot remove it safely.

sources.title: CDC · Preventing tick bites, 28 August 2024

credit: James Gathany; William L. Nicholson / CDC PHIL #7663 · Public domain
imageAlt: Dorsal view of a female western blacklegged tick, Ixodes pacificus, photographed in 2005; not a mosquito, proof of infection in this specimen or local YSPH surveillance.

title.zh: 剩菜要在桌上放到完全凉透吗？
title.en: Should leftovers sit out until completely cool?

summary.zh: 及时冷藏，比一直放在室温下等待更重要。
summary.en: Prompt refrigeration matters more than waiting on the counter.

body.zh:
## 室温下，微生物仍会繁殖
熟食放在室温下，微生物可能快速繁殖。WHO的食品安全五要点建议：熟食不要在室温下放置超过两小时，易腐食品应及时冷藏，冷藏温度最好低于5℃。两小时不是所有环境下都能安全等待的承诺。

## 冰箱也不能无限延长保质期
不要为了等饭菜完全凉透而长时间放在桌上。妥善分装、及时冷藏，并避免存放过久；再次食用时充分加热。冷冻食品也不应直接放在室温下解冻。无法确认储存过程是否安全时，别把重新加热当成万能补救。
body.en:
## Room temperature allows microbes to grow
Microorganisms can multiply quickly in cooked food left at room temperature. WHO advises not leaving cooked food out for more than two hours and refrigerating perishable food promptly, preferably below 5°C. Two hours is not a promise that waiting is safe in every setting.

## Refrigeration has limits
Do not leave a meal on the table for a long time while waiting for it to cool completely. Portion and refrigerate it promptly, avoid prolonged storage, and reheat thoroughly before eating. Do not thaw frozen food at room temperature. Reheating is not a universal fix for an unsafe storage history.

sources.title: WHO · Five keys to safer food manual (2006), safe temperatures

imageAlt: An open food refrigerator documented by a health inspector at a migrant worker camp in 1975; archival storage illustration, not verified food temperatures, a current storage demonstration or a YSPH inspection.

title.zh: 1型糖尿病，是因为糖吃多了吗？
title.en: Is type 1 diabetes caused by eating too much sugar?

summary.zh: 认识胰岛素和自身免疫，少一些对患者的误解。
summary.en: Understanding insulin and autoimmunity helps avoid misplaced blame.

body.zh:
## 先分清是哪一种糖尿病
1型糖尿病中，免疫系统破坏胰腺里制造胰岛素的细胞。胰岛素帮助葡萄糖进入细胞；供应不足时，血糖会升高。把它简单归因于爱吃糖，会误解这种自身免疫性疾病。

## 日常管理需要持续支持
患者通常需要每天使用胰岛素并监测血糖，饮食和活动安排也要纳入个人照护计划。频繁口渴、排尿增多或不明原因消瘦，应及时就医检查。不要因网上一句“少吃糖就好”自行停药，也不要用同学是否吃甜食来判断他有没有认真管理病情。
body.en:
## The type matters
In type 1 diabetes, the immune system destroys insulin-producing cells in the pancreas. Insulin helps glucose enter cells; when there is too little, blood glucose rises. Blaming a preference for sweet food misrepresents this autoimmune disease.

## Management needs ongoing support
People usually need insulin every day and blood-glucose monitoring, with food and activity included in a personal care plan. Persistent thirst, frequent urination or unexplained weight loss need prompt medical assessment. Do not stop prescribed treatment because of online dietary advice, or judge a classmate's care by whether they eat something sweet.

sources.title: NIDDK / NIH · Type 1 diabetes, reviewed February 2025

credit: Amanda Mills / CDC PHIL #13708 · Public domain
imageAlt: A woman using an electronic blood glucose meter in a 2011 CDC photograph; illustrates self-monitoring, not a diagnosis from the displayed reading or a YSPH clinic.

title.zh: 上次只起了疹子，下次就一定没事吗？
title.en: Does a mild food reaction mean the next one will be mild?

summary.zh: 过敏反应的轻重不能靠上一次经历保证。
summary.en: The previous reaction cannot guarantee the severity of the next.

body.zh:
## 反应可能改变
食物过敏涉及免疫系统对某些食物的反应，可能表现为瘙痒、荨麻疹或胃肠不适，也可能出现严重反应。曾经反应较轻，不代表再次接触也一定较轻。怀疑过敏时，应由医生结合病史和必要检查评估，不要在家反复试吃验证。

## 共同吃饭前，把信息问清楚
确诊后按个人方案避开过敏原，仔细看配料标签，向备餐者说明需要避开的食物。不要劝有过敏史的人“尝一点”。进食后出现呼吸困难、明显头晕或晕厥，应立即寻求急救；已经有医生制定的应急方案时，按方案处理。
body.en:
## Reactions can change
Food allergy involves an immune reaction to a food. It can cause itching, hives or digestive symptoms, and sometimes a severe reaction. A mild past reaction does not guarantee a mild one next time. Suspected allergy needs clinical assessment, not repeated test bites at home.

## Ask before sharing food
After diagnosis, follow the personal management plan, read ingredient labels and tell the person preparing food what must be avoided. Do not pressure someone to try a little. Trouble breathing, marked dizziness or fainting after eating needs immediate emergency care. Follow any emergency plan already provided by the person's clinician.

sources.title: NIH News in Health · Understanding food allergies (March 2017), symptoms and precautions

credit: James Gathany / CDC PHIL #13120 (content provider: Mary Anne Fenley) · Public domain
imageAlt: A rice dish containing peanuts, walnuts and raisins in a 2007 CDC photograph; a food-allergy topic illustration, not an allergy test, allergy-safe recipe or claim about an individual's reaction.

title.zh: 运动过了，剩下的时间就能一直坐着吗？
title.en: After exercise, does sitting time still matter?

summary.zh: 每天运动和减少久坐，是可以同时安排的两件事。
summary.en: Regular exercise and less sedentary time can fit into the same day.

body.zh:
## 留意整天的安排
WHO的2020年指南同时讨论身体活动与久坐。完成一次运动，并不意味着其余时间可以完全忽略活动。对儿童和青少年，指南建议限制久坐时间，尤其是娱乐性屏幕时间；对成年人，用任何强度的活动替代一部分久坐也有益。

## 找到能起身的间隙
在课间走动、步行取水，或把一部分坐着聊天的时间改成散步，都是调整日常的例子。它们不能完全代替适龄的运动安排。指南没有给所有人规定统一的“每坐多少分钟必须起立”，无需把某个计时器数字当成医学界限。
body.en:
## Look at the whole day
WHO's 2020 guidelines address activity and sedentary behaviour together. One exercise session does not make the rest of the day's movement irrelevant. Children and adolescents should limit sedentary time, particularly recreational screen time. For adults, replacing sitting with activity of any intensity has benefits.

## Use the gaps that suit your day
Walk during a break, get up for water, or turn part of a seated conversation into a walk. These are examples, not replacements for age-appropriate exercise. The guidelines do not set one universal interval at which everyone must stand up; a timer is a reminder, not a medical boundary.

sources.title: WHO · Guidelines on physical activity and sedentary behaviour (2020)

credit: Amanda Mills / CDC PHIL #13755 · Public domain
imageAlt: Hands working at a laptop with reference books in the background, CDC archive, 2011; illustrates desk work, not a complete ergonomic posture assessment or YSPH activity.

title.zh: 墙角反复发霉，为什么擦掉还不够？
title.en: Why does mould keep coming back in the same corner?

summary.zh: 处理霉斑的同时，要找到让它生长的水分来源。
summary.en: The moisture source needs attention as well as the visible patch.

body.zh:
## 潮湿条件没有改变
霉菌孢子在空气中存在，落到潮湿表面后可能生长。若只擦掉霉斑，漏水、冷凝或长期潮湿的问题还在，霉菌往往会回来。修复漏水、让受潮材料及时干燥，是处理过程的一部分。

## 别把所有清理都当成家务小事
霉菌可能引起过敏和刺激，对霉菌过敏的哮喘患者也可能出现发作。大面积霉变、严重水损或污水污染，应请有经验的专业人员处理。不要直接在霉斑上刷漆遮盖；有健康顾虑的人，清理前先咨询专业人员。
body.en:
## The damp conditions may still be there
Airborne mould spores can grow when they land on damp surfaces. If a leak, condensation or persistent dampness remains, wiping away the visible patch often leaves the cause unchanged. Repairing leaks and drying wet materials are part of the work.

## Some cleanup needs professional help
Mould can cause allergic reactions and irritation, and can trigger asthma in people allergic to it. Extensive growth, major water damage or sewage contamination needs experienced professional help. Do not paint over mould. Anyone with health concerns should seek professional advice before starting cleanup.

sources.title: US EPA · A brief guide to mold, moisture and your home (2012 reprint)

credit: Ginger Chew / CDC PHIL #20859 (content providers: Ginger Chew; Lisa Marianni) · Public domain
imageAlt: Exposed wooden wall studs with mould in a flood-damaged home photographed after Hurricane Sandy in 2012; not a species identification, medical diagnosis or YSPH site inspection.

title.zh: 被动物咬伤后，为什么不能等症状出现？
title.en: Why act after an animal bite instead of waiting for symptoms?

summary.zh: 暴露后处置要及时，是否需要疫苗应由专业人员评估。
summary.en: Post-exposure care is time-sensitive and needs professional assessment.

body.zh:
## 预防要赶在发病之前
狂犬病病毒可通过受感染动物的唾液进入咬伤、抓伤或黏膜。一旦出现临床症状，疾病几乎总是致命的；及时、规范的暴露后预防能够避免死亡。因此，不能靠等自己有没有不舒服来决定是否就医。

## 冲洗后，尽快去评估
可能暴露后，应立即用肥皂和大量清水冲洗伤口至少15分钟，并尽快就医。专业人员会评估是否需要疫苗，以及是否需要免疫球蛋白等处置。此前接种过疫苗，也仍应就医评估。不要为了自行观察动物或寻找接种记录而拖延就诊。
body.en:
## Prevention must come before illness
Rabies can enter through bites, scratches or mucous membranes exposed to infected saliva. Once clinical symptoms appear, the disease is almost always fatal. Prompt, appropriate post-exposure prevention can prevent death, so waiting to feel unwell is unsafe.

## Wash and seek care promptly
After a possible exposure, immediately wash the wound with soap and plenty of water for at least 15 minutes and seek medical care promptly. Professionals assess the need for vaccination and additional measures such as immunoglobulin. Previous vaccination does not remove the need for assessment. Do not delay care to observe the animal yourself or search for records.

sources.title: WHO · Rabies post-exposure prophylaxis protocol (1 May 2024)
WHO · Rabies vaccines: position paper (April 2018)
