title.zh: HPV疫苗和宫颈筛查，作用有什么不同？
title.en: HPV vaccination and cervical screening do different jobs

summary.zh: 一个着眼于预防感染，一个帮助发现癌前变化。
summary.en: Vaccination prevents infections; screening can find precancerous changes.

body.zh:
## 接种疫苗不能治疗已有感染
HPV是一组常见病毒。多数感染会由身体自行控制，但部分高危型持续感染可能导致宫颈癌等癌症。预防性HPV疫苗帮助预防相关感染，并非用来治疗已经存在的感染或病变。

## 筛查寻找没有症状的变化
宫颈筛查可以发现癌前变化，让人有机会在发展为癌症前接受处理。疫苗与适龄筛查承担不同作用，不能互相简单替代。接种产品、适用年龄与剂次，向当地接种门诊确认；何时开始筛查及复查间隔，应结合当地指南和个人情况咨询医生。
body.en:
## Vaccination does not treat an existing infection
HPV is a common group of viruses. The body controls most infections, but persistent infection with some high-risk types can cause cervical and other cancers. Preventive HPV vaccines help prevent infection; they do not treat existing infection or lesions.

## Screening looks for changes before symptoms
Cervical screening can detect precancerous changes that can be treated before cancer develops. Vaccination and age-appropriate screening have different roles. Ask a local vaccination clinic about available products, eligible ages and doses. Discuss screening timing with a clinician using local guidance and your personal circumstances.

sources.title: WHO · Human papillomavirus and cancer (5 March 2024)

credit: James Gathany / CDC PHIL #9400 (content provider: Judy Schmidt) · Public domain
imageAlt: An adolescent receiving an intramuscular vaccination from a nurse in 2006; the vaccine is unspecified, not confirmed as HPV vaccine, and this is not a YSPH clinic.

title.zh: 防诺如病毒，免洗洗手液能代替洗手吗？
title.en: Can hand sanitizer replace washing for norovirus prevention?

summary.zh: 肥皂和流动水仍然重要，戴手套也不能省去洗手。
summary.en: Soap and water still matter, including when gloves are used.

body.zh:
## 用肥皂和水认真洗
诺如病毒可通过受污染的手、食物和表面传播。CDC建议用肥皂和水揉搓洗手至少20秒，尤其是如厕后，以及进食、备餐前。酒精免洗产品可以作为补充，不能替代这一步；戴手套前后也应洗手。

## 不舒服时，别替别人备餐
呕吐、腹泻时为他人处理食物，容易把病毒带给别人。CDC给食品从业人员的建议是：生病期间，以及症状停止后至少48小时不要工作。学校和当地卫生部门可能另有要求，应按规定执行；恢复后也要继续认真洗手。
body.en:
## Use soap and water
Norovirus can spread through contaminated hands, food and surfaces. CDC advises washing with soap and water for at least 20 seconds, especially after using the toilet and before eating or preparing food. Alcohol-based sanitizer can supplement washing, not replace it. Wash before and after using gloves, too.

## Do not prepare food for others while ill
Vomiting or diarrhoea makes food handling a risk to others. CDC advises food workers to stay off work while ill and for at least 48 hours after symptoms stop. Follow school and local health requirements, which may differ, and keep washing carefully after recovery.

sources.title: CDC · Norovirus: facts for food workers (revised 20 March 2024)

credit: Erskin L. Palmer / CDC PHIL #2172 · Public domain
imageAlt: Genuine transmission electron micrograph of two clusters of norovirus particles, CDC archive, 1981; not a computer rendering, current outbreak specimen or YSPH laboratory image.

title.zh: 会游泳，就可以少一层防护吗？
title.en: Does knowing how to swim remove the need for other precautions?

summary.zh: 游泳技能、持续看护和合适的救生衣，各有作用。
summary.en: Swimming skills, supervision and a suitable life jacket each have a role.

body.zh:
## 技能不能消除水域风险
学习游泳能降低溺水风险，但学过游泳的孩子，在水边和水中仍需成年人持续、近距离看护。负责看护的人应避免看手机或做其他分散注意力的事；有救生员也不能把看护责任完全交出去。

## 充气玩具不是救生设备
泳圈、充气臂圈可能滑脱，不能替代合适且正确穿戴的救生衣。乘船和参加自然水域活动时，选择符合当地适用标准、尺寸合适并扣好的救生衣。河流、湖泊和海洋还有水流、能见度等风险，不能用泳池里的经验判断是否安全。
body.en:
## Skills do not remove water hazards
Swimming lessons can reduce drowning risk, but children still need close, constant adult supervision in and around water. The supervising adult should avoid phones and other distractions. A lifeguard does not replace that responsibility.

## Inflatable toys are not safety equipment
Rings and inflatable arm bands can slip off. They do not replace a correctly fitted, fastened life jacket that meets applicable local standards. Use suitable life jackets for boating and natural-water activities. Rivers, lakes and seas have currents and visibility hazards that a pool may not have.

sources.title: CDC · Preventing drowning (29 September 2025)

imageAlt: Orange lifejackets stored overhead aboard a Staten Island ferry in New York, photographed in 2009; archival water-safety illustration, not a fit demonstration or YSPH activity.

title.zh: 手足口病，只有小孩子会得吗？
title.en: Can older children and adults get hand, foot and mouth disease?

summary.zh: 它在幼儿中常见，但年龄大不代表不会感染。
summary.en: It is common in young children, but older age does not rule it out.

body.zh:
## 常见于幼儿，不限于幼儿
手足口病在5岁以下儿童中较常见，其他年龄的人也可能感染。常见表现包括发热、咽痛、口腔疼痛性疱疹，以及手脚皮疹。多数患者约7至10天好转，但不能仅凭一处皮疹自行确诊。

## 照顾弟妹时，也要认真洗手
经常用肥皂和水洗手，清洁并消毒常接触的表面，避免与患者密切接触，有助于减少传播。口腔疼痛可能影响喝水，要留意补水情况；喝不下水、担心脱水或症状严重时及时就医。返校和托幼安排应按医生、学校及当地卫生部门要求处理。
body.en:
## Common in young children, possible at other ages
Hand, foot and mouth disease is common under age five, but anyone can get it. Fever, sore throat, painful mouth blisters and a rash on the hands or feet are typical. Most people improve in about seven to ten days. A rash alone does not confirm the diagnosis.

## Take care when looking after younger children
Wash with soap and water, clean and disinfect frequently touched surfaces, and avoid close contact with someone who is ill. Painful mouth sores can make drinking difficult. Seek care if drinking is difficult, dehydration is a concern or symptoms are severe. Follow local advice on returning to school or childcare.

sources.title: CDC · About hand, foot and mouth disease (7 May 2024)

credit: Amanda Mills / CDC PHIL #13532 · Public domain
imageAlt: Hands rubbing together with soap lather beside a running faucet, CDC archive, 2011; a hand-hygiene photograph, not a disease diagnosis, pathogen image or YSPH activity.

title.zh: 和乙肝感染者一起吃饭，会被传染吗？
title.en: Can sharing a meal spread hepatitis B?

summary.zh: 了解传播途径，才能把预防和日常相处分开。
summary.en: Knowing the routes of transmission helps avoid unnecessary exclusion.

body.zh:
## 共同用餐不是传播途径
乙肝病毒主要通过受感染的血液及某些体液传播，也可在分娩时由母亲传给婴儿。共用餐具、拥抱、咳嗽和打喷嚏不是传播途径。一起吃饭或上课，不是排斥感染者的理由。

## 预防重点是接种与必要检查
乙肝疫苗可以预防感染。是否需要补种或检查，应结合接种记录、接触风险和医生建议决定。感染者可能长期没有明显症状，不能凭气色判断；确诊慢性感染后，应按医嘱随访，评估肝脏情况及是否需要治疗。
body.en:
## Ordinary shared meals do not transmit it
Hepatitis B spreads through infected blood and certain body fluids, and can pass from mother to baby at birth. Sharing utensils, hugging, coughing and sneezing are not routes of transmission. Sharing a meal or classroom is not a reason to exclude someone.

## Focus on vaccination and appropriate testing
Vaccination can prevent infection. Discuss records, exposure risks and any need for testing or additional vaccination with a clinician. Infection can remain without obvious symptoms, so appearance cannot establish someone's status. People with chronic infection need follow-up to assess liver health and whether treatment is needed.

sources.title: CDC · Hepatitis B general information (June 2016), transmission and testing
WHO · Chronic hepatitis B guidelines (29 March 2024)

credit: Dr. Erskine Palmer / CDC PHIL #270 · Public domain
imageAlt: Genuine black-and-white transmission electron micrograph of hepatitis B virus particles, including Dane particles; CDC archive, 1981, not a patient blood-test result or YSPH laboratory image.

title.zh: 烫伤后，别急着涂牙膏
title.en: After a scald, skip the toothpaste

summary.zh: 先脱离热源，用凉的流动水降温，避免偏方造成额外伤害。
summary.en: Move away from the heat and cool with running water, not household remedies.

body.zh:
## 先确认现场安全
处理烫伤前，先让伤者脱离热源，也要保证施救者安全。WHO建议用凉的流动水降低烧伤部位温度。不要直接敷冰，也不要涂牙膏、油或其他偏方；这些做法可能加重损伤或妨碍后续处理。

## 不要自己挑破水疱
保持创面清洁，不随意涂药或挑破水疱，并及时获得医疗评估。这篇介绍的是热烧烫伤的基本原则，不能替代现场判断。化学品、电或火灾造成的损伤，需要先处理相应危险并寻求专业救助；冲水降温时也要避免让伤者长时间受冷。
body.en:
## Make the scene safe first
Move the person away from the heat without putting the helper at risk. WHO recommends cool running water to lower the temperature of a burn. Do not apply ice, toothpaste, oil or household pastes; they may worsen injury or complicate care.

## Leave blisters intact
Keep the area clean, avoid unprescribed topical treatments and do not burst blisters. Seek medical assessment. These are basic principles for thermal burns, not a substitute for assessment of the situation. Chemical, electrical and fire-related injuries have additional hazards requiring professional help. Avoid prolonged cooling that leaves the person too cold.

sources.title: WHO · Burns (13 October 2023), first aid

credit: Troy Kelly (troykelly) / Wikimedia Commons · CC BY 2.0
imageAlt: A metal kettle heating over a blue gas flame in a Tokyo apartment kitchen, photographed in 2007; hot-water and burn-hazard illustration, with no injury shown and no claim that the whole setup is safe.

title.zh: 没有闻到异味，为什么也可能一氧化碳中毒？
title.en: Why can carbon monoxide be dangerous without a warning smell?

summary.zh: 一氧化碳无色无味，开门窗也不能让室内使用燃油发电机变得安全。
summary.en: Carbon monoxide is colourless and odourless. Open windows do not make indoor generator use safe.

body.zh:
## 嗅觉不是报警器
一氧化碳是无色、无味的有毒气体，可在燃料燃烧时产生。燃油发电机等设备在封闭或半封闭空间使用，可能造成危险积聚。没有烟味或臭味，不能证明空气安全。

## 室外也要远离开口
不要在住宅、车库或其他室内空间运行便携式燃油发电机，即使门窗开着也不行。CDC建议放在室外，并与门、窗及通风口保持至少20英尺（约6米）的距离。怀疑中毒时，应在确保自身安全的前提下立即离开危险区域，到新鲜空气处寻求急救，不要自行返回现场救人。
body.en:
## Your nose is not an alarm
Carbon monoxide is a colourless, odourless poisonous gas produced during fuel combustion. Fuel-powered generators in enclosed or partly enclosed spaces can cause dangerous build-up. A lack of smoke or smell does not establish safety.

## Outdoors still means away from openings
Never run a portable fuel-powered generator inside a home, garage or other indoor space, even with doors and windows open. CDC advises outdoor use at least 20 feet, about six metres, from doors, windows and vents. If poisoning is suspected, leave for fresh air without endangering yourself and seek emergency help. Do not re-enter to attempt a rescue yourself.

sources.title: CDC / NIOSH · Carbon monoxide hazards at work (30 September 2024)

credit: Tony Webster / Wikimedia Commons · CC BY 2.0
imageAlt: An old four-burner gas stove with no visible flames, photographed in 2005; fuel-appliance illustration, not evidence of a carbon monoxide leak, measured exposure or safe heating use.

title.zh: 麻疹还没出疹，也可能传染吗？
title.en: Can measles spread before the rash appears?

summary.zh: 认识出疹前的传染期，别把有无皮疹当成唯一判断。
summary.en: The infectious period starts before the rash, so appearance alone is not enough.

body.zh:
## 出疹并不是传播的起点
麻疹是一种传染性很强的呼吸道病毒感染。早期可能发热、咳嗽、流鼻涕或眼结膜发炎，之后才出现皮疹。CDC的临床资料指出，患者在出疹前4天至出疹后4天可具有传染性。没有皮疹，不能据此排除传播风险。

## 怀疑感染时，先联系医疗机构
发热出疹，尤其伴有已知接触史时，应及时寻求医疗评估，并先告知医疗机构疑似麻疹和接触情况，方便安排防护。不要只在网上比对皮疹照片。接种记录不清楚的人，可咨询接种门诊，按当地要求核查含麻疹成分疫苗的接种情况。
body.en:
## Transmission can start before the rash
Measles is a highly contagious respiratory viral infection. Fever, cough, a runny nose or conjunctivitis can precede the rash. CDC clinical guidance identifies an infectious period from four days before to four days after rash onset. Absence of a rash does not rule out transmission risk.

## Contact the clinic before arriving
Seek prompt assessment for fever with a rash, particularly after a known exposure. Tell the clinic beforehand about possible measles and the exposure so precautions can be arranged. Comparing rash photographs online cannot confirm a diagnosis. If vaccination records are unclear, ask a local vaccination clinic to review them under local guidance.

sources.title: CDC · Measles clinical diagnosis fact sheet (2025)

credit: Dr. Erskine Palmer / CDC PHIL #5622 · Public domain
imageAlt: Digitally colorized genuine transmission electron micrograph showing a large measles virus particle with smaller SV40 particles; CDC archive, 1981, not a rendering or YSPH specimen.

title.zh: 书包背得肩颈疼，先检查这几处
title.en: Shoulders aching after school? Check the backpack

summary.zh: 减少不必要的负重，调整双肩带和物品位置。
summary.en: Remove unnecessary weight and check the straps and packing.

body.zh:
## 双肩带都用上
过重或使用不当的书包可能带来肩、颈和背部疼痛。选择尺寸合适、有宽软肩带的书包，使用双肩带并调整到负重贴近背部。不要总靠一边肩膀承担重量。

## 先清包，再谈换包
只带当天需要的物品，把较重的东西放在包内较低、靠近中间的位置。有条件时利用储物柜或与学校商量减少来回搬书。若背包让人提起、穿脱都很吃力，就需要重新检查负重；持续疼痛、麻木或刺痛不应硬扛，应告诉家长并寻求评估。
body.en:
## Use both shoulder straps
An overloaded or poorly worn backpack can cause shoulder, neck and back pain. Choose an appropriate size with wide, padded straps. Use both straps and adjust them to keep the load close to the back. Avoid carrying everything on one shoulder.

## Empty unnecessary items before buying another bag
Carry what the day requires and put heavier items low and towards the centre. Use a locker where available or discuss reducing book transport with school. Struggling to lift or put on the bag is a reason to review the load. Tell a parent about persistent pain, numbness or tingling and seek assessment.

sources.title: AAOS · Avoid pain from backpacks this school year (3 August 2018)

credit: Personal Creations / Wikimedia Commons · CC BY 2.0
imageAlt: School backpacks, water bottles, notebooks and pencil cases arranged on a wooden surface in a 2015 photograph; not a patient's diagnosis, a measured bag load or a YSPH school scene.

title.zh: 朋友情绪低落，怎样陪伴比较合适？
title.en: When a friend is struggling, how can you help?

summary.zh: 认真听、询问需要什么，也知道何时找成年人一起帮忙。
summary.en: Listen, ask what they need and know when to involve a trusted adult.

body.zh:
## 给对方说话的余地
可以从一句具体的关心开始，例如“最近看你很累，愿意聊聊吗？”这是对话示例，不需要照着背。听对方愿意说的内容，少急着评价或给出解决办法，也不要逼问。联合国儿童基金会等机构的同伴支持资料强调倾听和帮助朋友连接支持。

## 不必独自承担照护责任
同伴陪伴不能替代专业帮助。可以和朋友商量，联系信任的家长、老师或学校心理老师；涉及人身安全或紧急危险时，要及时找可信任的成年人及专业救助。尊重朋友的隐私，但不要承诺无论发生什么都替他保密。支持别人时，也要照顾自己的状态。
body.en:
## Leave room for them to speak
An opening might be, 'You seem tired lately. Would you like to talk?' This is an example, not a script. Listen to what they choose to share without pressing for details, judging or rushing to solve the problem. UNICEF and partner guidance stresses listening and connecting a friend with support.

## Do not carry the responsibility alone
Friendship does not replace professional care. Discuss involving a trusted parent, teacher or school counsellor. Immediate safety concerns need trusted adult and professional help promptly. Respect privacy, but do not promise unconditional secrecy. Look after your own wellbeing while helping someone else.

sources.title: UNICEF / partners · I Support My Friends: theory and implementation guide (June 2021)

credit: Chris Waits / Wikimedia Commons · CC BY 2.0
imageAlt: Two friends seated and chatting in the Jardin du Luxembourg in Paris in 2011; archival social-connection illustration, not a diagnosis, documented counseling session or YSPH activity.

title.zh: “风险降低一半”，到底少了多少？
title.en: A risk cut in half: how much has actually changed?

summary.zh: 把相对变化和绝对变化放在一起看。
summary.en: Read the relative change alongside the absolute change.

body.zh:
## 先问原本有多大
用一个假设例子：同样的观察期内，某事件发生概率从每100人中2人降到1人。相对而言，风险降低了50%；绝对而言，减少了1个百分点。两个说法描述的是同一次变化，都不是每100人少了50人。这个例子不对应任何具体药物。

## 再问研究说的是谁、多久
比较数字时，要确认观察期、研究人群和统计的事件相同。某一人群的平均风险，也不直接等于你的个人风险。读到“翻倍”“减半”时，寻找原始发生率，再结合研究对象理解，而不是只凭标题决定停药、用药或改变检查安排。
body.en:
## Ask what the starting risk was
In a hypothetical example, the chance of an event during the same follow-up period falls from two people in 100 to one in 100. That is a 50% relative reduction and a one-percentage-point absolute reduction. Both describe the same change, not 50 fewer people in 100. No particular medicine is being described.

## Check who and how long
Compare the same event, population and observation period. A group average is not automatically your personal risk. When a headline says doubled or halved, look for the starting frequency. A headline alone should not determine treatment or screening decisions.

sources.title: NIH News in Health · Understanding health risks (October 2016)

credit: Ella's Dad / Wikimedia Commons · CC BY 2.0
imageAlt: Two physical six-sided dice on a surface with shadows, photographed in 2007; a probability illustration, not clinical data, a calculated personal risk or a claim about whether the dice are fair.

title.zh: RSV像感冒，为什么还要留意？
title.en: Why pay attention to RSV if it feels like a cold?

summary.zh: 同一种病毒，对不同年龄的人影响可能不同。
summary.en: The same virus can affect people differently at different ages.

body.zh:
## 得过一次，还可能再感染
呼吸道合胞病毒（RSV）常引起流鼻涕、咳嗽和食欲下降，也可能出现喘息。感染后并不会获得终身保护。较大的孩子和成年人常症状较轻，但婴儿、老年人和免疫功能较弱者可能出现严重疾病。

## 看呼吸和进食情况
呼吸困难、喝不下水或症状持续加重时，应及时就医，不能只看有没有发热。洗手、遮挡咳嗽和打喷嚏、避免用未清洁的手摸脸，有助于减少传播。有感冒样症状时，尽量避免与婴儿等高风险人群密切接触。
body.en:
## Infection can happen again
Respiratory syncytial virus, or RSV, commonly causes a runny nose, cough and reduced appetite; wheezing can occur. Having had it does not provide lifelong protection. Older children and adults often have mild illness, but infants, older adults and people with weakened immunity can become seriously ill.

## Watch breathing and drinking
Seek prompt care for difficulty breathing, difficulty drinking or worsening symptoms. Do not judge severity by fever alone. Wash hands, cover coughs and sneezes, and avoid touching your face with unwashed hands. With cold-like symptoms, avoid close contact with high-risk people, including babies.

sources.title: NIH News in Health · Recognizing RSV (September 2021), symptoms and prevention

credit: Dr. Erskine Palmer / CDC PHIL #276 · Public domain
imageAlt: Genuine black-and-white transmission electron micrograph of liberated, chain-like RSV RNA, CDC archive, 1981; not an illustration, whole-virus portrait or current specimen.

title.zh: 孩子咳嗽时，为什么要观察呼吸？
title.en: Why watch a child's breathing when they have a cough?

summary.zh: 呼吸费力，比咳嗽声音更值得警惕。
summary.en: Breathing effort matters more than the sound of a cough.

body.zh:
## 肺炎影响的是肺部换气
肺炎可由细菌、病毒或真菌引起。肺内的小气囊发生炎症、积聚液体后，会影响氧气进入身体。幼儿咳嗽时，呼吸明显加快、吸气时下胸部向内凹陷，都是需要医疗评估的信号；不能靠咳嗽声音判断病原体。

## 没有高热，也不能忽视
肺炎可以伴随发热，也可以没有。孩子呼吸困难、无法进食喝水或意识异常时，应立即寻求医疗帮助。抗生素是否需要、如何使用，应由医务人员判断，不要自行用家中剩药。按当地安排接种相关疫苗，并减少接触烟草烟雾，有助于预防。
body.en:
## Pneumonia affects oxygen exchange
Bacteria, viruses or fungi can cause pneumonia. Inflamed air sacs filled with fluid make oxygen exchange harder. In young children with a cough, fast breathing or the lower chest drawing inward during inhalation needs medical assessment. The sound of a cough cannot identify the organism.

## Fever is not always present
Seek emergency care for breathing difficulty, inability to feed or drink, or altered consciousness. A clinician should decide whether antibiotics are needed; do not use leftover medicines. Follow local vaccination advice and reduce exposure to tobacco smoke to help prevent pneumonia.

sources.title: WHO · Pneumonia in children (11 November 2022)

credit: Phyllis Q. Edwards / CDC PHIL #20122 · Public domain
imageAlt: Historical frontal chest radiograph, CDC archive, 1966; the source describes normal findings. Respiratory-imaging context only, not an example or diagnosis of pneumonia.

title.zh: 百日咳，不一定有典型的“鸡鸣声”
title.en: Whooping cough does not always have a whoop

summary.zh: 识别不同年龄的表现，别等咳满一百天才就医。
summary.en: Symptoms vary with age; the name is not a reason to delay care.

body.zh:
## 开始时可能像普通感冒
百日咳由百日咳鲍特菌引起，早期可表现为流鼻涕、轻咳，随后出现阵发性咳嗽，有时咳后呕吐。较大的孩子和成年人可能没有典型的吸气鸣声；婴儿甚至可能咳嗽不明显，却出现呼吸暂停。

## 接种过，也要认真看待症状
疫苗能提供保护，但接种过的人仍可能感染，表现也可能较轻。持续或剧烈咳嗽应就医评估，尤其家中有婴儿时。呼吸暂停或明显呼吸困难需要立即急救。就诊时说明咳嗽持续时间、接种记录及已知接触情况，方便医生判断。
body.en:
## It may begin like a cold
Bordetella pertussis causes whooping cough. A runny nose and mild cough may come before coughing fits, sometimes followed by vomiting. Older children and adults may have no classic whoop. Infants may have little cough but develop pauses in breathing.

## Vaccination does not rule out infection
Vaccines provide protection, but vaccinated people can still become infected, sometimes with milder symptoms. Seek assessment for persistent or severe coughing, especially with a baby at home. Pauses in breathing or marked breathing difficulty require emergency help. Tell the clinician about symptom duration, vaccination records and known exposure.

sources.title: CDC · Pink Book, Chapter 16: Pertussis (12 April 2024), clinical features

imageAlt: Genuine Gram-stained culture photomicrograph of Bordetella pertussis bacteria, CDC archive, 1954; not Bordetella bronchiseptica, a computer rendering or a current specimen.

title.zh: 湿疹反复痒，洗得更勤会好吗？
title.en: Will washing more often help itchy eczema?

summary.zh: 刺激性清洁可能让皮肤更难受。
summary.en: Harsh cleansing can make the skin feel worse.

body.zh:
## 先减少刺激
特应性湿疹会让皮肤干燥、瘙痒，有时好转、有时加重，而且不会传染。香皂、洗涤剂和过热等因素可能诱发不适。反复用力搓洗，不能把湿疹“洗掉”。选择合适的润肤护理，并留意哪些接触会使自己的症状加重。

## 好转后也要继续护理
按医嘱使用润肤剂，症状改善后仍需保湿。不要仅因长湿疹就自行大范围忌口。皮肤突然疼痛、发热、渗液或明显加重，尤其伴有全身不适时，应尽快就医，排查感染等问题；药膏的种类和疗程需要专业指导。
body.en:
## Reduce irritation first
Atopic eczema causes dry, itchy skin with periods of improvement and flare-ups. It is not contagious. Soap, detergents and heat can aggravate symptoms. Hard scrubbing cannot wash eczema away. Use appropriate moisturising care and notice which exposures worsen your own symptoms.

## Continue care when skin improves
Use emollients as advised, including when symptoms settle. Do not cut out whole food groups simply because eczema has appeared. Painful, hot, weeping or rapidly worsening skin, especially with feeling unwell, needs prompt assessment for infection or other complications. Get advice on prescribed creams and treatment duration.

sources.title: NHS · Atopic eczema (reviewed 6 September 2024)

credit: Roland Tanglao / Wikimedia Commons · CC BY 2.0
imageAlt: Small lotion and shampoo bottles with boxed toiletries on a tray, photographed December 4, 2005; ordinary skin-care context, not eczema treatment or a product recommendation.

title.zh: 黑头是没洗干净吗？
title.en: Are blackheads a sign of dirty skin?

summary.zh: 了解毛孔堵塞，也就知道为什么不该使劲搓。
summary.en: Understanding blocked pores helps explain why scrubbing is unhelpful.

body.zh:
## 黑色不等于污垢
痤疮与毛囊被油脂和细胞堵塞有关，青春期激素变化可增加皮脂分泌。黑头暴露于空气后颜色变深，不是洗脸不认真留下的脏东西。长痘也不说明一个人不爱干净。

## 温和清洁，别挤
使用温和洁面产品，避免粗糙磨砂和反复搓洗；挤、抠痘痘可能留下瘢痕或色素沉着。护肤品可以留意“不易堵塞毛孔”标识。治疗通常需要一段时间，不宜几天就频繁换方案；深部疼痛的痘痘、瘢痕或明显困扰，应寻求医生帮助。
body.en:
## The dark colour is not dirt
Acne involves follicles blocked by oil and cells. Hormonal changes during puberty can increase oil production. Blackheads darken on exposure to air; they are not dirt left by poor washing. Acne does not show that someone is unclean.

## Clean gently and avoid squeezing
Use a mild cleanser rather than rough scrubs. Picking and squeezing can leave scars or dark marks. Look for skincare labelled non-comedogenic, meaning less likely to block pores. Treatment takes time, so avoid changing plans every few days. Seek help for deep painful spots, scarring or substantial distress.

sources.title: NIH News in Health · Understanding acne (January 2010), mechanisms and gentle care

imageAlt: Skin-care containers, pink balm and a spoon of powder on a pink surface, photographed December 22, 2021; a neutral product still life, not an acne diagnosis, facial-cleansing sequence or treatment recommendation.

title.zh: 没每天排便，就算便秘吗？
title.en: Does missing a daily bowel movement mean constipation?

summary.zh: 还要看大便是否干硬、排便是否费力，以及习惯有没有改变。
summary.en: Stool consistency, straining and changes from your usual pattern matter too.

body.zh:
## 不只数次数
便秘可能表现为排便比平时少、大便干硬或结块、排便费力，以及排完仍感觉没排净。不能只用“今天没排便”判断，也不能忽视自己排便习惯的持续变化。

## 从饮食和如厕习惯调整
成人可逐渐增加膳食纤维，保持足够饮水和日常活动，有便意时别总忍着。突然大量增加纤维可能不舒服，调整要循序渐进。这些做法仍无改善，或伴便血、无故体重下降、腹痛，应就医。儿童持续便秘应请医生评估，不要照搬成人泻药方案；也不要擅停处方药。
body.en:
## Count more than trips to the toilet
Constipation may involve going less often than usual, hard or lumpy stools, straining or feeling incompletely emptied. One missed day alone is not enough to judge it. Persistent changes from your usual pattern deserve attention.

## Adjust food and toilet habits
Adults can increase fibre gradually, drink enough, stay active and respond to the urge to go. Seek care if changes do not help, or with blood in stools, unexplained weight loss or abdominal pain. Persistent constipation in children needs assessment; do not copy an adult laxative plan. Do not stop prescribed medicines without advice.

sources.title: NHS · Constipation (text reviewed 26 October 2023; adult self-care)

credit: Debora Cartagena / CDC PHIL #14442 · Public domain
imageAlt: Six slices of whole-wheat bread on a green plate, CDC archive, 2012; wholegrain food context, not a prescribed diet, measured fiber portion or guaranteed constipation remedy.

title.zh: 腹泻时，补的为什么不只是水？
title.en: Why does diarrhoea require more than replacing water?

summary.zh: 口服补液盐帮助补回随大便丢失的水和电解质。
summary.en: Oral rehydration solution replaces water and electrolytes lost in stools.

body.zh:
## 丢失的还有盐分
腹泻会让身体丢失水和电解质，脱水是重要风险。口服补液盐（ORS）含有按比例配制的糖和盐，帮助肠道吸收水分，不能简单理解成甜饮料。使用正规产品，按包装要求用清洁水冲配，不要随意增减水量。

## 有些情况不能在家硬撑
便血、腹泻持续不缓解或出现脱水迹象，需要医疗评估；严重脱水可能需要静脉补液。孩子喝不下水、明显嗜睡时应尽快求助。补液是处理的一部分，不能替代对病因和严重程度的判断。预防时仍要注意饮水安全、洗手和食物卫生。
body.en:
## Salts are lost too
Diarrhoea removes water and electrolytes, making dehydration a major concern. Oral rehydration salts, or ORS, contain a measured combination of sugar and salts that helps the intestine absorb water. They are not simply a sweet drink. Mix a recognised product with clean water exactly as its packet directs.

## Know when home care is insufficient
Blood in stools, persistent diarrhoea or dehydration needs assessment. Severe dehydration may require intravenous fluids. Seek prompt help for a child unable to drink or unusually drowsy. Rehydration does not replace assessment of severity and cause. Safe water, handwashing and food hygiene help prevention.

sources.title: WHO · Diarrhoeal disease (7 March 2024)

imageAlt: A server holding a glass of drinking water below its rim, CDC archive, 1975; drinking-water context, not oral rehydration solution or proof of water quality.

title.zh: 不喝牛奶，还能从哪里获得钙？
title.en: Where can you get calcium if you do not drink milk?

summary.zh: 看食物种类，也要看是否强化了钙。
summary.en: Food choices and calcium fortification both matter.

body.zh:
## 奶不是唯一来源
钙参与维持骨骼，也帮助肌肉和神经正常工作。除奶和酸奶外，带骨食用的小鱼、部分绿叶蔬菜、用含钙凝固剂制作的豆腐，以及强化钙的饮品，都可以提供钙。不同产品含量差别很大，不能把所有植物饮品都当成牛奶的等量替代。

## 先看标签，再考虑补充剂
选购时查看营养标签中的钙含量和每份大小；维生素D也有助于钙的吸收。是否需要补充剂，要结合饮食和健康情况咨询专业人员。补钙并非越多越好，也不能靠一片钙片替代日常饮食。
body.en:
## Milk is not the only source
Calcium supports bones, muscles and nerves. Beyond milk and yoghurt, sources include small fish eaten with their bones, some leafy vegetables, calcium-set tofu and calcium-fortified drinks. Amounts vary considerably. Not every plant-based drink provides as much calcium as milk.

## Read the label before buying supplements
Check the calcium amount and serving size. Vitamin D helps calcium absorption too. Discuss whether you need a supplement in light of your diet and health rather than assuming more is better. A calcium tablet does not replace everyday meals.

sources.title: NIAMS · Calcium and vitamin D: important for bone health (May 2023)

credit: James Gathany; Mary Anne Fenley / CDC PHIL #13114 · Public domain
imageAlt: Breakfast setting with a glass of milk, juice, pancakes and turkey bacon, CDC archive, 2007; neutral food context, not a calcium measurement or recommended complete meal plan.

title.zh: 擦干净和消毒，是同一回事吗？
title.en: Are cleaning and disinfecting the same thing?

summary.zh: 先清洁，再按需要消毒；混用清洁剂并不会更安全。
summary.en: Clean first, disinfect when needed, and never mix cleaning chemicals.

body.zh:
## 清洁先把污物去掉
清洁通过水、清洁剂和擦拭去除污物及许多病菌；消毒则利用化学品杀灭表面的大多数病菌。污物可能影响消毒剂发挥作用，所以需要消毒时也应先清洁。日常家庭环境通常做好常规清洁即可，有人生病或免疫功能较弱时再评估消毒需要。

## 留够作用时间
按标签选择适用的表面、浓度和接触时间；一擦就干不一定达到要求。使用时保持通风，按需戴防护用品，不把不同清洁或消毒产品混在一起。把产品放在儿童拿不到的地方，也不要用它们清洁人体。
body.en:
## Remove dirt first
Cleaning uses water, detergent and wiping to remove dirt and many germs. Disinfecting uses chemicals to kill most germs on surfaces. Dirt can interfere, so clean before disinfecting. Routine cleaning is usually sufficient at home; illness or weakened immunity may change the need for disinfection.

## Allow the required contact time
Follow the label for suitable surfaces, dilution and how long the surface must stay wet. An immediate wipe dry may not work. Ventilate and use protective equipment as directed. Never mix cleaning or disinfecting products, keep them away from children, and do not apply them to the body.

sources.title: CDC · When and how to clean and disinfect your home (31 January 2025)

credit: Lauren Bishop; Kelsey Schwarz / CDC PHIL #27976 · Public domain
imageAlt: A yellow-gloved hand using a spray bottle at a kitchen sink, CDC archive, 2023; surface-cleaning context with no chemical mixing shown, not a complete disinfection protocol.

title.zh: “刚挤出来”，不等于更安全
title.en: Freshly collected milk is not necessarily safer

summary.zh: 了解生乳和巴氏杀菌，别只看新鲜程度。
summary.en: Freshness does not replace pasteurisation.

body.zh:
## 生乳可能带有致病菌
未经巴氏杀菌的奶可能含有沙门菌、大肠杆菌、李斯特菌等致病菌。看起来干净、来自熟悉的农场，都不能保证没有这些微生物。儿童、孕妇、老年人及免疫功能较弱者尤其可能出现严重后果。

## 杀菌不是把营养都去掉
巴氏杀菌通过受控加热减少致病微生物，并不会把奶的营养价值全部破坏。购买时查看是否经过适当杀菌，按标签冷藏并留意保质期；经过杀菌也不代表可以随意存放。不能把未经杀菌的生乳当成“天然所以安全”的饮品。
body.en:
## Raw milk can carry harmful germs
Unpasteurised milk can contain Salmonella, E. coli, Listeria and other pathogens. A clean appearance or a familiar farm cannot establish their absence. Children, pregnant people, older adults and people with weakened immunity face particular risks of serious illness.

## Pasteurisation does not remove all nutrition
Controlled heating reduces harmful microorganisms without destroying milk's nutritional value. Check that milk has been appropriately treated, refrigerate as labelled and observe its shelf life. Pasteurised milk still needs proper storage. Natural or freshly collected does not mean safe to drink raw.

sources.title: FDA · Food facts: the dangers of raw milk (May 2024)

credit: CDC / Minnesota Department of Health, R.N. Barr Library; librarians Melissa Rethlefsen and Marie Jones / PHIL #8530 · Public domain
imageAlt: Historical creamery and milk-pasteurization equipment in Faribault, Minnesota, photographed in 1933; not a current factory, brand claim or home-pasteurization demonstration.

title.zh: HIV感染和艾滋病，是同一阶段吗？
title.en: Are HIV infection and AIDS the same stage?

summary.zh: 认识病毒、疾病阶段和治疗，不用外表判断。
summary.en: Understand the virus, disease stages and treatment rather than judging appearance.

body.zh:
## 感染不等于已经发展为艾滋病
HIV会损害免疫系统。艾滋病（AIDS）指HIV感染的最晚期，并不是所有感染者都处于这一阶段。有效的抗逆转录病毒治疗可以控制病毒、保护免疫功能，让感染者长期保持健康。

## 检测和治疗比猜测有用
HIV可经特定体液传播，例如无保护性行为、共用注射器，以及母婴传播。不能凭外表或有没有不舒服判断感染。检测是了解感染状态的途径，初筛或自检阳性仍需专业复核。感染者应按医嘱治疗和随访，不自行停药，也不应被用疾病标签定义。
body.en:
## Infection does not mean AIDS has developed
HIV damages the immune system. AIDS describes the most advanced stage of HIV infection, not everyone living with the virus. Effective antiretroviral treatment can control HIV, protect immunity and support a long, healthy life.

## Testing is more useful than guessing
Transmission involves certain body fluids, including through unprotected sex, shared injection equipment and mother-to-child transmission. Appearance or a lack of symptoms cannot establish HIV status. Testing provides that information; a positive screening or self-test still needs professional confirmation. Follow prescribed treatment and monitoring rather than stopping medicines independently. A diagnosis should not define a person.

sources.title: WHO · HIV and AIDS: questions and answers (30 July 2024)

credit: A. Harrison, P. Feorino, E. L. Palmer and C. Goldsmith / CDC PHIL #1839 · Public domain
imageAlt: Genuine black-and-white transmission electron micrograph of HIV particles cultured with human lymphocytes; CDC archive, 1984. Not a personal test result, disease-stage assessment, current specimen or YSPH image.

title.zh: 天冷时犯困、说话含糊，别只当成累了
title.en: Cold, drowsy and slurring words? Do not assume it is tiredness

summary.zh: 低体温可能发生在室外，也可能发生在寒冷的室内。
summary.en: Hypothermia can happen indoors as well as outside.

body.zh:
## 低体温会影响反应
低体温是核心体温危险下降的状态。寒冷环境中出现反应迟缓、说话含糊、嗜睡或意识混乱，需要警惕；老年人和部分慢性病患者尤其容易受影响。没有身处冰天雪地，也不代表没有风险，室内长时间偏冷同样可能造成问题。

## 怀疑时及时求助
怀疑低体温应立即寻求急救，在不危及自身的前提下帮助对方到温暖处。平时外出采用多层穿衣，保护头部和手部，提前告诉家人行程并带好电话。冬季也要关心家中老人的室内保暖，不能只问一句“你觉得冷吗”。
body.en:
## Low body temperature affects responses
Hypothermia is a dangerous fall in core temperature. Slow responses, slurred speech, drowsiness or confusion during cold exposure need attention. Older adults and some people with chronic conditions are especially vulnerable. It does not require snow or ice; a persistently cold home can also be hazardous.

## Seek help promptly
If hypothermia is suspected, get emergency help and move the person somewhere warmer without endangering yourself. For prevention, wear layers and protect the head and hands. Tell someone your outdoor plans and carry a phone. Check older relatives' indoor warmth rather than relying only on whether they feel cold.

sources.title: NIH / NIA · Hypothermia: a cold weather hazard (21 December 2018)

imageAlt: Winter cycling gloves laid on stone; Commons record dated December 19, 2009. Archival cold-weather clothing illustration, not a current event, product endorsement or proof of protection at any particular temperature.

title.zh: 嘴歪、抬不起手、说话含糊，出现一个就该行动
title.en: Face, arm or speech changes: one sign is enough to act

summary.zh: 怀疑卒中，不要等症状凑齐。
summary.en: Do not wait for several signs before seeking emergency help.

body.zh:
## 记住FAST的含义
FAST帮助识别常见卒中信号：Face，面部一侧下垂或笑容不对称；Arms，一侧手臂突然无力、难以抬起；Speech，突然说话含糊或困难。Time提醒我们：出现其中一个信号，就应立即寻求急救。

## 不必等到看起来很严重
轻微或不够戏剧性的表现也可能是急症。不要等到几个症状同时出现，再决定是不是卒中。这个口诀是帮助行动的线索，不是家庭确诊工具；即使不符合全部描述，也不能用它排除卒中。尽快接受专业评估和治疗很重要。
body.en:
## What FAST means
FAST highlights common stroke signs: Face, a drooping or uneven smile; Arms, sudden weakness or difficulty raising one arm; Speech, sudden slurring or difficulty speaking. Time means seeking emergency help immediately if even one of these signs appears.

## It need not look dramatic
A subtle change may still be an emergency. Do not wait for several symptoms to appear together before acting. FAST is a prompt to seek help, not a way to diagnose someone at home or exclude stroke when the description does not fit completely. Prompt professional assessment and treatment matter.

sources.title: NHS England · Act FAST stroke campaign (4 November 2024)

credit: Dr. Charles Farmer, Jr. / CDC PHIL #30043 · Public domain
imageAlt: A public health nurse visiting a man using a walker; CDC archive, 1963. The source documents a post-stroke rehabilitation visit. Historical care context, not a diagnosis inferred from appearance, a current-care demonstration or a YSPH activity.

title.zh: 有人抽搐时，不要往嘴里塞东西
title.en: Do not put anything in the mouth during a seizure

summary.zh: 保护周围空间、计时，比按住身体更有帮助。
summary.en: Clear hazards and time the seizure; do not restrain the person.

body.zh:
## 先避免受伤
有人倒地抽搐时，移开周围硬物，在头下垫柔软、扁平的物品，在能安全做到时轻轻帮助其侧卧。陪在身边并开始计时。不要强行按住四肢，也不要塞筷子、手指或其他东西进嘴里，这可能造成伤害。

## 哪些情况要立即急救
发作超过5分钟、短时间内再次发作、之后呼吸或清醒困难，或伴有受伤、水中发作，应立即求助。首次发作、孕期发作，或糖尿病患者发作伴失去意识，也需要急救。完全清醒前不要喂水或食物；已知患者还应遵循个人急救计划。
body.en:
## Protect them from injury
Clear nearby hard objects, cushion the head with something soft and flat, and gently help the person onto their side when safe. Stay and time the seizure. Do not hold their limbs down or put chopsticks, fingers or anything else in their mouth.

## When emergency help is needed
Get help for a seizure over five minutes, another soon afterwards, difficulty breathing or waking, injury or a seizure in water. A first seizure, pregnancy, or diabetes with loss of consciousness also needs emergency help. Give no food or drink until fully alert. Follow any established individual seizure plan.

sources.title: CDC · First aid for seizures (15 May 2024)

credit: Chris Hope; shared by Tim Sheerman-Chase / Wikimedia Commons · CC BY 2.0
imageAlt: A research participant wearing EEG electrodes, October 29, 2012, during a human-computer-interface study associated with mammography image screening. General EEG context only; no epilepsy diagnosis is inferred. Not a seizure, first-aid demonstration or YSPH study.

title.zh: 偏头痛，不能只按疼的位置判断
title.en: Migraine is not defined only by where the pain is

summary.zh: 恶心、怕光和发作规律，也能给医生提供线索。
summary.en: Nausea, light sensitivity and attack patterns provide useful clues.

body.zh:
## 还要看伴随症状
偏头痛可能有搏动样疼痛、活动时加重，并伴恶心或对光、声音敏感。部分人会出现闪光、锯齿线等先兆，但不是每个人都有。反复头痛应由医生判断类型，不能只凭“偏一边疼”自我确诊。

## 记录比反复猜测更有用
头痛日记可记录发作时间、持续多久、伴随症状和用药，也留意睡眠、饮水和进餐变化。规律作息、按时吃饭有助于管理部分诱因。频繁使用止痛药本身也可能造成头痛，反复发作或影响上学生活时，应讨论治疗方案，不要自行不断加药。
body.en:
## Associated symptoms matter
Migraine may cause throbbing pain that worsens with movement, nausea, and sensitivity to light or sound. Some people have aura, such as flashing lights or zigzag lines; many do not. Recurrent headache needs assessment rather than diagnosis based only on one-sided pain.

## Keep a headache diary
Record timing, duration, accompanying symptoms and medicines, alongside changes in sleep, hydration and meals. Regular sleep and meals may help manage some triggers. Frequent painkiller use can itself contribute to headache. Discuss a treatment plan if attacks recur or disrupt school and daily life, rather than continually increasing medicines yourself.

sources.title: University Hospitals of Leicester NHS Trust · Managing migraines, leaflet 187 v2 (June 2024)

credit: Sasha Wolff / Wikimedia Commons · CC BY 2.0
imageAlt: A woman with her hands against her head, photographed December 14, 2008; published by Sasha Wolff with a self-reported headache account. Headache-context illustration only, not independent clinical confirmation of migraine, a severity assessment or a YSPH patient.

title.zh: 受伤后，为什么医生会问接种记录？
title.en: Why does a clinician ask about vaccination after an injury?

summary.zh: 伤口处理和破伤风预防，需要一起考虑。
summary.en: Wound care and tetanus prevention need to be considered together.

body.zh:
## 不只是把血擦掉
开放性伤口的清洁、清除坏死组织和异物，都是预防破伤风的重要环节，有些需要由医务人员处理。不能只看表面有没有血，就决定伤口不需要评估。污染或较深的伤口尤其应及时就医。

## 疫苗和免疫球蛋白各有用途
医生会结合伤口情况和既往接种史，判断是否需要含破伤风成分的疫苗，以及是否需要破伤风免疫球蛋白。两者不能简单互相替代。就诊时带上能找到的接种记录；记不清就如实说明，不要凭印象认定小时候打过便终身不必处理。
body.en:
## More than wiping away blood
Cleaning an open wound and removing dead tissue or debris are important parts of tetanus prevention. Some procedures require professional care. Little visible bleeding does not establish that a wound needs no assessment. Contaminated or deep wounds deserve prompt medical attention.

## Vaccines and immunoglobulin have different roles
A clinician considers the wound and vaccination history to decide whether a tetanus-containing vaccine and possibly tetanus immunoglobulin are needed. They are not simply interchangeable. Bring available vaccination records and say when the history is uncertain. Do not assume a childhood injection removes every future need for assessment.

sources.title: WHO · Tetanus: immunization (12 February 2024), wound care principles

imageAlt: Genuine light micrograph of Clostridium tetani bacteria, some showing terminal spores with a tennis-racket appearance; CDC archive, 1995. Not a wound image, personal diagnosis, current sample or YSPH laboratory image.

title.zh: 维生素补得多，就更健康吗？
title.en: Do more vitamins mean better health?

summary.zh: 补充剂也有剂量、重复摄入和相互作用的问题。
summary.en: Dose, overlapping ingredients and interactions matter with supplements too.

body.zh:
## 先问是否需要
营养补充剂用于补足饮食，不能代替多样化进食，也不能当作治病药物。某些饮食限制或健康状况可能使人需要补充特定营养素，但种类和剂量应结合个人情况判断。疲劳等表现也不能单凭感觉认定为缺某种维生素。

## 几瓶一起吃，要算总量
复合维生素、单方补充剂可能含有相同成分，叠加后摄入更多。部分维生素和矿物质过量会有害，草本产品也可能与药物相互作用。咨询医生或药师时，把正在吃的补充剂一并说明；“天然”不是安全保证。
body.en:
## Ask whether you need them
Supplements fill dietary gaps; they do not replace varied meals or act as medicines for disease. Dietary restrictions or health conditions may create particular needs, but the product and dose should fit the person. Tiredness alone cannot identify a vitamin deficiency.

## Add up overlapping ingredients
A multivitamin and separate supplements may contain the same nutrients. Some vitamins and minerals can be harmful in excess. Herbal products can also interact with medicines. Tell a clinician or pharmacist about every supplement you take when seeking advice. A natural label does not guarantee safety.

sources.title: NIH News in Health · Do you need dietary supplements? (December 2021)

credit: Debora Cartagena / CDC PHIL #14418 · Public domain
imageAlt: Two uncapped supplement containers with inner seals visible, the smaller container's seal broken; CDC archive, 2012. Contents are unspecified. Generic packaging context, not a brand endorsement, efficacy claim or safe-storage demonstration.

title.zh: 筛查有异常，和确诊之间还差什么？
title.en: What comes between an abnormal screen and a diagnosis?

summary.zh: 筛查可能带来收益，也可能出现误报和漏报。
summary.en: Screening can help, but false positives and false negatives are possible.

body.zh:
## 筛查先寻找线索
筛查通常在没有相关症状的人群中寻找可能的问题。异常结果可能提示需要进一步检查，并不自动等于确诊。假阳性指结果提示可能患病，实际却没有；假阴性则可能漏掉已有疾病。

## 检查不是越多越好
是否筛查、多久一次，要考虑年龄、家族史及具体检查的利弊。后续检查也可能带来风险和不必要的担心。拿到异常结果后，按建议复核，不要自己下结论；即使此前筛查正常，后来出现症状，也应就医，不能把一次阴性结果当作长期保证。
body.en:
## Screening looks for clues
Screening generally looks for possible problems before related symptoms appear. An abnormal result may call for further testing rather than establish a diagnosis. A false positive suggests disease that is absent; a false negative misses disease that is present.

## More tests are not always better
Age, family history and a test's benefits and harms affect whether and how often to screen. Follow-up procedures can have risks too. Follow advice on confirming an abnormal result rather than drawing your own conclusion. New symptoms still need assessment after a normal screen; one negative result is not a lasting guarantee.

sources.title: NIH News in Health · To screen or not to screen? (March 2017)

credit: Dr. Kokko / CDC PHIL #29879 · Public domain
imageAlt: Laboratory technician Dorothy Allain adding red blood cells to test tubes during a hemagglutination test; CDC archive, 1963. General historical laboratory context, not a modern screening protocol, personal result, screening recommendation or YSPH laboratory.

title.zh: 吃药后不舒服，都算药物过敏吗？
title.en: Is every unpleasant drug reaction an allergy?

summary.zh: 记录具体反应，比只写“过敏”更有用。
summary.en: Recording what happened is more useful than an unexplained allergy label.

body.zh:
## 不良反应不全是过敏
药物可以引起不良反应，但并非都由免疫机制导致。只有恶心、腹泻等胃肠道症状时，药物过敏的可能性相对较低，仍需医生结合完整情况判断。不要自行把一次不适写成终身过敏，也不要擅自删除已有过敏记录。

## 把过程记清楚
记录药名、剂型、服药时间、出现了什么反应，以及多久后发生，带给医生评估。怀疑过敏时，后续是否停用、避用哪些药，需要专业建议；严重反应应立即寻求急救。不要为了验证自己是否过敏，在家再次尝试可疑药物。
body.en:
## Not every adverse reaction is allergic
Medicines can cause adverse effects without an immune-mediated allergy. Isolated nausea or diarrhoea makes allergy less likely, but a clinician needs the full history. Do not turn one unpleasant experience into a lifelong allergy label yourself, or remove an existing label without assessment.

## Record the sequence
Write down the drug name, formulation, dose timing, exact reaction and how soon it began. Share this with the clinician. Suspected allergy needs advice on stopping treatment and which medicines to avoid; severe reactions need emergency help. Do not test a suspected allergy by taking the medicine again at home.

sources.title: NICE · Drug allergy: diagnosis and management, CG183 (3 September 2014; recommendations 1.1–1.3)

imageAlt: Landscape close-up photograph of assorted tablets and capsules, dated August 26, 2016 in the Commons record. Neutral medicine still life; the products are unidentified, with no allergy diagnosis, culprit-drug identification, treatment claim or endorsement implied.

title.zh: 情绪低落持续影响生活，别只归因于不够努力
title.en: When low mood disrupts life, effort is not the whole answer

summary.zh: 抑郁会影响感受、思考和日常活动，需要认真对待。
summary.en: Depression can affect feelings, thinking and everyday activities.

body.zh:
## 留意生活受到的影响
偶尔难过很常见，抑郁障碍则可能持续影响睡眠、进食、思考和日常活动。它与生物、心理及环境等多种因素有关，不是单靠意志力就能解释。不能凭一篇文章或一次网上测试确诊，也不该用“想开点”结束讨论。

## 可以从一次求助开始
情绪或行为变化已经妨碍生活时，可以告诉信任的家长、老师，并寻求医疗评估。专业治疗可包括心理治疗和药物等，方案因人而异。陪伴者可以帮助联系支持，但不能替代诊断；如存在即时安全危险，应立即寻求成年人和专业急救帮助。
body.en:
## Notice the effect on daily life
Occasional sadness is common. Depression can seriously affect sleep, eating, thinking and everyday activities. Biological, psychological and environmental factors contribute; it cannot be explained simply as weak willpower. An article or online quiz cannot establish a diagnosis, and 'cheer up' is not adequate care.

## Start by asking for support
When emotional or behavioural changes disrupt life, tell a trusted parent or teacher and seek medical assessment. Treatment may include psychotherapy or medicines, depending on the person. Friends can help someone reach support but cannot replace diagnosis. Immediate safety danger requires trusted adult and professional emergency help.

sources.title: NIMH · Depression (reviewed December 2024)

credit: Scottish Government / Wikimedia Commons · CC BY 2.0
imageAlt: A group portrait at a Scottish mental-health anti-stigma campaign activity, May 15, 2018, with Maureen Watt, Leith Academy pupils and See Me volunteers. Public advocacy and social-support context; no depression or other diagnosis is inferred. Not a counseling session or YSPH event.

title.zh: 发现头虱，不代表头发脏
title.en: Head lice do not mean dirty hair

summary.zh: 头贴头的接触可以传播，确认时要寻找活虱。
summary.en: Head-to-head contact spreads lice; look for live lice to confirm them.

body.zh:
## 头痒不一定就是头虱
头虱可通过头与头的直接接触传播，与头发是否干净无关。头痒或看到白色小点都不能单独确认，寻找活虱更可靠。细齿检查梳可以帮助检查，不必因为发现头虱就责备或排斥同学。

## 检查身边密切接触的人
确认后，可按指导湿梳去除，也可咨询药师选择适用产品；有些处理需要重复，不能只梳一次便认为结束。检查同住者及密切接触者，有活虱的人应同步处理。不要为了预防就反复使用灭虱药，这可能刺激头皮。
body.en:
## Itching alone does not confirm lice
Head lice spread through direct head-to-head contact, not dirty hair. Itching or white specks alone cannot confirm them; finding a live louse is more reliable. A fine-toothed detection comb helps. Finding lice is not a reason to blame or exclude a classmate.

## Check close contacts too
Follow wet-combing instructions or ask a pharmacist about suitable treatment. Some methods require repeated sessions. Check household members and close contacts, treating those with live lice at the same time. Do not repeatedly use medicated products as prevention; they can irritate the scalp.

title.zh: 眼睛红了，都要用抗生素眼药水吗？
title.en: Does every red eye need antibiotic drops?

summary.zh: 感染和过敏都可能让眼睛发红，处理并不相同。
summary.en: Infection and allergy can both cause redness, but need different care.

body.zh:
## 先弄清原因
结膜炎可能与病毒、细菌或过敏有关，表现可包括发红、流泪、异物感或分泌物。抗生素对病毒和过敏无效，不能因为眼睛红就自行使用。过敏性结膜炎不传染，但也不能仅凭外观确定原因。

## 这些表现不要只当结膜炎
眼痛、怕光或视力变化，应及时就医，排查更严重的问题。眼部不适时暂停佩戴隐形眼镜，不揉眼、不共用毛巾和枕头，并认真洗手。症状持续或加重时请医生评估，别借用别人开过的眼药水。
body.en:
## Establish the cause
Viruses, bacteria and allergies can cause conjunctivitis, with redness, watering, grittiness or discharge. Antibiotics do not treat viral or allergic conjunctivitis. Allergic conjunctivitis is not contagious, but appearance alone cannot establish the cause.

## Some signs need prompt assessment
Eye pain, light sensitivity or changes in vision need medical attention to rule out more serious problems. Stop wearing contact lenses while the eyes are affected. Avoid rubbing your eyes or sharing towels and pillows, and wash hands carefully. Seek assessment for persistent or worsening symptoms rather than borrowing someone else's prescribed drops.

title.zh: 打过疫苗，水痘还可能只像几个红点
title.en: After vaccination, chickenpox may look like just a few spots

summary.zh: 接种后仍可能感染，皮疹不一定有典型水疱。
summary.en: Breakthrough infection can have fewer blisters or none at all.

body.zh:
## 皮疹可能不典型
典型水痘会出现瘙痒的含液水疱，之后结痂。接种过疫苗的人仍可能发生突破性感染，通常较轻，可能只有少量红点、很少或没有水疱，发热也可能不明显。因此，不能只靠有没有水疱排除水痘。

## 告知接触史和接种史
出现可疑皮疹时，告诉家长并寻求医疗评估，就诊时说明接种记录及已知接触情况，不凭网上照片确诊。水痘对孕妇、婴儿及免疫功能较弱者可能更危险。是否返校以及需要怎样防护，应按医生、学校和当地卫生部门安排处理。
body.en:
## The rash may be less typical
Classic chickenpox causes itchy, fluid-filled blisters that later scab. Vaccinated people can still develop breakthrough infection, usually with milder illness. There may be only a few red spots, few or no blisters, and little or no fever. No blisters does not rule it out.

## Share exposure and vaccination history
Tell a parent and seek assessment for a suspicious rash. Explain vaccination records and known contact rather than diagnosing from online photographs. Chickenpox can be more serious for pregnant people, infants and those with weakened immunity. Follow clinical, school and local public-health advice about precautions and returning to class.

title.zh: 流鼻血时，头要往前倾
title.en: Lean forward during a nosebleed

summary.zh: 坐下、前倾，持续捏住鼻孔上方的柔软处。
summary.en: Sit forward and maintain pressure on the soft part above the nostrils.

body.zh:
## 保持压力，不反复松开看
流鼻血时坐下，头和身体稍向前倾，张口用嘴呼吸。用手指捏住鼻孔上方的柔软处，持续10至15分钟。不要仰头，避免血向咽喉流。计时有助于保持足够的压迫时间。

## 什么时候需要急诊
正确压迫后仍流血超过10至15分钟，或出血很多、头晕乏力、呼吸困难、头部受撞后流血，应寻求急诊帮助。经常鼻出血或正在服用影响凝血的药，也需要评估。止血后暂时避免擤鼻、抠鼻及剧烈运动，不要马上反复刺激鼻腔。
body.en:
## Keep steady pressure
Sit down, lean your head and body slightly forward, and breathe through your mouth. Pinch the soft part of the nose just above the nostrils continuously for 10–15 minutes. Do not tilt your head back and let blood run towards the throat. Use a timer rather than repeatedly releasing pressure to check.

## When urgent care is needed
Seek urgent care for bleeding beyond 10–15 minutes despite correct pressure, heavy bleeding, dizziness, breathing difficulty or bleeding after a head injury. Recurrent nosebleeds or medicines affecting clotting also need assessment. Afterwards, avoid nose-blowing, picking and strenuous activity for a while.

sources.title: NHS · Nosebleed (text reviewed 5 December 2023)

imageAlt: A small red first-aid pouch and supplies on an office desk, photographed in 2007; general first-aid context, not a nosebleed treatment demonstration.

title.zh: 崴脚后，别急着揉开
title.en: After an ankle injury, do not rush to massage it

summary.zh: 先停止活动并保护受伤部位，明显异常要及时评估。
summary.en: Stop activity, protect the injury and get concerning signs assessed.

body.zh:
## 先减少继续受伤的机会
刚扭伤时停止运动，保护受伤部位。可用毛巾包裹冰袋，单次冷敷不超过20分钟，并适当抬高。最初几天不要急着热敷或用力按摩。疼痛缓解、活动不再被疼痛阻碍后，逐步恢复轻柔活动，避免一直完全不动。

## 不能负重，不要硬走
无法负重或只能走几步、疼痛或肿胀明显加重，应就医。若肢体变形、麻木、发冷或颜色异常，需要急诊评估，不能自行认定只是扭伤。何时恢复跑跳应看恢复情况及专业建议，不以“还能忍”为标准。
body.en:
## Prevent further injury
Stop sport and protect the injured area. An ice pack wrapped in a towel can be applied for up to 20 minutes at a time; elevate the limb when possible. Avoid heat and vigorous massage in the first few days. Resume gentle movement when pain no longer prevents it, rather than remaining completely immobile.

## Do not force yourself to walk
Inability to bear weight, walking only a few steps, or worsening pain and swelling needs assessment. Deformity, numbness, coldness or abnormal colour needs emergency assessment. Do not assume it is only a sprain. Return to running and jumping should reflect recovery and professional advice.

title.zh: 能量饮料的咖啡因，也会影响睡眠
title.en: Caffeine in energy drinks can disrupt sleep

summary.zh: 咖啡因可能带来心悸、焦虑和睡眠问题。
summary.en: Caffeine can cause palpitations, anxiety and disrupted sleep.

body.zh:
## 提神不等于适合青少年
能量饮料常含咖啡因，有些也含较多糖。摄入过多咖啡因可能引起心跳加快、心悸、焦虑和睡眠问题。FDA引用的儿科建议不主张儿童和青少年饮用能量饮料，不能把面向成人的咖啡因摄入参考量直接套用。

## 别只数咖啡杯数
茶、部分汽水、巧克力及某些药品也可能含咖啡因，要把不同来源一起考虑。饮品容量和咖啡因含量差别很大，看看标签，不要只凭“喝了一瓶”估计。已经出现不适时应咨询专业人员，而不是继续叠加饮用来对抗疲劳。
body.en:
## Alertness does not establish suitability
Energy drinks often contain caffeine and sometimes substantial sugar. Too much caffeine can cause a racing heart, palpitations, anxiety and sleep problems. Paediatric advice cited by FDA discourages energy drinks for children and teens. Adult intake figures should not be treated as a teen allowance.

## Count sources beyond coffee
Tea, some soft drinks, chocolate and certain medicines also contain caffeine. Consider them together. Container size and caffeine content vary widely, so check the label rather than counting bottles alone. Discuss symptoms with a health professional instead of adding more caffeinated drinks to overcome tiredness.

title.zh: 恒牙被撞掉，先别捏牙根
title.en: A permanent tooth is knocked out: avoid touching the root

summary.zh: 及时找牙医，并正确保存整颗脱落的牙。
summary.en: Get urgent dental care and handle the whole tooth carefully.

body.zh:
## 拿牙冠，尽快就诊
整颗恒牙被撞脱，需要尽快接受牙科急诊处理。捡起时拿住露在牙龈外的白色牙冠，不摸牙根。若不能立即复位，可把牙放进装有牛奶的容器中，迅速带去就诊，不要干放着等到放学。

## 乳牙不能照此复位
被撞掉的乳牙不要塞回牙槽，以免伤到下面正在发育的恒牙。不确定是乳牙还是恒牙时，立即联系牙医指导，不要强行处理。即使牙没找到，也仍应尽快就诊，检查伤口及其他损伤。这些做法针对整颗牙脱落，不能替代现场评估。
body.en:
## Hold the crown and seek urgent care
A whole permanent tooth knocked out by injury needs urgent dental care. Pick it up by the white crown, not the root. If it cannot immediately be put back, place it in a container of milk and take it to the dentist promptly. Do not leave it dry until school finishes.

## Never replant a baby tooth
Putting a baby tooth back can harm the developing permanent tooth beneath it. If unsure which type it is, contact a dentist immediately rather than forcing it into place. Seek care even if the tooth cannot be found, so other injuries can be checked.

sources.title: NHS · Knocked-out tooth (reviewed 6 February 2025)

credit: Ivan Radic / Wikimedia Commons · CC BY 2.0

title.zh: 刷过牙，牙缝也清洁到了吗？
title.en: Does brushing reach between your teeth?

summary.zh: 牙线或牙间刷处理的是牙刷难以触及的地方。
summary.en: Floss or interdental brushes reach places a toothbrush misses.

body.zh:
## 牙菌斑不只在看得见的地方
牙菌斑是附着在牙齿表面的黏性生物膜，也会形成在牙缝里。普通刷牙难以充分清洁这些位置，牙线或合适的牙间刷可以补充清洁。已经硬化成牙结石的沉积物，则需要口腔专业人员处理，不能靠更用力刷掉。

## 轻轻滑入，不要猛压
使用牙线时轻柔地通过牙齿接触点，不要突然弹入牙龈，避免损伤。牙缝大小、是否戴矫治器等会影响工具选择，可请牙医演示适合的做法。目标是清洁牙间，而不是追求动作快或用力大。
body.en:
## Plaque forms where you cannot easily see it
Dental plaque is a sticky biofilm on tooth surfaces, including between teeth. A toothbrush does not adequately reach every space. Floss or a suitable interdental brush can supplement brushing. Hardened calculus needs professional removal; harder brushing will not remove it.

## Slide gently rather than snapping
Ease floss through the contact between teeth instead of snapping it into the gum. Space size and orthodontic appliances affect which tool is suitable. Ask a dental professional to demonstrate a method that fits your mouth. The goal is cleaning between teeth, not speed or force.

sources.title: NIDCR · Do I really need to floss? (reviewed December 2024)

credit: Alan Levine (cogdogblog) / Wikimedia Commons · CC BY 2.0
imageAlt: A dental-floss container beside a pair of 3D glasses on a wooden surface, photographed in 2010; an everyday object still life.

title.zh: 打鼾很响，就代表睡得香吗？
title.en: Does loud snoring mean sound sleep?

summary.zh: 反复呼吸暂停、憋醒和白天困倦，值得告诉医生。
summary.en: Breathing pauses, gasping and daytime sleepiness deserve assessment.

body.zh:
## 留意有没有呼吸中断
睡眠呼吸暂停可能表现为频繁大声打鼾、呼吸反复停止又恢复，或睡中喘气。本人可能不知道，往往是家人先发现。白天嗜睡、疲劳和注意力困难，也可能是线索，但打鼾本身不能确诊。

## 上课走神，不一定只是没努力
儿童可能表现为过度活跃、注意力问题或尿床，并非都一副困倦的样子。如果这些变化伴随明显打鼾或呼吸异常，应向医生说明。诊断有时需要睡眠监测，不能只凭一段手机录音决定，也不要自行购买设备代替评估。
body.en:
## Notice pauses in breathing
Sleep apnoea may involve frequent loud snoring, breathing that repeatedly stops and starts, or gasping during sleep. A family member may notice before the sleeper does. Daytime sleepiness, fatigue and difficulty concentrating can be clues, but snoring alone does not establish the diagnosis.

## Children may not simply look sleepy
Children can show overactivity, attention problems or bedwetting. Discuss these changes with a clinician when they accompany loud snoring or abnormal breathing. Diagnosis may require a sleep study. A phone recording alone is not enough to diagnose it, and buying equipment should not replace assessment.
