imageAlt: A person resting their head on folded arms at a desk, photographed in 2009; sleep context only, with no sleep-apnoea diagnosis inferred.

title.zh: 怀疑乳糜泻，检查前别急着戒麸质
title.en: Suspect coeliac disease? Discuss testing before cutting gluten

summary.zh: 提前改变饮食，可能影响诊断结果。
summary.en: Changing your diet beforehand can affect diagnostic results.

body.zh:
## 症状相似，病因可能不同
乳糜泻的部分症状与其他消化系统问题相似，不能凭腹胀、腹泻或吃面食后的感觉确诊。医生会结合病史、家族史和检查，通常可能涉及血液检测及小肠活检，而不是只看一份食物记录。

## 饮食改变会改变线索
在诊断检查前自行开始无麸质饮食，可能影响结果。怀疑时先与医生商量检查安排；已经戒麸质的人，也应如实说明，不自行重新大量进食来“测试”。有确诊亲属或其他相关风险时，可以咨询是否需要评估，不必靠尝试各种忌口寻找答案。
body.en:
## Similar symptoms can have different causes
Coeliac disease can resemble other digestive conditions. Bloating, diarrhoea or how you feel after bread cannot establish a diagnosis. Clinicians consider symptoms, medical and family history and tests, often including blood tests and small-intestinal biopsies.

## Diet changes can alter the evidence
Starting a gluten-free diet before diagnostic testing may affect results. Discuss testing before changing your diet. If already avoiding gluten, say so; do not start a large gluten challenge yourself. A diagnosed relative or other relevant risk may warrant discussing assessment rather than trying successive restrictions on your own.

sources.title: NIDDK · Diagnosis of celiac disease (reviewed October 2020)

imageAlt: Wheat grains on a white plate against a dark surface, photographed in 2011; a gluten-containing grain, not a gluten-free food recommendation.

title.zh: 登革热退烧了，也要留意身体变化
title.en: With dengue, watch symptoms even after the fever falls

summary.zh: 严重腹痛、持续呕吐或出血，需要立即求助。
summary.en: Severe abdominal pain, persistent vomiting or bleeding needs immediate care.

body.zh:
## 体温下降不一定代表脱离风险
登革热经受感染蚊虫叮咬传播，可引起发热、头痛、肌肉关节痛或皮疹。重症警示表现有时在退热后出现，包括严重腹痛、持续呕吐、呼吸急促、鼻牙龈出血或呕吐物、粪便带血，需要立即就医。

## 告诉医生旅行和活动情况
在有传播风险的地区活动后发热，应说明去过哪里及何时开始不适，不靠症状自行确诊。怀疑登革热时，不自行用阿司匹林或布洛芬退热，以免增加出血风险，应咨询医生。白天也要防蚊，减少住处周围积水。
body.en:
## A lower temperature does not settle the risk
Dengue spreads through infected mosquitoes and can cause fever, headache, body aches or rash. Severe warning signs may appear after fever falls: severe abdominal pain, persistent vomiting, rapid breathing, bleeding gums or nose, or blood in vomit or stool. These need immediate care.

## Explain travel and exposure
Tell the clinician where you have been and when illness began. Symptoms alone cannot confirm dengue. If dengue is suspected, avoid self-treating with aspirin or ibuprofen because they can increase bleeding risk; seek advice. Prevent mosquito bites during the day too and remove standing water nearby.

sources.title: WHO · Dengue (21 August 2025)

credit: James Gathany / CDC PHIL #8932 · Public domain
imageAlt: Genuine close-up of a female Aedes aegypti feeding on skin; mosquito-vector context, not proof of dengue infection in the mosquito or host.

title.zh: 感染后突然很不对劲，为什么不能只等退烧？
title.en: Why not just wait for a fever to settle when infection worsens?

summary.zh: 认识脓毒症：感染引起的失控反应可能损害器官。
summary.en: Sepsis is an extreme response to infection that can damage organs.

body.zh:
## 不只是体温高
脓毒症是身体对感染出现极端反应、引起器官功能障碍的危急状态。可能出现意识混乱、呼吸困难、极度不适、皮肤湿冷或尿量减少；体温可能高，也可能低。不能单靠体温正常就放心。

## 病情迅速恶化要立即求助
感染期间出现这些明显变化，或感觉情况在快速恶化，应立即寻求医疗帮助，不等待症状凑齐，也不自行加抗生素处理。就诊时说明近期感染、症状变化和正在用的药。症状表不能在家确诊脓毒症，但可以提醒我们及时行动。
body.en:
## More than a high temperature
Sepsis is a life-threatening extreme response to infection that causes organ dysfunction. Confusion, breathing difficulty, extreme discomfort, clammy skin or reduced urine can occur. Temperature may be high or low; a normal reading alone is not reassuring.

## Rapid deterioration needs immediate help
Seek medical help immediately for these marked changes during infection or rapid worsening. Do not wait for every sign or increase antibiotics yourself. Explain recent infection, symptom changes and medicines being taken. A symptom list cannot diagnose sepsis at home, but it can prompt timely action.

sources.title: WHO · Sepsis (3 May 2024)

credit: S. Ombelet, B. Barbé, D. Affolabi, J. B. Ronat, P. Lompo, O. Lunguya, J. Jacobs and L. Hardy / Wikimedia Commons · CC BY 4.0
imageAlt: Published photographic plate showing pellicle, gas, turbidity and puff-ball growth patterns in blood culture bottles; not a rendering or an individual sepsis diagnosis.

title.zh: 怀疑脑膜炎，别等皮疹出现
title.en: Suspect meningitis? Do not wait for a rash

summary.zh: 严重头痛、颈部僵硬和意识变化，需要认真对待。
summary.en: Severe headache, neck stiffness and altered awareness need urgent attention.

body.zh:
## 开始可能像流感
脑膜炎球菌感染可引起脑膜炎或严重血流感染，早期可能像流感，但病情可在数小时内明显加重。高热、严重头痛、颈部僵硬、意识混乱或难以唤醒，都是需要立即求助的表现，不能只当作普通感冒。

## 没出疹也不能排除
压迫后不褪色的皮疹是危险信号，但它可能较晚出现，也可能不出现。不要等出疹或所有症状齐全才就医。怀疑严重感染、病情快速恶化时立即寻求急救。疫苗能预防部分相关病原体，但接种过也不能忽视可疑症状。
body.en:
## It may start like flu
Meningococcal infection can cause meningitis or serious bloodstream infection. Early illness may resemble flu, yet worsen substantially within hours. High fever, severe headache, neck stiffness, confusion or difficulty waking needs immediate help rather than treatment as an ordinary cold.

## A rash is not always present
A rash that does not fade under pressure is dangerous, but may develop late or not at all. Do not wait for a rash or a complete checklist. Rapid deterioration or suspected serious infection needs emergency care. Vaccination protects against some relevant organisms, but does not remove the need to respond to concerning symptoms.

sources.title: UKHSA · MenACWY leaflet (July 2024), signs and symptoms, pages 4–6

credit: Amanda Mills / CDC PHIL #13549 · Public domain
imageAlt: An electronic oral thermometer on a reflective surface, displaying 98.0 degrees Fahrenheit. General symptom-monitoring context, not evidence of fever or meningitis.

title.zh: 查结核，为什么拍片之外还可能要留痰？
title.en: Why might TB assessment need sputum as well as an X-ray?

summary.zh: 影像看肺部变化，实验室检查寻找病原体等证据。
summary.en: Imaging shows lung changes; laboratory tests look for further evidence.

body.zh:
## 不同检查回答不同问题
胸部影像帮助医生查看肺部可疑变化；痰标本的实验室检查则可寻找结核分枝杆菌的证据，部分检查还帮助了解耐药情况。它们并非简单重复。评估还需结合症状、接触史和其他结果，不能只拿一张片子自行下结论。

## 按要求留取标本
医生安排痰检查时，应了解具体留取方法、时间和送检要求，不自行减少或取消。痰是从呼吸道咳出的分泌物，不是单纯唾液；不容易咳出时告诉医务人员，寻求合适的方法。检查组合及是否需要重复，应由接诊机构根据情况决定。
body.en:
## Different tests answer different questions
Chest imaging helps clinicians examine suspicious lung changes. Laboratory testing of sputum looks for evidence of TB bacteria; some tests also inform drug resistance. These are not simply duplicates. Symptoms, exposure history and other findings matter too, so do not interpret an image in isolation.

## Follow collection instructions
Ask about collection method, timing and transport rather than reducing or cancelling requested samples yourself. Sputum is material coughed up from the airways, not just saliva. Tell staff if you cannot produce it so they can arrange an appropriate approach. The clinic decides which tests and repeat samples are needed.

sources.title: CDC · Diagnosing tuberculosis (17 January 2025)

credit: Dilyara Nabirova / CDC PHIL #19651 · Public domain
imageAlt: Outdoor sputum-collection enclosure and a protected staff member at a tuberculosis dispensary in Bishkek; documented diagnostic context, with no individual result inferred.

title.zh: 撞到头没昏倒，也可能是脑震荡
title.en: A concussion can happen without passing out

summary.zh: 受撞后头痛、发懵或平衡异常，先离场再评估。
summary.en: Headache, fogginess or balance trouble after a hit means stopping for assessment.

body.zh:
## 不只看有没有失去意识
头部受撞，或身体受撞导致头和脑快速晃动，都可能引起脑震荡。表现可包括头痛、恶心、头晕、反应变慢或记不清事情；有些症状会延后出现。没有昏倒，不能据此排除。

## 当天不要自行重返比赛
怀疑脑震荡就停止运动，告诉教练和家长，接受医疗评估，不让队友决定能否继续。即使感觉好些，当天也不应自行返场。头痛持续加重、反复呕吐、抽搐或难以唤醒，需要立即急救；恢复运动应遵循专业安排。
body.en:
## Loss of consciousness is not required
A head impact, or a body impact that rapidly moves the head and brain, can cause concussion. Headache, nausea, dizziness, slow responses or memory trouble may follow. Some symptoms appear later. Not passing out does not rule it out.

## Do not return to play that day
Stop sport when concussion is suspected, tell the coach and a parent, and get assessed. Teammates should not decide whether you can continue. Feeling better does not justify a same-day return. Worsening persistent headache, repeated vomiting, seizures or difficulty waking needs emergency help. Follow professional advice for returning to sport.

sources.title: CDC HEADS UP · Fact sheet for youth sports coaches (revised August 2019)

credit: Wutthichai Charoenburi / Wikimedia Commons · CC BY 2.0
imageAlt: A real association-football ball resting on grass; generic sports context for concussion education, not evidence of an injury or a safe-return-to-play assessment.

title.zh: 户外时间和近视，不能简单理解成“看远就治好”
title.en: Outdoor time is not a cure for existing myopia

summary.zh: 减少新发近视风险，与逆转已经发生的近视不同。
summary.en: Lowering the chance of onset differs from reversing established myopia.

body.zh:
## 有关的是近视发生风险
近视时，眼睛的光学成像使远处物体模糊。NEI介绍的研究发现，户外时间较多的儿童更不容易开始近视，但原因仍在研究中。这不能直接解释为只要看远处，就能把已经发生的近视恢复。

## 已经近视，也需要专业管理
户外活动不替代验光、合适的视力矫正及后续评估，也不能用“多出去玩”作为停戴眼镜的理由。给孩子留出户外时间时，同时注意防晒和活动安全。看到远处模糊，应告诉家长并接受检查，而不是等待视力自行恢复。
body.en:
## The evidence concerns onset
Myopia makes distant objects look blurred because of how light focuses in the eye. Research described by NEI found that children spending more time outdoors were less likely to become myopic, though the mechanism remained under study. This does not mean looking into the distance reverses existing myopia.

## Existing myopia still needs care
Outdoor time does not replace assessment, appropriate vision correction or follow-up, and is not a reason to stop wearing prescribed glasses. Make room for outdoor activity with sun protection and safe play. Tell a parent about blurred distance vision and arrange an eye assessment rather than waiting for it to disappear.

sources.title: NEI · Myopia: a close look at efforts to turn back a growing problem (3 October 2017), outdoor-time research

credit: Adam Jones / Wikimedia Commons · CC BY 2.0
imageAlt: Children playing outdoors around a tree in daylight in San Cristobal de las Casas, Mexico; not a diagnosis, measured light exposure or demonstration of a prescribed activity.

title.zh: 腹泻、喝不下水时，用止痛药要多问一句
title.en: Dehydrated and reaching for pain relief? Ask first

summary.zh: 部分止痛药在脱水或低血压时会增加肾损伤风险。
summary.en: Some pain medicines carry additional kidney risk during dehydration or low blood pressure.

body.zh:
## 同一种药，身体状态会影响风险
布洛芬、萘普生等属于非甾体抗炎药（NSAIDs）。这类药在长期使用时可能损害肾脏，脱水或血压较低时使用也可能导致急性肾损伤。腹泻、呕吐或喝不下水时，不宜只按平时的经验自行用药。

## 把所有药带进咨询
向医生或药师说明已有肾病、正在服用的降压药及其他药品。有些感冒药也含NSAIDs，不能只凭品牌不同认为成分不同。生病时是否需要调整处方药、何时恢复，应提前问清，不要自行停药或加量。
body.en:
## Your condition changes the risk
Ibuprofen and naproxen are nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, or NSAIDs. Long-term use can harm kidneys, and taking them while dehydrated or with low blood pressure can cause acute kidney injury. Vomiting, diarrhoea or difficulty drinking changes the situation from your usual experience.

## Include every medicine in the discussion
Tell a clinician or pharmacist about kidney disease, blood-pressure medicines and other products. Some cold remedies contain NSAIDs too; different brands do not guarantee different ingredients. Ask whether prescriptions need adjustment during illness and when to restart any paused treatment. Do not stop medicines or increase doses independently.

sources.title: NIDDK · Keeping kidneys safe: smart choices about medicines (reviewed June 2018)

credit: Alabama Extension / ACES, Devontae Lindsey / Wikimedia Commons · CC0 1.0
imageAlt: A plastic drinking-water bottle with a green cap; generic hydration context, not a kidney scan, NSAID safety claim, prescribed fluid intake or brand endorsement.

title.zh: 酒精的风险，不只发生在喝醉之后
title.en: Alcohol risks do not begin only with drunkenness

summary.zh: 低度酒同样含乙醇，清醒感也不是安全证明。
summary.en: Low-strength drinks still contain ethanol; feeling sober does not establish safety.

body.zh:
## 酒精不是普通饮料成分
酒精饮品中的乙醇具有精神活性、毒性和成瘾风险。饮酒与肝脏疾病、某些癌症及交通伤害等有关。WHO指出，没有完全无风险的饮酒方式；风险还受饮用量、频率、年龄、健康状况和所处环境影响。

## 别把“没醉”当作保护
果味、低度或包装像汽水，不会让饮品里的乙醇失去风险。是否感觉醉了，也不能概括长期健康影响。不要为了所谓养生而开始饮酒，尤其不要把成人的饮酒习惯当作青少年社交的要求。聚会里选择不喝酒，不需要用健康理由反复辩解。
body.en:
## Ethanol is not an ordinary drink ingredient
Ethanol is psychoactive, toxic and can cause dependence. Drinking is linked to liver disease, some cancers and injuries, including traffic injuries. WHO identifies no risk-free drinking pattern. Amount, frequency, age, health and context affect risk.

## Feeling sober is not protection
Fruit flavour, low strength or soft-drink-like packaging does not remove ethanol's risks. How drunk you feel does not capture long-term health effects. Do not start drinking for a supposed health benefit, or turn adult drinking habits into an expectation for teenagers. Choosing an alcohol-free drink at a gathering does not require repeated justification.

sources.title: WHO · Alcohol (28 June 2024)

credit: Steph Laing / Wikimedia Commons · CC BY 2.0
imageAlt: Two branded glasses containing beer on a table; neutral alcohol-exposure context, not a recommended serving size, consumption recommendation or endorsement.

title.zh: 痛经让你反复请假，不必一直忍着
title.en: Period pain repeatedly keeping you out of class deserves care

summary.zh: 影响日常生活的疼痛，需要评估，也可能有可治疗的原因。
summary.en: Pain that disrupts daily life needs assessment and may have treatable causes.

body.zh:
## 疼痛严重，值得被认真听见
子宫内膜异位症是类似子宫内膜的组织出现在其他部位，可引起严重痛经、盆腔痛及其他不适。它可能从青春期开始影响生活，但不是所有痛经都是这个病。疼痛已经妨碍上课、睡眠或日常活动时，应寻求评估。

## 就诊时说明影响了什么
告诉医生疼痛与月经的关系、持续多久，以及是否伴排便排尿疼痛或经量变化。诊断可能需要不同检查，不能只靠一条症状判断。治疗有药物等不同选择，需要结合个人情况讨论；不必等到无法忍受才求助，也不要自行照搬别人的激素治疗。
body.en:
## Severe pain deserves attention
Endometriosis involves tissue similar to the womb lining growing elsewhere. It can cause severe period pain, pelvic pain and other symptoms, sometimes beginning in adolescence. Not every painful period is endometriosis. Pain interfering with class, sleep or daily activities warrants assessment.

## Explain what the pain disrupts
Describe its timing relative to periods, duration, changes in bleeding and any pain passing urine or stools. Diagnosis may require several investigations; a single symptom cannot confirm it. Medicines and other treatments depend on individual circumstances. You need not wait until pain is unbearable, and should not copy someone else's hormonal treatment.

sources.title: NHS · Endometriosis (reviewed 27 August 2024)

credit: MIKI Yoshihito / Wikimedia Commons · CC BY 2.0
imageAlt: Plastic hot-water bottles displayed in a shop, with a retail sign; generic comfort-object context, not a diagnosis, heat-use demonstration or treatment endorsement.

title.zh: 药品放哪里，也要看说明书
title.en: Where you store a medicine matters too

summary.zh: 避光、防潮或冷藏要求，不能只凭习惯判断。
summary.en: Light, moisture and refrigeration instructions should guide storage.

body.zh:
## 每种药的要求可能不同
存药时先看包装和说明书，保留清晰标签，把药放在儿童看不到、拿不到的地方。需要避光、防热和防潮的药，不适合随手放在阳光直射处或潮湿位置。不要把不同药片混在没有标识的小瓶里，以免失去辨认和使用信息。

## 冷藏药离开冰箱后，先问再用
需要冷藏的药应按具体要求保存。若冰箱故障或药物在外放置了一段时间，记录情况并联系药师或供药机构确认，不要仅凭外观或尚未过期就继续使用。不同药物耐受情况不同，也不能自行认为重新放回冰箱就恢复正常。
body.en:
## Requirements differ between medicines
Read the packaging and leaflet, retain clear labels and keep medicines out of children's sight and reach. Products needing protection from light, heat and moisture should not be left in direct sun or damp places. Avoid mixing unlabelled tablets and losing identification and instructions.

## Ask after a refrigeration problem
Follow the specific instructions for refrigerated medicines. If the fridge fails or medicine is left outside it, record what happened and ask the pharmacist or supplier before using it. Appearance or an unexpired date cannot settle the question. Returning it to the fridge does not automatically establish that it is safe.

sources.title: Kingston and Richmond NHS Trust · Controlled drugs (21 December 2024), general safe-storage principles
University Hospitals of Morecambe Bay NHS Trust · Homecare medicines service (13 August 2024), refrigerator storage

imageAlt: A weekly pill organizer with tablets and capsules; medicine-handling still life, not proof of suitable temperature, humidity, child resistance or safe repackaging.

title.zh: 剩饭再炒热，也不能补救所有储存问题
title.en: Reheating rice cannot fix every storage problem

summary.zh: 有些细菌的芽孢和毒素，比想象中更耐热。
summary.en: Some bacterial spores and toxins withstand heat.

body.zh:
## 问题可能在炒饭之前
蜡样芽孢杆菌的芽孢可能在煮饭后存活。熟饭长时间放在室温下，芽孢可以萌发，细菌繁殖并产生毒素，其中有耐热毒素。再把饭炒得很烫，并不能保证把此前产生的风险全部消除。

## 关键是别给细菌繁殖的时间
不马上吃的熟饭要尽快冷却并妥善冷藏，避免整锅在室温下放很久；需要持续热存时，也要保持安全温度。不要把“之后会再加热”当成随意存放的理由。无法确定之前储存是否安全的饭，不值得用尝一口来判断。
body.en:
## The problem may start before frying
Bacillus cereus spores can survive cooking. When cooked rice stays at room temperature too long, spores can germinate and bacteria multiply and produce toxins, including heat-stable toxin. Frying the rice until hot does not guarantee removal of hazards that developed earlier.

## Limit time for growth
Cool rice promptly and refrigerate it properly when it will not be eaten immediately. Avoid leaving a whole pot at room temperature for hours. Food kept hot also needs a safe holding temperature. Planned reheating is not permission for careless storage. Do not taste rice to establish whether uncertain storage was safe.

sources.title: Hong Kong CFS · Food Safety Focus 192: Bacillus cereus in fried rice (July 2022), page 4

credit: Biyu Lau / Wikimedia Commons · CC BY 2.0
imageAlt: Plates of American-style fried rice with accompaniments at MBK Center in Bangkok, photographed in 2009; food context, not evidence of leftovers, bacterial contamination or toxin.

title.zh: 野蘑菇能不能吃，别凭照片决定
title.en: Do not decide whether a wild mushroom is edible from a photo

summary.zh: 长得相似、煮过或买来的，都不能单独保证安全。
summary.en: Similarity, cooking or purchase alone cannot establish safety.

body.zh:
## 可食用和有毒种类可能混在一起
野生蘑菇不易辨认，可食用和有毒种类可能相似，也可能混在同一包产品里。部分毒素在烹煮后仍会造成伤害。因此，不要采摘野蘑菇食用，也不要依赖识图软件、网上对照图或“煮熟就行”的经验。

## 出现不适，留下线索并就医
从可靠供应商购买，不吃混有不明种类的菇类。食用后出现恶心、呕吐、腹痛、头晕等不适，怀疑中毒时应立即就医；有剩余食物或包装，可安全保留供识别。不要因为别人吃后暂时没事，就认定自己也没有风险。
body.en:
## Edible and poisonous species can be mixed
Wild mushrooms are difficult to identify. Edible and poisonous kinds can resemble each other or appear together in one package. Some toxins remain harmful after cooking. Do not collect wild mushrooms to eat or rely on identification apps, online pictures or cooking alone.

## Keep useful evidence and seek care
Buy from reliable suppliers and avoid products mixed with unidentified species. Nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain or dizziness after eating mushrooms warrants immediate assessment when poisoning is suspected. Safely retain leftovers or packaging for identification. Someone else feeling well for now does not establish your safety.

sources.title: Hong Kong CHP · Mushroom-poisoning warning and public advice (15 April 2024)

credit: Charlie Marshall / Wikimedia Commons · CC BY 2.0
imageAlt: Wild mushrooms growing on a mossy log, photographed in 2020; no species, toxicity or edibility identification is made.

title.zh: 游泳后耳朵疼，别用棉签往里掏
title.en: Ear pain after swimming? Do not reach inside with a cotton bud

summary.zh: 外耳道长时间潮湿，可能给细菌提供生长条件。
summary.en: Trapped moisture can allow bacteria to multiply in the outer ear canal.

body.zh:
## “游泳耳”不是中耳炎
水长时间留在外耳道，可破坏耳垢和皮肤的保护作用，形成利于细菌繁殖的潮湿环境，导致急性外耳道炎，也叫游泳耳。可能出现耳内瘙痒、疼痛、红肿或流液。它与中耳感染不同，也不是人人游泳后都会发生。

## 排水、擦干外部，不伸工具进去
游泳或淋浴后让头向两侧倾斜，帮助水流出，用毛巾擦干外耳。不要把棉签等物品伸进耳道，也不要刻意把耳垢全部清掉。耳痛或流液应咨询医生；干耳滴液并非人人适用，尤其鼓膜穿孔、置管或已有流液时不要自行使用。
body.en:
## Swimmer's ear differs from a middle-ear infection
Water trapped in the outer ear canal can damage protective wax and skin, creating conditions for bacterial growth. The resulting infection may cause itching, pain, redness or drainage. It is not the same as a middle-ear infection, and does not happen after every swim.

## Drain and dry without inserting objects
Tilt your head to let water drain and towel-dry the outer ear. Do not insert cotton buds or remove all earwax. Ask a clinician about pain or drainage. Ear-drying drops are not suitable for everyone, particularly with a perforated eardrum, ear tubes or drainage.

sources.title: CDC · Preventing swimmer's ear (28 May 2025)

imageAlt: An outdoor public swimming pool with lane ropes and starting blocks in Santa Clara, California, photographed in 2012; swimming context without any inference about ear infection or water quality.

title.zh: 戴隐形眼镜游泳，自来水冲一下也不算消毒
title.en: Water is not disinfectant for contact lenses

summary.zh: 泳池水和自来水都不适合接触或保存镜片。
summary.en: Pool water and tap water should not be used with lenses.

body.zh:
## 看起来干净的水，也不是无菌的
自来水、湖水等可能含有伤害眼睛的微生物，包括棘阿米巴。水接触软性隐形眼镜还可能使镜片变形、黏附眼表，增加角膜损伤和感染机会。洗澡、游泳前应取下镜片，而不是认为戴着泳镜就可以忽略风险。

## 镜片和镜盒都要用合适护理液
不要用水冲洗或保存镜片。镜片不慎接触水后应尽快取下，根据镜片类型丢弃，或按护理要求清洁并消毒后再使用。处理前洗净双手，镜盒按要求使用护理液清洁。有水上活动视力需求时，可咨询适合的有度数泳镜。
body.en:
## Clear water is not sterile
Tap and lake water can contain organisms harmful to eyes, including Acanthamoeba. Water can also make soft lenses change shape and stick to the eye, increasing corneal injury and infection risk. Remove lenses before showering or swimming; goggles are not a reason to disregard the risk.

## Use suitable lens-care solution
Never rinse or store lenses in water. After water exposure, remove them promptly and discard them or clean and disinfect them as appropriate for the lens type. Wash hands before handling lenses and clean the case with the recommended solution. Prescription swimming goggles may be an alternative for water activities.

sources.title: CDC · Healthy habits: keeping water away from contact lenses (27 May 2025)

credit: Amanda Mills / CDC PHIL #13556 · Public domain
imageAlt: An open contact-lens case with lenses in its two wells, CDC archive, 2011; the source describes storage solution, not tap water.

title.zh: 听到雷声，户外活动就该暂停
title.en: Hearing thunder is a reason to stop outdoor activity

summary.zh: 不要等雨下大了，才开始寻找安全遮蔽处。
summary.en: Do not wait for heavy rain before moving to safe shelter.

body.zh:
## 有雷声，就已有雷击风险
听得到雷声，通常意味着已在可能遭雷击的范围内。外出前查看天气预报，雷暴将至时提前调整活动，给转移留出时间。足球场、步道或水边都不适合为了完成行程而继续逗留。

## 大树不是安全避雷处
尽快进入坚固建筑物或硬顶汽车，不要躲在孤立高树下，也不要靠近周围最高的物体。进入室内后仍应避免使用有线电话、接触插电设备和水管设施，不在雷暴期间洗澡。保护自己比拍摄闪电或等同伴集合完再走更重要。
body.en:
## Thunder means lightning is within range
If you can hear thunder, you are within possible striking distance. Check forecasts and change plans before a storm, allowing time to move. A pitch, trail or waterside is not somewhere to linger simply to finish an activity.

## A tall tree is not safe shelter
Move into a sturdy building or hard-topped vehicle. Do not shelter beneath an isolated tall tree or stay beside the tallest nearby object. Indoors, avoid corded phones, plugged-in equipment and plumbing, including showers. Prioritise moving to safety over filming lightning or waiting to complete a group activity.

sources.title: US National Weather Service, Phoenix · Spotter newsletter (June 2024), lightning safety, page 9

imageAlt: Branching lightning against a dark thunderstorm sky in Germany, photographed in 2017 with a 30-second exposure; not a current local weather report or demonstration of a safe outdoor viewing position.

title.zh: 晕车时刷手机，为什么可能更难受？
title.en: Why can scrolling make motion sickness worse?

summary.zh: 眼睛和内耳传来的运动信息，可能互相矛盾。
summary.en: Your eyes and inner ear can send conflicting movement signals.

body.zh:
## 大脑收到的信息不一致
乘车、船或飞机时，内耳感知的运动可能与眼睛看到的不同，引起头晕、恶心、出汗或面色苍白。低头读书、看视频或刷手机可能让不适加重，不是意志力不够的问题。

## 先把视线从屏幕移开
向前看相对固定的远处，例如地平线；也可以闭眼缓慢呼吸，条件允许时获得新鲜空气，长途行程安排休息。出发前避免过饱。晕车药的年龄限制和使用方法各不相同，尤其给孩子用时应先问药师，不照搬成人方案。
body.en:
## The brain receives conflicting information
During travel, movement sensed by the inner ear may differ from what the eyes see. This can cause dizziness, nausea, sweating or pallor. Reading, videos and scrolling may worsen symptoms. It is not a failure of willpower.

## Move your attention away from the screen
Look ahead at a fixed distant point, such as the horizon, or close your eyes and breathe slowly. Get fresh air when possible and break up long journeys. Avoid a heavy meal beforehand. Motion-sickness medicines have different age restrictions and instructions; ask a pharmacist, especially for children, rather than copying an adult plan.

sources.title: NHS · Motion sickness (reviewed 19 June 2023)

imageAlt: Clouds and snow-covered mountains in the Otztal Alps seen from an airplane window in 2017; air-travel context, not evidence of motion sickness, turbulence or a treatment technique.

title.zh: 营养标签写“每份”，不一定指整包
title.en: One serving on a label may not mean the whole package

summary.zh: 先确认标签的计算单位，再看实际吃了多少。
summary.en: Check the labelled quantity before calculating what you consumed.

body.zh:
## 同一个数字，单位不同意思就不同
营养信息可能按每份、每100克或每100毫升列出。比较两个产品时，要把数量基础统一，不能直接把不同份量的数值放在一起。标签上的“每份”也不自动等于你一次应该吃的量。

## 用一个假设例子算整瓶
如果某饮品标明每100毫升含钠120毫克，一瓶500毫升喝完，钠摄入量就是600毫克。若只喝一半，再按实际饮用量计算。这个例子只说明换算方法，不对应具体产品，也不是摄入量建议。看清单位，比只盯着一个醒目的数字更有用。
body.en:
## Check what the number refers to
Nutrition information may be shown per serving, per 100 grams or per 100 millilitres. Use the same quantity when comparing products. A labelled serving is not automatically a recommendation for how much you should eat.

## Calculate the whole bottle
In a hypothetical example, a drink contains 120 milligrams of sodium per 100 millilitres. Finishing a 500-millilitre bottle provides 600 milligrams. If you drink half, calculate for that amount. This demonstrates arithmetic, not a real product or an intake recommendation. Understanding the quantity matters more than reading one prominent number alone.

sources.title: FDA · Using the Nutrition Facts label (February 2020), serving-size arithmetic, pages 3–4

imageAlt: A photographed U.S. Nutrition Facts panel on confectionery packaging, showing serving size and per-serving values, 2014; a historical packaging example rather than a current universal label format.

title.zh: 旅行后起了痒包，就一定是臭虫吗？
title.en: Do itchy marks after a trip prove bed bugs?

summary.zh: 咬痕相似，要结合床垫、行李等处的线索判断。
summary.en: Bite marks overlap with other causes; look for environmental clues.

body.zh:
## 不能只凭咬痕认虫
臭虫叮咬可引起瘙痒、睡眠受影响，外观可能像蚊虫或跳蚤叮咬，部分人甚至没有明显痕迹。它们目前不被认为会传播人类疾病，但也不代表可以忽略。是否有臭虫，并不能用酒店档次或表面整洁程度判断。

## 找证据，别盲目喷药
检查床垫接缝、床架及行李缝隙，留意虫体、蜕皮和锈色血点。它们可能随行李和衣物转移。怀疑有虫害时，联系有经验的专业防治人员，不仅凭皮肤照片自行大量喷杀虫剂。叮咬后严重肿胀或怀疑过敏，应就医评估。
body.en:
## Bite marks do not identify the insect
Bed bugs can cause itching and lost sleep. Marks may resemble mosquito or flea bites, and some people show none. They are not known to spread human diseases, but still need attention. Hotel rating or apparent cleanliness does not establish their absence.

## Look for evidence, not just a spray
Check mattress seams, bed frames and luggage folds for bugs, shed skins or rusty blood spots. Bugs can travel with bags and clothing. Contact experienced pest-control professionals if infestation is suspected rather than spraying extensively based on skin photographs. Seek assessment for severe swelling or a suspected allergic reaction.

sources.title: CDC · About bed bugs (26 April 2024)

credit: World Health Organization / CDC PHIL #6283 · Public domain
imageAlt: A genuine close-up photograph of a common bed bug, Cimex lectularius, on human skin, CDC/WHO archive, 1976; not a bat bug, kissing bug, bite-diagnosis image or current infestation report.

title.zh: 甲肝和乙肝，不能套用同一套传播印象
title.en: Hepatitis A and B do not share the same transmission pattern

summary.zh: 甲肝主要经粪口途径传播，饮食和手卫生很重要。
summary.en: Hepatitis A spreads through the faecal–oral route, making food and hand hygiene important.

body.zh:
## 都伤肝，但病原体和途径不同
甲型肝炎由甲肝病毒引起，主要通过吞入被感染者粪便污染的食物、水等传播，污染量很少也可能感染。它与主要经血液和某些体液传播的乙肝不同，不能把一种肝炎的传播知识直接套用到另一种。

## 没有黄疸，也不能只凭外观排除
感染可出现乏力、食欲下降、恶心、深色尿或眼睛皮肤发黄，也可能没有明显症状。出现可疑表现或已知接触时应咨询医生。认真洗手、注意食品和饮水卫生，并按当地安排核查甲肝疫苗接种情况；不要仅凭气色判断谁有感染。
body.en:
## Different viruses, different routes
Hepatitis A mainly spreads when someone ingests microscopic amounts of faecal contamination, including in food or water. Hepatitis B mainly involves infected blood and certain body fluids. Knowledge about one should not simply be applied to the other.

## Appearance cannot exclude infection
Fatigue, poor appetite, nausea, dark urine or yellowing eyes and skin can occur, but infection may have no obvious symptoms. Seek advice for concerning symptoms or known exposure. Careful handwashing, food and water hygiene, and reviewing hepatitis A vaccination under local guidance matter. A person's appearance cannot establish infection status.

sources.title: CDC · The ABCs of hepatitis (updated 2016), transmission, symptoms and prevention

credit: Amanda Mills / CDC PHIL #13579 · Public domain
imageAlt: Hands washing a green bell pepper under running tap water before food preparation; food-hygiene context, not proof of hepatitis A infection, decontamination efficacy or a society activity.

title.zh: 伤寒不是“受凉”，持续发热要查原因
title.en: Typhoid is an infection, not the result of getting cold

summary.zh: 伤寒沙门菌可经污染的食物和水进入人体。
summary.en: Salmonella Typhi can enter the body through contaminated food or water.

body.zh:
## 名称不能代替病因
伤寒由伤寒沙门菌引起，通常通过受污染的食物或水传播。可出现持续高热、乏力、头痛、腹痛，也可能便秘或腹泻，并不是吹风受凉造成的。症状与其他疾病可能重叠，需要医疗检查确认。

## 旅行后发热，说明去过哪里
持续发热应及时就医，并告诉医生近期出行、饮食饮水情况。伤寒可以用抗生素治疗，但耐药性会影响选择，不能自行吃剩药。安全饮水、食物卫生和如厕后洗手有助预防；前往有风险地区前，可咨询旅行门诊是否需要接种及其他防护。
body.en:
## The name does not explain the cause
Typhoid is caused by Salmonella Typhi, usually spread through contaminated food or water. Prolonged fever, fatigue, headache and abdominal pain may occur, with constipation or diarrhoea. Cold air does not cause it. Symptoms overlap with other illnesses, so medical testing is needed.

## Explain travel after a persistent fever
Seek care and describe recent travel, food and drinking-water exposure. Antibiotics can treat typhoid, but resistance affects selection; do not use leftover treatment yourself. Safe water, food hygiene and handwashing after the toilet help prevention. Before travel to a risk area, discuss vaccination and other precautions with a travel clinic.

sources.title: WHO · Typhoid (30 March 2023)

credit: Alabama Extension / ACES, Margaret Barse / Wikimedia Commons · CC0 1.0
imageAlt: A glass of water with a pitcher in the background. General drinking-water context, not a Salmonella image, contamination finding or verification that the water is safe to drink.

title.zh: 被蛇咬后，不要切伤口、吸毒或扎紧止血带
title.en: After a snakebite, do not cut, suck or tightly tourniquet the wound

summary.zh: 减少活动，尽快获得医疗救助，别让偏方拖延治疗。
summary.en: Keep movement down and get medical care promptly; remedies can delay treatment.

body.zh:
## 错误急救可能增加伤害
切开伤口、吸吮、用窄止血带扎紧或敷不明药物，可能无效甚至造成额外损伤。不要凭伤口小、暂时不痛或自己认不出蛇，就等待症状出现后再处理。

## 安静下来，安排转运
尽量让被咬者保持不动，减少行走并及时安排医疗转运，遵从急救人员指导。不同蛇毒造成的损伤不同，某地推荐的加压包扎方法并不一定适合所有地区，不应照视频自行套用。专业治疗可能需要合适的抗蛇毒血清，不能由家庭处理替代。
body.en:
## Improvised first aid can add harm
Cutting, sucking, tight narrow tourniquets or unknown remedies may be ineffective and cause further injury. Do not wait for symptoms because the wound is small, pain is limited or you cannot identify the snake.

## Keep still and arrange transport
Keep the person as still as possible, minimise walking and arrange prompt medical transport, following emergency professionals' instructions. Venoms differ. Pressure-bandaging advice appropriate in one region is not necessarily suitable everywhere, so do not copy a video indiscriminately. Treatment may require appropriate antivenom; home measures cannot replace professional care.

sources.title: WHO · Snakebite envenoming: questions and answers (20 November 2019), first aid

credit: Michael Smith; Edward J. Wozniak / CDC PHIL #8133 · Public domain
imageAlt: A real snake identified in the CDC source as Crotalus atrox, photographed on the ground; generic snakebite-awareness context, not a local species-identification guide, handling instruction or first-aid demonstration.

title.zh: 误服清洁剂或药品，不要自行催吐
title.en: Do not induce vomiting after swallowing a harmful substance

summary.zh: 先求助，保留容器和包装，帮助医务人员判断。
summary.en: Seek help and retain the container or packaging for clinicians.

body.zh:
## 不能靠“吐出来就没事”处理
误服清洁剂、药物等可疑有害物质后，应立即寻求医疗建议，不等到明显不舒服才行动。自行催吐可能导致呛入气道甚至影响呼吸。不要擅自喂食物、饮料或其他东西，按专业人员指导处理。

## 带上信息，不让施救者也受伤
记下物质名称、接触时间和大概情况，有条件时带上包装或容器。呼吸困难、抽搐、失去意识或停止呼吸需要立即急救，并按调度指导施救。平时把化学品和药物放在儿童看不到、拿不到的位置，最好上锁；不要让一次“暂时没症状”成为放松的理由。
body.en:
## Vomiting is not a reliable solution
Seek immediate medical advice after possible ingestion of a harmful cleaner or medicine, without waiting for symptoms. Inducing vomiting can cause choking and interfere with breathing. Do not give food, drinks or other substances without professional instructions.

## Bring information, not additional risk
Note the product, exposure time and circumstances; retain packaging where possible. Breathing difficulty, seizures, unconsciousness or absent breathing needs emergency help and dispatcher-guided action. Keep chemicals and medicines out of children's sight and reach, preferably locked away. Feeling well initially does not establish that an exposure was harmless.

sources.title: NHS · Poisoning (reviewed 12 June 2025)

imageAlt: Packaged car-cleaning and care products displayed in a hardware store in Munich, Germany. General chemical-exposure context, not an actual poisoning, proof of child resistance, storage advice or brand endorsement.

title.zh: 对食物和体形的担忧占满生活时，需要支持
title.en: When food and body worries take over daily life, seek support

summary.zh: 进食障碍是可以治疗的疾病，不是简单的意志力问题。
summary.en: Eating disorders are treatable illnesses, not a simple issue of willpower.

body.zh:
## 留意持续的困扰
进食障碍涉及严重的进食行为紊乱。对体重、体形或控制进食的想法过度执着，可能是需要评估的信号，不能只当作挑食或“追求自律”。偶尔关注饮食不等于确诊，但持续困扰并影响生活时值得认真对待。

## 求助不必等到身体撑不住
这类疾病可能伴随身体并发症、焦虑或抑郁，早发现、早治疗很重要。可向可信任的家长、学校心理老师或医生说明情况，获得专业评估。陪伴者少评论身材，不以比赛式节食鼓励对方，也不要自行替朋友设计严格饮食计划来“纠正”问题。
body.en:
## Notice persistent distress
Eating disorders involve serious disturbances in eating behaviour. Fixation on weight, shape or controlling intake can signal a need for assessment, rather than simply picky eating or discipline. Occasional dietary concern is not a diagnosis, but persistent distress disrupting life deserves attention.

## Do not wait for a physical crisis
These illnesses can involve medical complications, anxiety or depression. Early recognition and treatment matter. Tell a trusted parent, school counsellor or clinician and seek professional assessment. Supporters can avoid body commentary and competitive dieting. Do not try to correct a friend's difficulties by designing a restrictive meal plan yourself.

sources.title: NIMH · Eating disorders (reviewed December 2024)

imageAlt: A table laid with dishes of food at Tassajara Hot Springs, with no people, body measurements or weight figures shown. Neutral meal context, not an eating-disorder diagnosis, prescribed portion size or treatment endorsement.

title.zh: 尿频、尿痛，不一定只是“上火”
title.en: Frequent, painful urination deserves more than a vague explanation

summary.zh: 膀胱感染可能需要治疗，发热和腰侧痛尤其要警惕。
summary.en: Bladder infection may need treatment; fever and flank pain need prompt attention.

body.zh:
## 有尿意，却只排出一点
膀胱感染可引起排尿灼痛、频繁或强烈尿意，即使实际尿量不多，也可能伴下腹不适、尿液混浊或带血。最常见的原因是细菌。仅凭“上火”解释，可能忽略需要处理的感染；这些表现也不能在家自行确诊。

## 出现全身不适要及时就医
有相关症状应咨询医生。若伴发热、寒战、恶心呕吐或背部、腰侧疼痛，需要尽快评估是否累及肾脏，不只靠多喝水等待。是否需要检查和药物，由医务人员判断，不自行使用家里剩下的抗生素。
body.en:
## A strong urge with little urine
Bladder infection may cause burning urination, frequent or intense urges despite passing little urine, lower-abdominal discomfort, and cloudy or bloody urine. Bacteria are the most common cause. A vague explanation can overlook an infection needing care, but symptoms alone cannot confirm the diagnosis at home.

## Systemic symptoms need prompt care
Discuss urinary symptoms with a clinician. Fever, chills, nausea, vomiting or back or flank pain needs prompt assessment for possible kidney involvement, rather than waiting with extra water alone. Clinicians decide which tests and treatment are needed. Do not use leftover antibiotics yourself.

sources.title: NIDDK · Symptoms and causes of bladder infection in adults (reviewed April 2024)

imageAlt: Rows of capped plastic water bottles. Generic hydration context, not a personal UTI diagnosis, prescribed fluid intake, treatment claim or endorsement of the visible brand.

title.zh: 孩子也可能有肾结石，腰侧痛别硬扛
title.en: Children can have kidney stones too: take flank pain seriously

summary.zh: 血尿、明显疼痛或排不出尿，都需要评估。
summary.en: Blood in urine, marked pain or inability to urinate needs assessment.

body.zh:
## 不只是成年人的问题
儿童和青少年也可能出现肾结石。表现可包括背部、腰侧、下腹或腹股沟的锐痛，疼痛可能一阵阵出现，也可能有血尿、排尿疼痛或强烈尿意。不能仅凭年龄小就排除，也不能把所有腰痛都当成结石。

## 排尿困难或发热时，尽快求助
出现这些症状应及时就医，尤其排不出尿、只能排很少、伴发热寒战或呕吐时，不要只在家尝试大量喝水“冲下去”。医生需要判断病因和是否存在更严重问题。结石可与尿中某些矿物质浓度较高有关，后续预防也应按评估结果安排。
body.en:
## Not only an adult condition
Children and teenagers can develop kidney stones. Sharp pain in the back, flank, lower abdomen or groin may come in waves. Blood in urine, painful urination or a persistent urge can occur too. Young age does not rule it out, but not all back pain is a stone.

## Get symptoms assessed promptly
Seek care, especially with inability to urinate, very little urine, fever, chills or vomiting. Do not simply try to flush a suspected stone out with large quantities of water. Clinicians need to establish the cause and check for serious problems. Prevention depends on the findings, including relevant mineral concentrations.

sources.title: NIDDK · Symptoms and causes of kidney stones in children (reviewed May 2017)

imageAlt: A real kidney stone photographed beside a ruler, identified as a kidney stone by its source. Not a rendered object, a personal diagnostic result or proof of a particular stone composition.

title.zh: 疥疮治疗，为什么同住的人也要一起考虑？
title.en: Why does scabies treatment involve the household?

summary.zh: 还没有开始痒，也可能已经有疥螨。
summary.en: An infestation can be present before itching begins.

body.zh:
## 传播可能早于症状
疥疮由疥螨寄生皮肤引起，可造成明显瘙痒和皮疹，主要通过密切皮肤接触传播。首次感染后，症状可能延迟出现，因此同住者没有发痒，并不能说明没有受到影响。诊断应由医生结合皮损等判断，不靠网上照片。

## 治疗和织物处理要配合
确诊后按医嘱完成处理，同住成员通常也需要同步治疗，即使没有症状。接触过的衣物和床品按指导清洗、干燥，不能洗的物品可按要求密封处理。治疗后短期仍痒不一定代表治疗失败，不自行反复加药，应询问医生是否需要复查。
body.en:
## Spread may precede symptoms
Scabies is a skin infestation by mites, causing itching and rash and spreading mainly through close skin contact. Symptoms can be delayed after first infestation. A household member who is not itchy may still be affected. Diagnosis needs clinical assessment rather than comparison with online photographs.

## Coordinate treatment and laundry
Follow the prescribed course. Household members generally need treatment at the same time, even without symptoms. Clean and dry affected clothing and bedding as directed, and seal non-washable items when advised. Itching can persist shortly after treatment, so do not assume failure or repeatedly add medicines yourself; ask whether reassessment is needed.

sources.title: WHO · Scabies (31 May 2023)

imageAlt: Folded towels arranged on retail shelves. Generic textile-care context, not an image of Sarcoptes scabiei, head lice or any other parasite, and not evidence of infestation or successful decontamination.

title.zh: 脚痒、脱皮，先别把所有问题都当作脚气
title.en: Itchy, peeling feet are not always athlete's foot

summary.zh: 潮湿容易让足癣反复，但症状相似不等于病因相同。
summary.en: Moisture encourages athlete's foot, but similar symptoms can have other causes.

body.zh:
## 趾缝发白、脱皮值得留意
足癣是真菌感染，可能使趾缝出现瘙痒、发白或脱屑，也可累及脚底、脚侧，造成裂口。脚部潮湿、多汗时更容易感染。不过，脚痒本身不能确诊足癣；症状不典型或一直不好时，需要评估，医生有时会取皮屑检查。别只凭网上照片反复换药。

## 洗后擦干，也要让鞋袜透气
洗脚后轻轻擦干，尤其是趾缝，每天换干净袜子，避免长时间穿让脚闷热、多汗的鞋。在公共淋浴间和更衣室穿拖鞋，不共用毛巾或鞋袜。药师可帮助选择适合年龄的抗真菌产品，按说明完成疗程。若治疗无效、疼痛明显，或脚和腿出现发热、疼痛、发红，应就医；有糖尿病或免疫功能低下的人，足部问题更应及时评估。
body.en:
## Look beyond itching alone
Athlete's foot is a fungal infection that can cause itchy, pale or flaky skin between the toes. It may affect the soles and sides or cause cracks. Wet, sweaty feet increase the risk. However, itching alone cannot confirm the cause. A persistent or uncertain rash needs assessment; a clinician may examine a skin scraping rather than rely on appearance alone.

## Dry feet and check treatment suitability
After washing, dab feet dry, especially between the toes. Change socks daily and avoid shoes that keep feet hot and sweaty. Wear flip-flops in shared showers and changing rooms, and do not share towels or footwear. Ask a pharmacist about an age-appropriate antifungal and follow its instructions. Seek care if treatment fails, pain is marked, or the foot or leg becomes hot, painful and red. Diabetes or weakened immunity warrants particular care with foot problems.

sources.title: NHS · Athlete's foot (reviewed 29 April 2024)

title.zh: 手上的普通疣，不等于生殖器疣
title.en: An ordinary hand wart is not a genital wart

summary.zh: HPV是一大类病毒，不同类型造成的问题不同。
summary.en: HPV is a large virus family whose different types behave differently.

body.zh:
## 同一个病毒家族，有不同类型
手指、手背等部位的普通疣，以及脚底的跖疣，可由感染皮肤的HPV引起。引起这些疣的类型，与引起生殖器疣及某些癌前病变的类型不同。不能因为手上长疣，就推断有生殖器感染或性接触史。普通疣可能摸起来粗糙、坚硬，有些会自行消退，但也可能持续数月甚至数年。

## 别抠、别剪，不确定时先检查
疣可经皮肤接触或受污染的表面传播，潮湿或破损皮肤更容易受影响。触摸后洗手，不抠疣、不咬长疣的手指，不共用毛巾。需要治疗时先问药师，产品可能刺激皮肤，不能随意用于面部或生殖器。若皮损出血、外观变化、很大或很痛，或根本不能确定是不是疣，请让医生检查。
body.en:
## Different HPV types affect different sites
Ordinary hand warts and plantar warts are caused by skin-infecting types of human papillomavirus, or HPV. These differ from types responsible for genital warts and those linked to precancerous changes. A hand wart does not establish genital infection or someone's sexual history. Common warts often feel firm and rough. Some disappear without treatment, although this can take months or years.

## Avoid picking and check uncertain growths
Warts can spread through skin contact or contaminated surfaces, particularly when skin is wet or damaged. Wash hands after touching one, avoid picking or biting affected fingers, and do not share towels. A pharmacist can advise on treatment; products may irritate skin and should not be used indiscriminately on the face or genitals. Get a growth assessed if it bleeds, changes appearance, becomes very painful or large, or may not be a wart.

sources.title: NHS · Warts and verrucas (reviewed 25 July 2023)
Cambridge University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust · Human papillomavirus (HPV), version 5 (approved 3 September 2024)

imageAlt: A hand resting on a trouser leg; generic hand context, not a photograph of diagnosed warts or an assertion about the person's health.

title.zh: 皮肤反复渗液、结黄痂，需要考虑脓疱疮
title.en: Weeping sores with golden crusts need assessment for impetigo

summary.zh: 这种细菌性皮肤感染容易传播，治疗与日常接触都要处理。
summary.en: This bacterial skin infection spreads easily and needs appropriate treatment and precautions.

body.zh:
## 外观相似，不能自己确诊
脓疱疮可从疮口或水疱开始，破溃后留下金黄色或褐黄色痂皮，常见于鼻口周围和手部。可能痒，也可能痛，皮损还会扩大。它是细菌感染，但湿疹、唇疱疹等也会出现相似表现。怀疑时应咨询医生或合适的医疗人员，判断是否需要局部治疗或抗生素，不自己用家中剩药。

## 治疗期间减少传播
接触皮损及共用毛巾、床品都可能传播感染。勤洗手，轻柔清洁并擦干患处，不抓挠或揭痂，不共用个人用品。完成医嘱疗程，不因刚有好转就停药。仍有传染性时避免接触性运动，返校时间按诊疗建议和当地要求安排。若治疗后症状变样或加重、反复发作，或本人免疫功能低下，应再次就医，而不是继续照原方案自行处理。
body.en:
## Similar-looking sores can have different causes
Impetigo can begin as sores or blisters that burst and leave golden-brown crusts, often around the nose, mouth or hands. Patches may itch, hurt or enlarge. It is a bacterial infection, but eczema and cold sores can resemble it. Ask a clinician or suitable healthcare professional to assess suspected infection and decide whether local treatment or antibiotics are needed. Do not use leftover medicines.

## Reduce spread while completing treatment
Skin contact and shared towels or bedding can transmit infection. Wash hands, gently clean and dry affected skin, avoid scratching or picking crusts, and keep personal items separate. Finish the prescribed treatment even when sores improve. Avoid contact sports while infectious and follow clinical advice and local requirements about school attendance. Seek reassessment if symptoms change or worsen after treatment, infection recurs, or you have a weakened immune system.

sources.title: NHS · Impetigo (reviewed 6 June 2024)

title.zh: 头皮屑多，不是评判头发脏不脏的标准
title.en: Dandruff is not a measure of dirty hair

summary.zh: 头皮的脱屑与炎症需要合适护理，不能只靠更用力地洗。
summary.en: Scalp flaking and inflammation need suitable care, not simply harder washing.

body.zh:
## 皮肤反应比“没洗干净”复杂
头皮屑可表现为轻度的头皮脱屑，也属于头皮脂溢性皮炎的表现范围。皮肤屏障以及对正常皮肤上马拉色菌相关产物的反应，都可能参与其中；不能把脱屑直接当作不讲卫生。疲劳、压力和寒冷干燥天气可能诱发反复。轻度头皮屑不具传染性，同学有头皮屑不应成为被疏远的理由。

## 按产品要求护理，明显炎症要评估
可向药师咨询适合年龄的去屑洗发产品，有些含抗真菌成分。按包装说明使用，不能靠抓挠或反复猛搓来处理脱屑，也不要擅自加用口服药或长期涂激素。若头皮明显疼痛、发炎、渗液，或规范护理后仍不改善，应请医生检查。不同头皮问题外观可能相近，医生需要判断是否为其他皮疹或头癣；单凭头皮屑不能推断有严重基础疾病。
body.en:
## Flaking has more than one explanation
Dandruff can be mild scalp scaling within the range of seborrhoeic dermatitis. The skin barrier and sensitivity to substances produced by Malassezia, a yeast normally present on skin, may contribute. Flakes do not establish poor hygiene. Tiredness, stress and cold, dry weather can trigger flares. Mild dandruff is not contagious, so it is not a reason to exclude someone socially.

## Choose suitable scalp care
Ask a pharmacist about an age-appropriate anti-dandruff shampoo; some contain antifungal ingredients. Follow the product instructions rather than trying to remove flakes through scratching or vigorous rubbing. Do not add oral medicines or prolonged steroid treatment yourself. A painful, inflamed or weeping scalp, or symptoms that resist appropriate care, needs assessment. Other rashes and scalp ringworm can resemble seborrhoeic dermatitis. Dandruff alone does not establish a serious underlying illness.

sources.title: British Association of Dermatologists · Seborrhoeic dermatitis patient information leaflet (updated January 2023), pages 1 to 4
NHS England · Over-the-counter prescribing policy guidance, dandruff section (published 12 March 2024)

imageAlt: Vintage shampoo and conditioner bottles displayed in Sapporo, cropped from a larger collection photograph; historical hair-care packaging, not a dandruff treatment or brand recommendation.

title.zh: 口腔溃疡超过三周，别再只等它自己好
title.en: A mouth ulcer lasting over three weeks needs checking

summary.zh: 常见溃疡通常会愈合，持续或明显变化的病损需要检查。
summary.en: Common ulcers usually heal; persistent or changing lesions need examination.

body.zh:
## 普通溃疡多在一两周内好转
常见口腔溃疡会出现在嘴唇内侧、颊黏膜或舌头上，通常一两周内自行愈合。咬伤、牙齿锐边或牙套摩擦都可能诱发。普通口腔溃疡不具传染性，也不等同于唇疱疹。口腔里出现疼痛病损有多种原因，不能看见白点就认定缺维生素，或直接开始大剂量补充。

## 让伤口少受刺激，也记住观察期限
使用软毛牙刷，选择柔软食物，避开会刺激伤处的辛辣、酸性或过烫食物和饮料。需要缓解疼痛时，可向药师询问适合年龄的产品。若同一处溃疡超过三周未愈、比平时大或位置不同，或出现出血、疼痛和发红加重，应让牙医或医生检查。持续病损偶尔与严重疾病有关，但“需要检查”不等于已经确诊癌症；有身体其他部位溃疡或关节肿痛时，也要说明。
body.en:
## Most ordinary ulcers heal
Common mouth ulcers appear inside the lips or cheeks, or on the tongue, and usually heal within one or two weeks. A cheek bite, sharp tooth or rubbing brace can trigger one. Ordinary ulcers are not contagious and are different from cold sores. A sore in the mouth has several possible causes; its appearance alone does not establish vitamin deficiency or justify high-dose supplements.

## Reduce irritation and track healing
Use a soft toothbrush and softer foods, and avoid very hot, acidic or spicy items that irritate the sore. A pharmacist can advise on age-appropriate pain relief. See a dentist or doctor if the same ulcer lasts over three weeks, is unusually large or differently located, bleeds, or becomes increasingly painful and red. Persistent lesions sometimes signal serious disease, but needing examination is not a cancer diagnosis. Mention ulcers elsewhere or painful, swollen joints too.

title.zh: 偶尔烧心和反复反流，处理方式不一样
title.en: Occasional heartburn and troublesome reflux need different responses

summary.zh: 留意出现频率和伴随症状，不把所有胸口不适都归为胃酸。
summary.en: Notice recurrence and accompanying symptoms; chest discomfort is not automatically reflux.

body.zh:
## 胃内容物回流，可能带来烧灼感
胃内容物回到食管时，可能引起胸骨后的烧灼感，或让口中尝到食物、酸味。青少年也会出现这些表现。偶尔反流很常见；反复出现、让人困扰或导致并发症时，需要评估是否为胃食管反流病。并非每个人都有典型烧心，也不能把所有胸痛都当成胃酸问题。

## 反复影响生活，或有警示症状时求助
把症状与进食、躺下的关系告诉医生。夜间或躺下时不适的人，医生可能建议调整睡前进食时间，并根据个人反应处理诱发食物，不必照着网上清单大范围忌口。青少年不要自行开始减重饮食或长期吃抑酸药。若吞咽困难或吞咽疼痛、反复呕吐、呕血或便血，或因拒食而体重下降，应尽快就医；呼吸困难需要立即急救。
body.en:
## Reflux can cause burning or a sour taste
When stomach contents return to the oesophagus, they may cause burning behind the breastbone or bring food and acid into the mouth. Teenagers can experience this too. Occasional reflux is common. Repeated, troublesome symptoms or complications need assessment for gastro-oesophageal reflux disease. Not everyone has typical heartburn, and chest discomfort should not automatically be labelled acid reflux.

## Notice patterns and warning signs
Tell a clinician how symptoms relate to meals and lying down. For night-time symptoms, they may suggest changing meal timing and addressing individual food triggers. Broad food exclusions are not automatically necessary. Teenagers should not start weight-loss diets or long-term acid-suppressing treatment themselves. Seek prompt medical care for difficult or painful swallowing, repeated vomiting, blood in vomit or stools, or food avoidance causing weight loss. Breathing difficulty needs emergency help.

title.zh: 喝奶后腹胀，乳糖不耐受和牛奶过敏要分清
title.en: Lactose intolerance and milk allergy are different problems

summary.zh: 一个涉及乳糖消化，另一个涉及免疫反应，饮食处理不能混用。
summary.en: One involves lactose digestion, the other an immune reaction; their management differs.

body.zh:
## 消化乳糖的能力因人而异
乳糖是奶和奶制品中的一种糖。小肠不能充分消化乳糖时，有些人会在进食后腹胀、排气增多或腹泻，这才可能是乳糖不耐受。乳糖吸收不良不一定都带来症状。牛奶过敏则涉及免疫系统，两者不同；不能因为喝奶不舒服，就直接认定是哪一种，也不能把一种情况的饮食方案用于另一种。

## 减少不适时，仍要保留足够营养
不少乳糖不耐受者仍能耐受一定量乳糖，耐受量因人而异。医生或营养师可帮助选择少量随餐、低乳糖或无乳糖奶制品等方案。无乳糖不等于适合牛奶过敏者。不要未经评估就长期删去所有奶及替代品，否则钙、维生素D等摄入可能不足。向医生说明吃了什么、症状和出现时间，比只给自己贴上“不能喝奶”的标签更有用。
body.en:
## Lactose is a sugar, not an allergen label
Lactose is a sugar in milk and milk products. When the small intestine cannot digest it adequately, some people develop bloating, gas or diarrhoea after eating it. Malabsorption does not always cause symptoms. Milk allergy involves the immune system and is a different condition. Discomfort after milk alone cannot establish which problem is present, and advice for one should not be substituted for advice about the other.

## Manage symptoms without losing nutrients
Many people with lactose intolerance can tolerate some lactose, although amounts differ. A clinician or dietitian can help plan smaller portions with meals or lactose-reduced and lactose-free dairy options. Lactose-free does not mean suitable for milk allergy. Avoid removing all dairy and suitable alternatives without a plan: calcium and vitamin D intake may suffer. Explain foods, symptoms and timing when seeking assessment.

sources.title: NIDDK · Definition and facts for lactose intolerance (reviewed February 2018)

title.zh: 怀疑阑尾炎，不要等到症状“全对上”再就医
title.en: Suspected appendicitis should not wait for a perfect symptom checklist

summary.zh: 腹痛可能迅速加重，儿童和青少年不一定出现典型过程。
summary.en: Abdominal pain may worsen quickly, and young people may lack the typical pattern.

body.zh:
## 肚脐周围到右下腹，并非人人如此
阑尾炎的腹痛可能先在肚脐附近出现，再移向右下腹，也可能突然开始，在数小时内加重。有人伴食欲下降、恶心、呕吐或发热，活动时也可能更痛。不过，尤其是儿童，可能没有这些典型表现。疼痛位置不完全相符、没有发热或同时腹泻，都不能单独排除阑尾炎。

## 怀疑时立即获得医疗评估
阑尾炎属于需要立即处理的急症。持续或不断加重的腹痛，尤其让人怀疑阑尾炎时，应马上告诉家长、老师或身边可信任的成人，安排及时就医；疼痛严重时直接寻求急诊帮助。不要自己反复按压、跳跃来“验证”症状，也不要等所有表现都出现后才行动。医生会结合病史、检查和需要时的检验或影像判断原因。其他疾病也可能引起腹痛，因此既不能在家确诊，也不能靠一个不典型表现自行排除。
body.en:
## Pain does not always follow the textbook
Appendicitis may cause pain that starts near the belly button and moves towards the lower right abdomen. It can begin suddenly and worsen within hours. Loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting or fever may accompany it, and movement may hurt. However, especially in children, typical symptoms can be absent. A different pain location, no fever or diarrhoea does not safely rule it out.

## Get assessment without home tests
Suspected appendicitis is a medical emergency requiring immediate care. Tell a parent, teacher or another trusted adult about persistent or worsening abdominal pain and arrange prompt assessment; severe pain warrants emergency help. Do not repeatedly press the abdomen or jump to provoke pain as a home test. Clinicians use the history, examination and appropriate tests or imaging to establish the cause. Other illnesses can cause abdominal pain, so neither diagnosis nor exclusion belongs to a home checklist.

NIDDK · Diagnosis of appendicitis (reviewed July 2021)

title.zh: 维生素D需要适量，不是越补越好
title.en: Vitamin D needs are not a reason for unlimited supplements

summary.zh: 食物、日照和补充剂各有适用范围，别用晒伤或大剂量来追求健康。
summary.en: Food, sunlight and supplements have limits; sunburn and high doses are not health goals.

body.zh:
## 它帮助身体利用钙和磷
维生素D参与调节钙和磷，对骨骼、牙齿及肌肉健康有作用。来源包括油性鱼类、蛋黄和部分强化食品，皮肤在户外日照下也能合成。需要多少、是否要补充，与年龄、饮食、日照及健康状况有关，不能把别人的补充方案直接照搬。食品是否强化要看标签，不能默认所有牛奶都含相同量的维生素D。

## 补充剂过量会伤身
长期摄入过多维生素D补充剂，可能使血钙过高，损伤肾脏、心脏并影响骨骼。不要叠加多种含维生素D的产品，也不要自行采用治疗缺乏时的大剂量方案；有担忧可向医生或药师咨询。补充维生素D同样不是故意晒伤的理由，户外仍需遮阴、衣物与防晒保护。
body.en:
## Vitamin D helps regulate calcium and phosphate
These nutrients support bones, teeth and muscles. Vitamin D sources include oily fish, egg yolks and some fortified foods; skin also makes it in outdoor sunlight. Needs and supplementation decisions depend on age, diet, exposure and health. Someone else's supplement plan may not suit you. Check food labels rather than assuming all milk contains the same added vitamin D.

## Excess supplements can cause harm
Taking too much vitamin D over time can raise blood calcium and damage the kidneys, heart and bones. Avoid stacking products containing vitamin D or adopting high-dose deficiency treatment without medical advice. Ask a clinician or pharmacist if you are concerned. Vitamin D is not a reason to seek sunburn: use shade, clothing and sunscreen outdoors.

sources.title: NHS · Vitamin D, vitamins and minerals (reviewed 3 August 2020)
University Hospitals Sussex NHS Foundation Trust · Be Sun Aware (published 13 June 2023; reviewed 21 June 2023)

title.zh: 增加膳食纤维，从日常食物慢慢调整
title.en: Build food fibre into meals gradually

summary.zh: 全谷、豆类、蔬果可以轮换，增加纤维不需要把饮食越吃越窄。
summary.en: Use varied wholegrains, pulses, fruit and vegetables without narrowing your diet.

body.zh:
## 从熟悉的饭菜里增加来源
膳食纤维有助于预防和缓解便秘。燕麦、全麦面包、豆类和多种蔬果都能提供纤维，不必只盯着一种所谓的高纤食品。可以在原有餐食中逐步加入豆类，或把部分主食换成全谷版本。这些是食物搭配的例子，不是要求每餐都照做，也不是适用于所有人的固定份量。

## 慢慢增加，同时照顾整体营养
逐步改变，让身体适应，并保持合适饮水；液体有助于纤维发挥作用。饮水需要随体型、活动、气候和健康状况调整，不必为了“通便”勉强灌水。增加纤维不等于取消主食、蛋白质食物或奶及替代品，青少年仍需要多样食物提供能量和营养。如果便秘持续，或有特殊疾病、饮食限制，应向医生或营养师咨询，而不是不断加纤维或把能吃的食物越删越少。
body.en:
## Start with familiar foods
Dietary fibre helps prevent and treat constipation. Oats, wholemeal bread, beans and a variety of fruit and vegetables provide it. There is no need to rely on one supposedly superior high-fibre food. Try adding pulses to a familiar meal or replacing part of a usual starchy food with a wholegrain option. These are meal ideas, not compulsory combinations or fixed portions for everyone.

## Increase gradually within a varied diet
Add fibre a little at a time so your body adapts, and drink appropriate fluids to help it work. Fluid needs vary with size, activity, climate and health; forcing excessive water is unnecessary. More fibre does not require removing starchy foods, protein foods or dairy and alternatives. Teenagers still need varied sources of energy and nutrients. Persistent constipation or special medical dietary needs warrants advice from a clinician or dietitian rather than progressively restricting foods.

sources.title: NIDDK · Eating, diet and nutrition for constipation in children (reviewed May 2018)
NHS · The Eatwell Guide (reviewed 29 November 2022)

title.zh: 前往疟疾风险地区，防护方案要按个人行程安排
title.en: Malaria prevention needs a plan for your particular trip

summary.zh: 出发前咨询旅行门诊，防蚊和预防用药不能照搬别人的方案。
summary.en: Ask a travel clinician about bite protection and whether preventive medicine is appropriate.

body.zh:
## 把行程和健康情况一起带去咨询
疟疾由疟原虫引起，可经受感染的按蚊叮咬传播。前往有传播风险的地区前，应咨询旅行门诊，说明具体目的地、停留时间和住宿安排。是否需要预防用药，要结合当地风险及个人情况判断；年龄、怀孕情况、已有疾病和正在服用的药物都可能影响选择。不要直接沿用同行者的处方。

## 旅途中仍要防蚊
按产品说明使用驱蚊剂，穿能遮盖皮肤的衣物，选择有纱窗或空调的住处，必要时使用合适的蚊帐。预防药物不能替代防蚊措施。若医生开了药，应提前问清何时开始、何时结束，并按要求服用。旅行期间或回来后出现发热，应尽快就医，主动说明去过哪里，不因已经采取防护就排除疟疾。
body.en:
## Bring your itinerary and health history
Malaria is caused by parasites transmitted through infected Anopheles mosquito bites. Before visiting an area with transmission risk, consult a travel clinician about your exact destination, length of stay and accommodation. Whether preventive medicine is needed depends on the location and the traveller. Age, pregnancy, existing conditions and other medicines can affect the choice. Do not copy a companion's prescription.

## Keep preventing bites during the trip
Use repellent as directed, cover exposed skin and choose screened or air-conditioned accommodation, with suitable mosquito nets when needed. Preventive medicine does not replace bite protection. If prescribed, clarify when to start and finish it. Seek prompt assessment for fever during or after travel and explain your itinerary, even if you took precautions.

sources.title: WHO · International travel and health: module 3: malaria (25 November 2024)
CDC · Preventing malaria while traveling (12 March 2024)
CDC · Malaria risk assessment for travelers (reviewed 28 March 2024; published 15 May 2024)

credit: Tjeerd Wiersma / Wikimedia Commons · CC BY 2.0
imageAlt: A real mosquito net hanging over a bed; general mosquito-bite prevention context. The photograph does not establish insecticide treatment, intactness, correct deployment or malaria protection.

title.zh: 大量水样腹泻，别等确诊后才补液求助
title.en: Severe watery diarrhoea needs rehydration and urgent care

summary.zh: 霍乱可迅速造成严重脱水，但水样腹泻本身不能确诊霍乱。
summary.en: Cholera can cause rapid dehydration, but watery diarrhoea alone does not confirm it.

body.zh:
## 留意迅速丢失的水分
霍乱可经受霍乱弧菌污染的食物或水传播。有些感染者症状很轻，也有人出现大量水样腹泻，迅速丢失水分和电解质。不要仅凭便的外观自行确诊，也不要等化验结果出来才处理脱水。腹泻量大、明显虚弱、喝不进去或意识异常时，需要紧急医疗帮助；重症可能需要静脉补液。

## 求助途中开始合适的补液
患者清醒且能够安全吞咽时，可在安排就医的同时使用口服补液盐，严格按包装要求用安全饮用水配制。普通饮料不能替代严重腹泻所需的规范补液；无法饮用时不要强灌，也不要只靠自行吃抗生素等待。日常预防应使用安全饮用水，妥善处理食物和排泄物，如厕后及准备食物前用肥皂洗手。这些措施也有助于预防其他腹泻病。
body.en:
## Watch for rapid fluid loss
Cholera spreads through food or water contaminated with Vibrio cholerae. Some infections are mild, while others cause profuse watery diarrhoea and rapid loss of water and electrolytes. Stool appearance cannot establish the diagnosis. Do not wait for laboratory confirmation before addressing dehydration. Large losses, marked weakness, inability to drink or altered consciousness require urgent medical help; severe cases may need intravenous fluids.

## Begin appropriate rehydration while arranging care
If the person is alert and can swallow safely, offer oral rehydration solution while seeking care. Prepare packets with safe water exactly as instructed. Ordinary drinks do not replace appropriate rehydration for severe diarrhoea. Do not force fluids into someone unable to drink or wait at home with self-selected antibiotics. Use safe drinking water, handle food and waste safely, and wash hands with soap after the toilet and before food preparation.

sources.title: WHO · Cholera, Chinese-language fact sheet (5 December 2024 edition)

imageAlt: Water running from a kitchen tap, with a drying cloth on the tap. General water-hygiene context, not verification of drinking-water safety, a cholera outbreak or an ideal hygiene demonstration.

title.zh: 没有腮部肿大，也不能单凭这一点排除流行性腮腺炎
title.en: Mumps can occur without swollen cheeks

summary.zh: 表现可能不典型，接种过疫苗也不能完全排除感染。
summary.en: Symptoms can be subtle, and previous vaccination does not completely rule out infection.

body.zh:
## 腮腺肿大不是每个人都有
流行性腮腺炎是一种病毒感染，常见表现包括发热、头痛、乏力和下颌附近唾液腺疼痛肿胀，可发生在一侧或两侧。有些人只有轻微不适或呼吸道症状，也有人没有明显症状。并发症也可能在没有腮腺肿大时出现。因此，接触史和整体症状都值得告诉医生，不能只看脸有没有肿。

## 疑似感染时，先咨询再参加集体活动
病毒可经唾液和呼吸道飞沫传播。怀疑感染时，应先联系医疗机构，说明症状和接触情况，按指导安排就诊及暂停集体活动，不共用饮水杯。出现明显头痛、颈部僵硬或睾丸疼痛肿胀时，应及时求助。含腮腺炎成分的疫苗能降低患病和并发症风险，但保护并非百分之百；接种记录不清楚时，可请接种门诊核对当地适用的补种安排。
body.en:
## Swollen salivary glands are not universal
Mumps is a viral infection that can cause fever, headache, tiredness and painful salivary-gland swelling near the jaw, on one or both sides. Some people have only mild or respiratory symptoms; others have no obvious symptoms. Complications can also occur without parotitis. Tell a clinician about relevant contact and the full pattern of illness rather than judging only by facial swelling.

## Ask for advice before joining group activities
The virus spreads through saliva and respiratory droplets. If mumps is suspected, contact a healthcare service before attending, explain symptoms and exposure, and follow advice about staying away from group settings. Avoid sharing drinking cups. Seek prompt care for severe headache, neck stiffness or painful testicular swelling. Mumps-containing vaccines reduce illness and complications without providing complete protection. Ask a vaccination service to check unclear records against local recommendations.

sources.title: CDC · Pink Book, chapter 15: mumps (14th edition, August 2021; web publication 16 July 2024)

title.zh: 风疹可能很轻，但孕期接触需要认真咨询
title.en: Mild rubella symptoms can still matter during pregnancy

summary.zh: 出疹不能自行确诊；孕期疑似接触应及时联系产科或医生。
summary.en: A rash is not a diagnosis; suspected exposure in pregnancy needs prompt clinical advice.

body.zh:
## 症状轻，不代表对胎儿没有风险
风疹可引起轻微发热、皮疹和淋巴结肿大，也可能没有明显症状。怀孕期间感染，尤其在孕早期，可能造成流产或先天性风疹综合征，影响孩子的听力、眼睛或心脏。皮疹有很多原因，不能靠网上图片认定风疹，更不能据此推断胎儿一定受损。

## 让医生核对接触史和免疫情况
孕妇若有疑似接触或出现相关症状，应及时联系产科或医生，说明接触时间、症状及已有接种或检测记录。就诊前先告知情况，避免未经安排进入有其他孕妇的候诊区。医生会判断是否需要检测及后续随访。计划怀孕时可提前咨询免疫情况和接种需要；含风疹成分的活疫苗不应在孕期接种，具体安排由专业人员结合当地建议决定，不自行补种。
body.en:
## Mild symptoms do not establish fetal safety
Rubella can cause a mild fever, rash and swollen lymph nodes, or no obvious symptoms. Infection during pregnancy, especially early pregnancy, can cause miscarriage or congenital rubella syndrome, affecting hearing, eyes or the heart. Many illnesses cause rashes. An online photograph cannot confirm rubella or establish that a fetus has been harmed.

## Let clinicians review exposure and immunity
If you are pregnant and have possible exposure or symptoms, contact your maternity team or clinician promptly. Describe the timing and bring any vaccination or previous test records. Call before attending so the service can arrange assessment without exposing other pregnant patients. Clinicians can decide which tests and follow-up are appropriate. Before pregnancy, discuss immunity and any vaccination needed. Live rubella-containing vaccine should not be given during pregnancy; individual arrangements need professional advice under local recommendations.

sources.title: CDC · Pink Book, chapter 20: rubella (14th edition, August 2021; web publication 16 July 2024)

imageAlt: A pen resting on the cover of a closed black notebook on a wooden surface.

title.zh: 脊灰感染可能没有症状，预防不能等到无力时
title.en: Polio prevention starts before weakness appears

summary.zh: 少数感染会损伤运动神经，接种和卫生措施需要提前落实。
summary.en: Some infections damage motor nerves, so vaccination and hygiene matter before illness.

body.zh:
## 没有明显不适，也可能传播
脊髓灰质炎由脊灰病毒引起，主要经粪口途径传播。很多感染者没有明显症状，或只有短暂发热、咽痛等不适，但仍可能排出病毒。少数感染会累及控制肌肉的神经，造成肢体无力或瘫痪，部分损伤可能永久存在。不能凭身边没人出现瘫痪，就判断不需要预防。突然出现肢体无力或呼吸困难，应立即就医，不自行认定是脊灰或等它自行恢复。

## 核对接种记录，保持手部和饮水卫生
疫苗是预防脊灰的重要手段。由接种门诊核对既往记录，按当地免疫程序安排接种；记录不全时不要自己猜测已经完成。出境前可向旅行门诊询问目的地是否有额外要求。便后和准备食物前洗手，使用安全饮用水并妥善处理排泄物，也有助于减少传播机会。卫生措施不能替代疫苗。
body.en:
## Infection can spread without obvious illness
Polio is caused by poliovirus, mainly transmitted through the faecal-oral route. Many infected people have no obvious symptoms or a brief illness such as fever or sore throat, yet can shed the virus. A minority develop damage to nerves controlling muscles, causing weakness or paralysis that may be permanent. The absence of visible paralysis around you is not a reason to skip prevention. Sudden limb weakness or breathing difficulty needs immediate medical assessment, without assuming the cause or waiting for recovery.

## Check vaccination records and hygiene
Vaccination is central to prevention. Ask a vaccination service to review records and follow the local programme rather than guessing that an incomplete record means protection. Before overseas travel, ask about additional destination requirements. Handwashing after the toilet and before food preparation, safe drinking water and safe waste disposal help reduce transmission opportunities but do not replace vaccination.

sources.title: CDC · Pink Book, chapter 18: poliomyelitis (14th edition; reviewed 1 May 2024, web publication 16 July 2024)

title.zh: 处理生鸡肉，防弯曲菌要靠分开操作和彻底煮熟
title.en: Prevent Campylobacter with separation and thorough cooking

summary.zh: 冲洗生禽肉可能把细菌溅到原本干净的食物和台面上。
summary.en: Rinsing raw poultry can splash bacteria onto clean food and surfaces.

body.zh:
## 风险会沿着手和厨具转移
弯曲菌可存在于生禽肉中，吃下未熟禽肉，或吃到被生肉汁污染的食物，都可能感染。腹泻、腹痛和发热通常不会在接触后立刻出现，所以不能靠当时感觉正常判断操作安全。用处理过生鸡肉的刀切沙拉，或没洗手就拿熟食，都可能让细菌绕过后续烹煮。

## 不冲洗生禽肉，把清洁留给手和用具
冲洗不能可靠去除病原体，飞溅水滴还可能污染水槽、台面及附近食物。把生肉与即食食物分开，使用不同的砧板和用具，接触生肉后洗净双手，清洁受污染的表面。禽肉要彻底煮熟，包括内部；熟食应放在干净盘中，不放回盛过生肉的容器。若出现血便、严重腹泻或脱水，应就医，不自行用剩余抗生素处理。
body.en:
## Bacteria can travel on hands and utensils
Campylobacter can be present in raw poultry. Infection may follow eating undercooked meat or food contaminated by raw juices. Diarrhoea, abdominal pain and fever usually develop later, so feeling well during preparation says nothing about safety. Cutting salad with a knife used for raw chicken, or touching cooked food before washing hands, can transfer bacteria to food that will not be cooked again.

## Cook poultry instead of rinsing it
Do not wash raw poultry: rinsing cannot reliably remove pathogens and splashes can contaminate the sink, worktop and nearby food. Separate raw meat from ready-to-eat food, use separate boards and utensils, wash hands after handling meat and clean contaminated surfaces. Cook poultry thoroughly, including the centre. Put cooked food on a clean plate rather than its raw-meat container. Seek care for bloody or severe diarrhoea or dehydration; do not use leftover antibiotics.

sources.title: WHO · Campylobacter (1 May 2020)
Hong Kong CFS · Safe food for all: prepare (revised 27 January 2023), cross-contamination precautions
UK Food Standards Agency · Food and You 2: wave 5 key findings (26 January 2023), avoiding cross-contamination

title.zh: 发现高低肩，先评估，不急着归咎于坐姿
title.en: Uneven shoulders deserve assessment, not blame about posture

summary.zh: 身体不对称是观察线索，不能靠照片确诊脊柱侧弯。
summary.en: Asymmetry is a reason to seek assessment, not a diagnosis from a photograph.

body.zh:
## 留意持续的不对称
脊柱侧弯涉及脊柱向侧方弯曲和旋转。可能看到肩膀不等高、一侧髋部或肋骨更突出，衣服两边不服帖。这些表现值得评估，但并不意味着任何高低肩都能确诊，也不能凭一张站姿照片判断严重程度。许多青少年病例原因不明，称为特发性脊柱侧弯，并不认为是坐姿差、运动或饮食造成的。

## 检查后再决定是否需要处理
若自己或家长持续发现上述变化，可预约医生检查；怀疑侧弯时可能需要专科评估及影像检查，以了解弯曲程度。处理取决于年龄、弯曲大小和进展可能性，有些只需观察，并非都要手术。不要因担心被责备而拖延，也不要自行购买支具或把网上的矫正动作当成治疗。大多数患者仍能参加日常活动和运动，具体限制应由医生根据情况说明。
body.en:
## Notice persistent asymmetry
Scoliosis involves sideways curvature and twisting of the spine. Uneven shoulders, a more prominent hip or ribs on one side, or clothing hanging unevenly can be clues. These changes deserve assessment, but not every uneven shoulder establishes scoliosis, and a standing photograph cannot measure its severity. Many adolescent cases have no known cause and are called idiopathic scoliosis. They are not thought to result from poor posture, exercise or diet.

## Decide on treatment after assessment
Arrange a medical appointment if you or a parent notices persistent changes. Suspected scoliosis may need specialist assessment and imaging to measure the curve. Management depends on age, curve size and likelihood of progression; some people need observation rather than treatment. Do not delay because of blame, buy a brace independently or treat online corrective exercises as a cure. Most people can continue ordinary activities and sport, with individual advice where needed.

sources.title: NHS · Scoliosis: overview (reviewed 12 April 2023)

credit: John Campbell / Wikimedia Commons · CC BY 2.0
imageAlt: A physical anatomical teaching model showing vertebrae, discs and nerves; not a patient's spine, an X-ray, a scoliosis diagnosis or a model of a confirmed scoliosis case.

title.zh: 分不清某些颜色，不等于失去视力
title.en: Difficulty telling colours apart is not the same as losing sight

summary.zh: 网上色觉图不能代替检查，学习材料也可以作出调整。
summary.en: Online colour plates cannot replace assessment, and learning materials can be adapted.

body.zh:
## 困难可能只出现在某些任务里
色觉异常会让人较难区分某些颜色，并不等于看不见。有人从小就有，可能在绘画、按颜色分类或读彩色图表时才被发现。不要把配色错误当作不用心，也不要凭一道测试题给同学贴标签。色觉也可能因眼病、其他疾病或药物发生变化；新出现的变化应告诉眼科专业人员，不能一概当成遗传问题。

## 正式检查，同时减少颜色障碍
有疑问时可预约眼科或视光检查，说明哪些任务遇到困难。专业人员可使用色点图或颜色排列等方法评估。网上测试不能代替诊断，尤其不应凭手机上的一次结果自行判断职业资格。确诊后，可与老师商量图表文字标注、符号或不同线型，让信息不只靠颜色区分。这类调整是帮助获取相同信息，不表示学习能力较差；需要时还可获得具体的学习支持。
body.en:
## Some tasks reveal the difficulty
Colour vision deficiency makes certain colours harder to distinguish; it does not mean losing sight. It can be present from childhood and become noticeable in drawing, sorting colours or reading charts. Do not treat colour mistakes as carelessness or label a classmate from one test. Colour vision can also change because of eye disease, other illness or medicines. Tell an eye professional about new changes instead of assuming they are inherited.

## Get checked and adapt materials
Arrange an eye assessment if concerned, describing the tasks that cause difficulty. Professionals may use coloured-dot plates or colour-arrangement tests. Online tests cannot replace diagnosis, and one phone result should not determine career eligibility. After assessment, discuss classroom adjustments such as text labels, symbols or different line patterns on charts. These practical changes make information accessible without relying solely on colour; they do not imply lower learning ability.

sources.title: NHS · Colour vision deficiency (colour blindness) (reviewed 17 March 2023)

imageAlt: Six coloured pencils in purple, blue, green, yellow, orange and red. A still-life colour illustration, not a calibrated colour-vision test or evidence of anyone's colour-vision status.

title.zh: 支持结核病患者，也要认真落实空气传播防护
title.en: Support people with TB while taking airborne precautions seriously

summary.zh: 保护隐私、减少歧视与遵循专业防护要求可以同时做到。
summary.en: Privacy, freedom from discrimination and evidence-based precautions belong together.

body.zh:
## 先问对方需要什么帮助
结核病患者可能需要就诊、完成治疗或暂时离开课堂期间的支持。可以在对方同意后提供学习资料，询问是否需要实际帮助，不责备、不在群聊传播姓名、诊断或检查报告。保护隐私并不意味着拒绝必要的公共卫生联系；接触者调查和正式通知应由负责的专业人员按规定处理，只向有必要知情的人提供相关信息。

## 传播风险由病情和专业评估决定
潜伏结核感染不会传染，但具有传染性的肺结核或喉结核可经空气传播，尤其在共处空气流通不良的空间时。不能为了反歧视而说所有结核都不传染。遵循医疗团队关于暂时限制接触、改善通风、口罩或呼吸防护及接触者检查的要求。治疗有助于减少传播，但何时能返校或恢复近距离接触，应由专业人员评估，不用固定服药天数自行判断。暂时不能见面时，仍可通过远程方式提供支持。
body.en:
## Ask what support is useful
Someone with TB may need help attending care, completing treatment or keeping up with lessons during an absence. Offer learning materials with permission and ask about practical needs. Avoid blame and do not circulate names, diagnoses or test reports in group chats. Privacy does not mean obstructing necessary public-health contact: responsible professionals should handle contact tracing and formal notifications, sharing relevant information only where needed.

## Match precautions to clinical assessment
Latent TB infection is not contagious. Infectious pulmonary or laryngeal TB can spread through the air, particularly in poorly ventilated shared spaces. Reducing stigma must not become a claim that all TB is non-infectious. Follow the clinical team's advice on temporary contact restrictions, ventilation, masks or respiratory protection and contact assessment. Treatment reduces transmission, but professionals should decide when close contact or school attendance is safe, not a fixed self-counted treatment period. Remote support can continue meanwhile.

sources.title: WHO · Guidance on ethics of tuberculosis prevention, care and control (2010; release announcement 1 December 2010)
CDC · Guidelines for preventing the transmission of Mycobacterium tuberculosis in health-care settings (30 December 2005)

credit: USAID U.S. Agency for International Development / Wikimedia Commons · CC BY 2.0
imageAlt: Participants looking at educational materials at a tuberculosis-awareness training workshop in South Africa, 2006.

title.zh: 喝过未经处理的水后腹泻，记得告诉医生
title.en: Mention untreated water when seeking help for persistent diarrhoea

summary.zh: 贾第虫是寄生虫，受污染的水和手都可能传播它。
summary.en: Giardia is a parasite that can spread through contaminated water or hands.

body.zh:
## 看起来清澈，也不代表能直接喝
贾第虫可随感染者或动物的粪便进入环境，吞入受污染的水、食物，或通过受污染的手接触嘴，都可能感染。未经处理的山泉、河湖水存在风险，游泳时吞水也可能带来感染。症状可包括持续腹泻、腹胀、腹痛和疲倦，有时粪便油腻、气味明显；不能只靠外观判断病因。

## 持续不适需要评估
若腹泻一直不缓解、反复出现，或担心感染，应就医，并说明近期饮水、游泳和旅行经历。医生可能需要粪便样本检查，再决定治疗。腹泻期间注意补充液体，避免脱水，不自行拿剩药尝试治疗。平时使用安全饮用水，用肥皂和水洗手，游泳时避免吞水；家中有人腹泻时，清洁可能受污染的区域也有助于减少传播。
body.en:
## Clear-looking water may still carry parasites
Giardia passes into the environment in infected people's or animals' faeces. Swallowing contaminated water or food, or transferring it from hands to the mouth, can cause infection. Untreated spring, river or lake water poses a risk, as can swallowing swimming water. Symptoms may include persistent diarrhoea, bloating, cramps and tiredness. Greasy, strong-smelling stools alone cannot identify the cause.

## Explain exposures when seeking care
Seek assessment for persistent or recurring diarrhoea or suspected infection. Mention drinking water, swimming and travel; clinicians may request stool samples before deciding treatment. Replace fluids during diarrhoea and avoid trying leftover medicines. Use safe drinking water, wash hands with soap and water, and avoid swallowing water while swimming. Clean areas contaminated during a household episode of diarrhoea.

sources.title: CDC · About Giardia infection (page dated 2 May 2024)

credit: Tony Webster / Wikimedia Commons · CC BY 2.0
imageAlt: A forest stream near Lake Ouachita, Arkansas; untreated surface-water context, without testing or identification of Giardia in this stream.

title.zh: 蛲虫治疗后又反复，家里的虫卵也要处理
title.en: Pinworm reinfection can start with eggs left around the home

summary.zh: 药物与家庭卫生需要配合，用药是否适合每个人应先咨询。
summary.en: Treatment and household hygiene work together; check who can safely take medicine.

body.zh:
## 虫卵容易经手进入嘴
蛲虫可引起夜间肛周瘙痒和睡眠受扰。抓挠后，虫卵可能留在指甲下，再到衣物、床品、玩具或食物上。吞入虫卵可以再次感染。治疗蛲虫的药物并不能杀死虫卵，因此症状改善后，家庭卫生仍需要继续；夜间瘙痒也不能单独作为确诊依据。

## 一起安排处理，不照搬别人的药
怀疑感染时咨询医生或药师，并询问同住者是否需要同步治疗，即使有人没有症状。幼儿、孕期或哺乳期成员的方案可能不同。饭前、如厕后洗手并清洁指甲，保持指甲短，避免咬指甲，早晨淋浴、换内衣。按指导清洗睡衣、床品和毛巾，不抖动脏织物，不共用毛巾。卫生措施持续多久，也应按专业建议安排，不因暂时不痒就停止。
body.en:
## Eggs can return from hands to mouths
Pinworms, also called threadworms, may cause night-time itching around the anus and disturbed sleep. Scratching transfers eggs under fingernails and onto clothing, bedding, toys or food. Swallowing eggs can cause reinfection. Medicines kill the worms but not their eggs, so hygiene remains necessary after symptoms improve. Itching alone does not confirm infection.

## Coordinate household care
Ask a clinician or pharmacist whether household members need treatment together, including those without symptoms. Young children and pregnant or breastfeeding people may need different advice. Wash hands and clean nails before meals and after using the toilet. Keep nails short, avoid nail-biting, shower in the morning and change underwear. Wash bedding, sleepwear and towels as advised without shaking them. Follow advice about how long hygiene measures should continue.

sources.title: NHS · Threadworms (reviewed 1 December 2023)

credit: Fritz Kleemann / SuSanA Secretariat / Wikimedia Commons · CC BY 2.0
imageAlt: A handwashing basin beside a toilet building in Omaruru, Namibia, with a water container and bucket; general hygiene context.

title.zh: 体癣里的“癣”是真菌感染，不是皮肤里长虫
title.en: Ringworm is a fungal infection, not a worm under the skin

summary.zh: 环形皮疹可以提供线索，但不能拿照片给自己或别人确诊。
summary.en: A ring-shaped rash is a clue, not a diagnosis from a photograph.

body.zh:
## 圆形只是可能出现的外观
体癣是皮肤真菌感染，英文叫ringworm，但并不是虫造成的。皮疹可能呈环状、脱屑或发痒，颜色随肤色不同而变化；也并非每处感染都有完整圆圈。相似皮疹还有其他原因，不凭网上照片给自己确诊，也不要据同学露出的皮肤就给对方贴标签。

## 确认后按部位治疗
请药师或医生评估，再选择适合年龄和感染部位的抗真菌治疗，并按要求完成。接触感染者、动物或受污染的毛巾、床品都可能传播，避免共用个人用品，清洗毛巾床品，不抓挠皮疹。若治疗后仍不改善，应复查；头皮受累或出现斑片脱发时也要就医，不能直接照搬身体皮肤的用药方案。
body.en:
## A circle is only one possible appearance
Body ringworm is a fungal skin infection, not an infestation by worms. A rash may be ring-shaped, scaly or itchy, with colour varying by skin tone. It does not always form a complete circle. Other conditions can look similar. Do not diagnose yourself from an online photograph or label a classmate from a glimpse of their skin.

## Match treatment to the affected area
Ask a pharmacist or clinician about suitable antifungal treatment and complete the advised course. Infection can spread through contact with people, animals or contaminated towels and bedding. Avoid sharing personal items, wash laundry and do not scratch the rash. Seek reassessment if treatment fails. Scalp involvement or patchy hair loss needs medical assessment rather than copying a body-rash treatment.

sources.title: NHS · Ringworm (reviewed 3 August 2023)

credit: Stewart Black / Wikimedia Commons · CC BY 2.0
imageAlt: Clothes hanging on a washing line beneath a partly cloudy sky; neutral laundry context, not a fungal specimen or proof of disinfection.

title.zh: 接触带状疱疹，易感者可能得水痘而不是带状疱疹
title.en: Shingles can pass on chickenpox to susceptible contacts

summary.zh: 带状疱疹来自体内水痘病毒重新活跃，接触传播的是病毒。
summary.en: Shingles is reactivation of the chickenpox virus; contacts do not catch shingles itself.

body.zh:
## 病毒在体内重新活跃
带状疱疹由水痘-带状疱疹病毒重新活跃引起。得过水痘后，病毒会留在体内，以后可能引起带状疱疹。局部刺痛或疼痛可先出现，随后在身体一侧长出疱疹。别人不会从患者那里直接“传染上带状疱疹”，但缺乏水痘免疫力的人接触后可能得水痘。

## 尽早求助，也保护易感接触者
怀疑带状疱疹应尽早就医，青少年尤其需要及时评估。眼周或鼻部出现疹子、视力变化，或免疫功能明显低下时，更应紧急咨询。让皮疹保持清洁、干燥，必要时用不粘敷料遮盖。疱疹仍在渗液期间，避免接触未得过水痘的孕妇、新生儿和免疫功能低下者；治疗需要由医生判断，不自行服用他人的抗病毒药。
body.en:
## The virus becomes active again
Shingles occurs when varicella-zoster virus, the virus that causes chickenpox, reactivates in the body. It can cause tingling or pain followed by a blistering rash, usually on one side. A contact cannot catch shingles itself. Someone without immunity to chickenpox can instead develop chickenpox after exposure.

## Seek early advice and protect contacts
Get prompt medical advice for suspected shingles, especially in a teenager. A rash near the eye or nose, altered vision or severely weakened immunity needs urgent assessment. Keep the rash clean and dry and cover it with a non-stick dressing if needed. While blisters are weeping, avoid contact with newborns, immunocompromised people and pregnant people who have not had chickenpox. A clinician should decide treatment; do not borrow antiviral medicines.

credit: Dr. Erskine Palmer / CDC, B.G. Partin / PHIL #1878 · Public domain
imageAlt: A genuine transmission electron micrograph of a single varicella-zoster virus particle, CDC PHIL 1878, created in 1982; not herpes simplex or a patient diagnosis.

title.zh: 咽痛不自动需要抗生素，怀疑链球菌感染先评估
title.en: A sore throat does not automatically need antibiotics

summary.zh: 链球菌可引起咽炎，但多数咽痛由病毒引起，不能只凭喉咙红来判断。
summary.en: Strep can cause throat infection, but most sore throats are viral and need different care.

body.zh:
## 喉咙红、吞咽痛都有多种原因
链球菌性咽炎是细菌感染，但多数咽痛由病毒引起。喉咙发红、吞咽痛或颈部淋巴结肿大，并不能让自己在家分清病因。抗生素通常不能帮助病毒性咽痛恢复；怀疑细菌感染时，需要医务人员评估是否适合抗生素，别因为症状相似就服用剩药。

## 看变化，也看能否喝水和呼吸
休息、饮水和柔软或偏凉的食物有助于缓解不适，药师可提供适合年龄的止痛建议。咽痛一周仍不改善、反复发作，或出现高热、尿量减少等脱水迹象，应就医。若呼吸困难、无法吞咽、流口水，或严重症状迅速加重，应立即寻求急救。即使已经按咽痛处理，出现这些变化也不能继续在家等待。
body.en:
## A red throat does not identify the cause
Strep throat is a bacterial infection, but viruses cause most sore throats. Redness, painful swallowing or swollen neck glands cannot establish the cause at home. Antibiotics usually do not help viral sore throats. A healthcare professional should assess suspected bacterial infection and decide whether antibiotics are appropriate; similar symptoms are not a reason to use leftover medicine.

## Watch swallowing, hydration and breathing
Rest, fluids and soft or cool foods may ease discomfort. Ask a pharmacist about age-appropriate pain relief. Seek care if symptoms persist beyond a week, recur, or include high fever or reduced urination suggesting dehydration. Difficulty breathing, inability to swallow, drooling or severe symptoms worsening quickly require emergency help rather than continued home treatment.
