title.zh: 耳垢有保护作用，不必用棉签往耳道里清
title.en: Earwax protects the ear: do not push cotton buds inside

summary.zh: 堵塞感需要合适处理，耳烛和自行挖耳并不是可靠办法。
summary.en: A blocked ear needs suitable care, not ear candles or improvised digging.

body.zh:
## 耳垢不是必须清空的脏东西
耳垢帮助阻挡污物和病菌，通常会自行排出。有时积聚会引起堵塞感、耳痛、耳鸣或听力下降，但不能把每次听不清都归因于耳垢。把棉签、手指或其他物品伸进耳道，可能把耳垢推得更深，让堵塞更严重。

## 不用耳烛，有症状先问专业人员
没有证据表明耳烛或家用吸耳装置能有效清除耳垢，不要自行尝试。药师或医生可判断是否需要软化耳垢或专业清除，并帮助选择合适处理。知道或怀疑鼓膜穿孔时，不要自行滴药。堵塞、耳痛或听力问题持续不缓解，尤其堵得几乎听不见时，应就医，而不是继续加力掏耳。
body.en:
## Wax is part of the ear's protection
Earwax helps keep dirt and germs out and usually leaves the ear naturally. A build-up can cause blockage, discomfort, tinnitus or reduced hearing, but hearing difficulty should not automatically be blamed on wax. Pushing cotton buds, fingers or other objects into the canal can pack wax further inside and worsen the blockage.

## Get advice instead of using ear candles
There is no evidence that ear candles or home ear vacuums remove wax effectively. Ask a pharmacist or clinician whether wax-softening treatment or professional removal is suitable. Do not put drops in an ear with a known or suspected perforated eardrum without medical advice. Persistent blockage, pain or hearing problems, especially being unable to hear, needs assessment rather than more digging.

title.zh: 眼睛总流泪，也可能有干眼问题
title.en: Watery eyes can still have a dry-eye problem

summary.zh: 流泪不代表泪膜一定正常，新出现的疼痛或视力变化不能只当眼疲劳。
summary.en: Watering does not rule out dry eye; new pain or visual changes need attention.

body.zh:
## 泪液不足或蒸发太快都可能不舒服
干眼可能让眼睛发涩、像有沙粒、发红，甚至比平常更爱流泪。泪液产生不足或蒸发过快都可能参与其中。长时间盯屏幕不休息、干燥环境及隐形眼镜，都可能增加不适，但这些症状也有其他原因，不能只凭流泪多少自行确诊。

## 可以调整习惯，但别忽略警示症状
使用屏幕时安排休息，减少待在烟尘或过于干燥环境中的时间；戴隐形眼镜不适时先取下，改戴框架眼镜。药师或眼科专业人员可建议合适的润眼产品。若一直不改善，应检查原因。新出现的眼痛，尤其伴红眼或佩戴隐形眼镜时，需要尽快评估；视力变化、畏光疼痛或突然看不见，应立即寻求急诊帮助，不靠继续滴润眼液等待。
body.en:
## More watering does not rule out dryness
Dry eyes can feel gritty, sore or red and may water more than usual. Too few tears or tears evaporating too quickly can contribute. Long screen sessions without breaks, dry environments and contact lenses can increase symptoms. Other eye conditions can feel similar, so the amount of watering cannot establish a diagnosis.

## Adjust habits and recognise warning signs
Take screen breaks and reduce exposure to smoke, dust and dry air. Remove uncomfortable contact lenses and wear glasses. Ask a pharmacist or eye-care professional about suitable lubricating products. Persistent symptoms need assessment. New eye pain, particularly with redness or contact-lens use, needs prompt care. Changes in vision, painful light sensitivity or sudden loss of sight need emergency assessment rather than more lubricating drops.

credit: British Columbia Institute of Technology / Wikimedia Commons · CC BY 4.0
imageAlt: A clinical-skills teaching photograph showing a professional administering an eye drop; generic eye-care context, with no inferred dry-eye diagnosis or claim about the medication.

title.zh: 反复腹痛、排便改变，别直接给自己诊断肠易激综合征
title.en: Repeated gut symptoms need assessment before an IBS label

summary.zh: 肠易激综合征涉及肠脑相互作用，但便血和不明原因消瘦不能简单归入其中。
summary.en: IBS involves gut-brain interaction, but bleeding or unexplained weight loss needs investigation.

body.zh:
## 看的是反复出现的症状组合
肠易激综合征（IBS）可表现为反复腹痛，伴腹泻、便秘或两者交替。它涉及肠道与大脑之间的相互作用，可能改变肠道敏感程度和运动方式；这不等于症状是想象出来的。偶尔肚子不舒服不能确诊，医生需要了解症状规律、病史和家族史，再判断是否需要检查。

## 有些变化不能只当作老毛病
出现直肠出血、黑色柏油样便、贫血或不明原因体重下降，应及时就医，即使以前被诊断过IBS也应说明新变化。就诊时可记录疼痛与排便的关系，以及大便外观和频率的改变，帮助医生判断。不要用网上症状清单代替诊断，也不要在未评估前把所有不适都归咎于压力。
body.en:
## Look at the recurring pattern
Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) can cause repeated abdominal pain with diarrhoea, constipation or both. It involves gut-brain interaction, which can change bowel sensitivity and movement. That does not make symptoms imaginary. An occasional upset stomach cannot confirm IBS. Clinicians review the pattern, medical history and family history before deciding whether tests are needed.

## Report changes that need investigation
Rectal bleeding, black tarry stools, anaemia or unexplained weight loss need medical attention, including new symptoms after an earlier IBS diagnosis. Explain how pain relates to bowel movements and note changes in stool appearance or frequency. These observations help assessment; an online checklist cannot replace it. Do not automatically attribute every symptom to stress.

title.zh: 右上腹持续痛，别只当作吃撑了
title.en: Persistent upper-right abdominal pain deserves attention

summary.zh: 胆结石可能没有症状；疼痛伴发热或黄疸时，需要尽快就医。
summary.en: Gallstones can be silent; pain with fever or jaundice needs urgent assessment.

body.zh:
## 胆管堵塞可引起疼痛
胆结石若堵住胆管，胆汁积聚可引起右上腹疼痛，有时持续数小时，也可能在一顿丰盛的饭后发作。不过，很多胆结石没有症状；有结石也不代表每次腹痛都由它引起。其他疾病可能有相似表现，需要医生评估，不能凭疼痛位置自行确诊。

## 这些伴随症状不要等
腹痛持续数小时，或出现恶心呕吐、发热寒战、皮肤或眼白发黄，应立即就医。茶色尿、浅色大便也值得主动告诉医生。这些变化可能提示胆道堵塞、感染或炎症，拖延可能加重病情。即使曾经痛一阵后自行缓解，也不能据此保证下一次安全，应说明既往发作经过。
body.en:
## A blocked duct can trigger pain
Gallstones blocking a bile duct can cause bile to build up and produce upper-right abdominal pain, sometimes lasting hours or following a heavy meal. Many gallstones cause no symptoms. Having stones does not mean every abdominal pain comes from them: other conditions can feel similar and need clinical assessment. Location alone cannot establish the cause.

## Do not wait with warning signs
Seek care immediately for abdominal pain lasting several hours, nausea or vomiting, fever or chills, or yellow skin or eyes. Mention tea-coloured urine or pale stools too. These changes can signal blockage, infection or inflammation. A previous attack settling by itself does not establish that another is safe; explain earlier episodes to the clinician.

sources.title: NIDDK · Symptoms and causes of gallstones (reviewed November 2017)

imageAlt: A histology micrograph showing dark gallstone fragments centrally and gallbladder mucosa along the lower edge.

title.zh: 便血不能自动归为痔，排便也别一味用力
title.en: Rectal bleeding is not automatically haemorrhoids

summary.zh: 减少便秘和用力排便有帮助，但出血原因仍需评估。
summary.en: Reducing constipation and straining helps, but bleeding still needs assessment.

body.zh:
## 有痔，也可能有别的出血原因
痔可引起肛周瘙痒、肿块或不适。内痔也可能在排便后出鲜血，却不明显疼痛。不过，肠道其他疾病同样会引起直肠出血，不能因为以前有痔或血色鲜红就不检查。出现便血应咨询医生；若伴明显肛门疼痛、腹痛或发热，更应尽快求助。

## 让大便更容易排出
经常用力排便、长期便秘和久坐马桶都可能增加问题。日常可选择富含膳食纤维的食物，按个人健康情况适当饮水，不要为了尽快排完而反复屏气使劲，也别长时间坐在马桶上等待。症状持续不改善时，应让医生评估，而不是一直自行换痔疮药，掩盖仍未查明的出血。
body.en:
## A history of piles does not explain every bleed
Haemorrhoids can cause anal itching, lumps or discomfort. Internal haemorrhoids may produce bright red blood after a bowel movement without much pain. Other bowel conditions also cause rectal bleeding, so previous piles or bright blood cannot establish the cause. Discuss bleeding with a clinician; marked anal pain, abdominal pain or fever warrants prompt care.

## Make bowel movements easier
Straining, chronic constipation and long periods on the toilet can contribute to problems. Choose fibre-rich foods and drink appropriate fluids for your health needs. Avoid repeatedly holding your breath and pushing, or sitting on the toilet for long periods. Persistent symptoms need assessment rather than repeated changes of over-the-counter treatment while bleeding remains unexplained.

title.zh: 饮料无糖，也不等于不会酸蚀牙齿
title.en: Sugar-free drinks can still expose teeth to acid

summary.zh: 糖与酸对牙齿的影响有区别，选择饮料不能只看含糖量。
summary.en: Acid erosion and sugar-related decay are different concerns when choosing drinks.

body.zh:
## 酸蚀和龋齿的过程不同
龋齿与牙菌斑中的细菌利用糖等可发酵碳水化合物产酸有关。酸蚀则涉及食物或饮料中的酸直接作用于牙齿表面。因此，一些无糖汽水虽然减少了糖，酸性仍可能损伤牙齿，不能把“无糖”当成保护牙齿的保证。运动饮料、能量饮料和果汁也值得留意，含糖量不是唯一要看的因素。

## 日常饮水选择白水
把白水作为日常主要饮品，减少频繁接触酸性饮料的机会。唾液有助于保护牙齿，补充适当水分也有意义。牙齿出现不适或担心饮食影响时，可请牙医检查，说明平时喝什么、喝得多频繁，由专业人员判断问题和护理需要。不要仅靠换成无糖饮料，就认为所有牙齿风险都已解决。
body.en:
## Erosion and decay follow different processes
Tooth decay involves plaque bacteria producing acid from fermentable carbohydrates, including sugars. Erosion involves acid from food or drinks acting directly on tooth surfaces. Some sugar-free soft drinks therefore remain acidic enough to harm teeth. A sugar-free label is not a guarantee of dental safety. Sports drinks, energy drinks and fruit juice also deserve attention.

## Choose plain water for everyday drinking
Make plain water your usual drink and reduce frequent exposure to acidic drinks. Saliva helps protect teeth, and adequate hydration supports that protection. Ask a dentist to assess discomfort or concerns, explaining what you drink and how often. Advice should address your dental findings, rather than assume that switching to sugar-free drinks solves every problem.

title.zh: 低血糖要及时处理，意识不清时不能喂糖水
title.en: Low blood glucose needs prompt action, with safe swallowing first

summary.zh: 糖尿病患者应有个人处理计划；嗜睡、昏迷或不能安全吞咽时，立即求助。
summary.en: Have an individual diabetes plan; drowsiness, unconsciousness or unsafe swallowing needs emergency help.

body.zh:
## 识别自己的早期信号
低血糖可能使人手抖、出汗、饥饿、心慌或意识混乱，使用胰岛素或某些降糖药的人尤其需要留意。有些人的预警症状不明显。应与糖尿病团队提前商量何时测血糖、如何处理和复查；清醒且能安全吞咽时，按个人计划及时补充合适的快速升糖食物，不把别人的方案直接照搬。

## 意识不清时，改按急症处理
若患者嗜睡、昏迷、抽搐或无法安全吞咽，不要喂食物、饮料，也不要向嘴里灌糖水，应立即呼叫急救并听从调度指导。若备有医生开具的胰高血糖素，且身边人受过使用培训，可按应急计划使用。留在患者身旁；反复低血糖或察觉不到症状，也需要团队重新评估治疗计划，不自行停药或改量。
body.en:
## Recognise your early warning signs
Low blood glucose can cause shaking, sweating, hunger, palpitations or confusion, particularly with insulin or certain diabetes medicines. Some people have little warning. Agree with your diabetes team when to check glucose, how to respond and when to recheck. If fully alert and swallowing safely, use appropriate fast-acting carbohydrate promptly under your individual plan.

## Unsafe swallowing changes the response
If someone is drowsy, unconscious, having a seizure or unable to swallow safely, give nothing by mouth. Call emergency services immediately and follow dispatcher instructions. Use prescribed glucagon if available and you are trained, following the emergency plan. Stay with the person. Repeated episodes or poor awareness need treatment review; do not change medicines yourself.

sources.title: NIDDK · Low blood glucose (hypoglycemia) (reviewed July 2021)
NHS · Low blood sugar (hypoglycaemia) (reviewed 3 August 2023)

title.zh: 胆固醇偏高常没感觉，家族史值得告诉医生
title.en: High cholesterol often has no symptoms: mention family history

summary.zh: 是否需要检测和干预，应结合个人风险，不靠感觉或极端限食判断。
summary.en: Testing and treatment depend on personal risk, not how you feel or extreme restriction.

body.zh:
## 感觉正常，不能代替血液检查
低密度脂蛋白胆固醇偏高通常没有明显症状，许多人在验血后才知道。遗传因素也会影响胆固醇水平；家里有人胆固醇很高或较早发生心脏病，值得主动告诉医生。不能因为自己年轻、没有不适，就认定无需评估，也不应把异常结果简单归为吃得不够自律。

## 把结果放进整体风险里理解
医生会结合血脂结果、其他疾病和生活情况，讨论适合的饮食、活动及是否需要药物。日常可选择全谷物、蔬果等多样食物，减少富含饱和脂肪的食品，而不是不吃主食或把所有脂肪都去掉。正在长身体的青少年，更应在专业指导下调整。不要因家族史自行吃降脂药，也不要用极端限食替代必要的治疗和复查。
body.en:
## Feeling well cannot replace a blood test
High LDL cholesterol usually causes no obvious symptoms; many people discover it through testing. Inherited factors can affect cholesterol levels. Tell a clinician if relatives have very high cholesterol or heart disease at a young age. Youth or feeling well does not establish low risk, and an abnormal result is not simply evidence of poor discipline.

## Discuss the whole risk picture
Review results alongside other conditions and lifestyle to decide on suitable food choices, activity and possible medicines. Choose varied foods, including whole grains, fruit and vegetables, while limiting foods rich in saturated fat. Do not eliminate whole food groups or all fats. Growing adolescents need appropriate professional guidance. Neither self-prescribed medicines nor extreme restriction replaces assessment and follow-up.

title.zh: 耐药结核，是细菌对药物耐药，不是身体“习惯了药”
title.en: Drug-resistant TB means resistant bacteria, not a resistant body

summary.zh: 需要检测细菌的耐药情况，并由结核病专业团队安排治疗和支持。
summary.en: Laboratory resistance testing and specialist-led treatment guide the response.

body.zh:
## 耐药说的是结核菌
耐药结核意味着某些抗结核药不能有效杀死相关细菌，不是患者的身体“习惯了药”。有人可能直接感染耐药菌，也可能在治疗用药不当、药品供应不足或质量有问题时产生耐药。不能仅凭耐药结果就责备患者没按时服药，更不能把它看作个人品行问题。

## 先检测，再由专业团队选方案
实验室可进一步检测结核菌对哪些药物耐药，帮助团队选择有效治疗。不要自行加药、换药、借用别人的处方或提前停药。出现副作用、拿不到药或难以按时复诊时，应尽快告诉团队，讨论如何处理和获得支持。耐药结核的治疗和随访需要专业人员安排，症状变轻也不等于疗程已经完成。
body.en:
## Resistance describes the TB bacteria
Drug-resistant TB means certain medicines cannot effectively kill the bacteria involved. It does not mean the patient's body has become used to medicine. Someone may acquire resistant bacteria directly, or resistance can develop when treatment is mismanaged, suitable medicines are unavailable or drug quality is poor. A resistance result alone does not justify blaming the patient.

## Testing guides specialist treatment
Laboratories can check which medicines the bacteria resist, helping a TB team select effective treatment. Do not add, swap, borrow or stop medicines yourself. Tell the team promptly about side effects, difficulty obtaining medicines or problems attending appointments so support can be arranged. Specialist follow-up matters; feeling better does not establish that treatment is complete.

title.zh: 鼻塞伴面部胀痛，鼻窦炎不一定需要抗生素
title.en: Sinus pressure does not automatically mean antibiotics

summary.zh: 感冒后鼻窦黏膜肿胀很常见，症状持续或加重时需要评估。
summary.en: Swollen sinuses often follow a cold; persistent or worsening symptoms need assessment.

body.zh:
## 留意鼻部与面部的症状
鼻窦炎是鼻窦内壁肿胀，常发生在感冒或流感之后。鼻塞、流鼻涕、嗅觉减退，以及脸颊、眼周或额头疼痛、压痛，都可能出现。鼻涕变黄或变绿并不能单独说明需要抗生素；很多鼻窦炎由病毒引起，会自行改善。

## 看恢复过程，也看严重程度
休息、补充液体并避开烟雾，有助于缓解不适。多数情况不需要抗生素，是否用药应由专业人员评估。自我护理三周仍未好转，或经常反复，应就医。若症状加重、疼痛难以控制、全身明显不适，或本身免疫功能较弱，应尽快求助，不要一直等待鼻涕颜色改变。
body.en:
## Notice the pattern
Sinusitis is swelling of the sinus lining, often after a cold or flu. It can cause a blocked or runny nose, reduced smell, and pain or tenderness around the cheeks, eyes or forehead. Yellow or green mucus alone does not establish a need for antibiotics. Many episodes involve viruses and improve without them.

## Watch recovery and severity
Rest, drink fluids and avoid smoke. A clinician can assess whether treatment is needed; antibiotics are rarely necessary. Arrange assessment if symptoms have not improved after three weeks of self-care or keep returning. Seek prompt help if symptoms worsen, pain is difficult to control, you feel very unwell, or you have a weakened immune system.

title.zh: 声音嘶哑时少说话，耳语也可能让声带费力
title.en: Rest a hoarse voice without switching to whispers

summary.zh: 喉炎影响发声，持续嘶哑和呼吸、吞咽困难需要不同程度的处理。
summary.en: Laryngitis affects the voice; prolonged hoarseness and breathing or swallowing problems need attention.

body.zh:
## 问题在发声部位
喉炎是喉部或声带受到刺激、肿胀，可让声音沙哑甚至暂时发不出声，也可能伴咳嗽或总想清嗓子。它常与感冒有关，多数在一至两周内缓解，但声音变化并不能说明具体病因。

## 让声音休息，也识别求助信号
尽量减少说话，补充水分，避开烟雾和灰尘。不要喊叫，也不要改成耳语，因为两者都可能增加发声负担。若两周后仍未改善，或发声问题反复出现，应安排评估，而不是持续勉强用嗓。明显疼痛或吞咽困难需要尽快就医；出现呼吸困难应立即寻求急救。
body.en:
## The voice box is irritated
Laryngitis involves irritation or swelling of the voice box or vocal cords. Your voice may become hoarse or disappear temporarily, sometimes with a cough or an urge to clear your throat. It often accompanies a cold and usually settles within one to two weeks, but a voice change alone cannot identify its cause.

## Reduce the work of speaking
Speak as little as practical, drink fluids and avoid smoke or dust. Both shouting and whispering can strain the voice, so neither is a useful workaround. Seek assessment if symptoms persist beyond two weeks or voice problems recur. Very painful or difficult swallowing needs prompt help. Breathing difficulty requires emergency assistance.

sources.title: NHS · Laryngitis (reviewed 17 January 2024)

imageAlt: A microphone against a dark background; neutral voice-use context, not a clinical image or a recommendation to sing or whisper during laryngitis.

title.zh: 孩子感冒后耳痛，要看鼓膜后面的中耳
title.en: Ear pain after a cold may involve the middle ear

summary.zh: 中耳炎与外耳道炎位置不同，抓耳朵本身不能确诊。
summary.en: Middle-ear inflammation differs from an outer-ear infection; ear-tugging alone is not diagnostic.

body.zh:
## 鼓膜两侧不是同一个部位
中耳炎涉及鼓膜后方的空间，可能在呼吸道感染后出现，并伴有积液；它不同于外耳道的炎症。年幼孩子可能抓耳、烦躁、睡不好或发热，也可能出现耳内流液、听声音反应变差或平衡受影响。单靠抓耳不能判断是不是中耳炎。

## 通过检查决定下一步
怀疑感染时应安排评估。医生会用耳镜检查鼓膜，有时还需检查鼓膜活动度或中耳积液。治疗要结合年龄、症状和检查结果决定，有些情况可先观察，并不是每次耳痛都需要抗生素。若观察期间未好转，或耳痛、听力问题持续，应按约复诊；向医生说明症状变化和持续时间。
body.en:
## Behind the eardrum
Otitis media affects the space behind the eardrum, sometimes with fluid after a respiratory infection. It is different from inflammation of the outer ear canal. Young children may tug an ear, become irritable, sleep poorly or develop fever. Ear discharge, reduced response to sounds or balance problems can also occur. Tugging alone cannot establish the diagnosis.

## Examination guides the next step
Arrange assessment for suspected infection. A clinician examines the eardrum and may check its movement or test for middle-ear fluid. Age, symptoms and examination findings guide whether observation or treatment is appropriate; antibiotics are not automatic. Follow the agreed review plan if symptoms do not improve, and report ongoing pain or hearing difficulties.

title.zh: 耳鸣持续要检查，突然听力下降不能等
title.en: Persistent tinnitus needs assessment; sudden hearing loss cannot wait

summary.zh: 耳鸣不只有铃声，随脉搏跳动或伴突发听力变化需要及时求助。
summary.en: Tinnitus can sound like buzzing or whooshing; pulse-linked sounds and sudden hearing changes need care.

body.zh:
## 没有外部声源，也听到了声音
耳鸣是没有对应外部声源时听到声音，可能像铃声、嗡嗡声或呼呼声，出现在一侧或两侧，也可能时有时无。它有多种可能原因。若持续出现、逐渐加重，或影响睡眠和注意力，应安排耳部及听力评估，不必独自猜测原因。

## 分清需要多快求助
声音与脉搏同步跳动时，应尽快就医评估。耳鸣伴突然听力下降、面部无力或眩晕，或发生在头部受伤后，应立即寻求急诊帮助。普通持续耳鸣可尝试轻柔背景声和规律作息来减轻困扰，但不要用大音量耳机遮盖它，也不要让这些办法延误检查。
body.en:
## Sound without an outside source
Tinnitus means hearing a sound without a matching external source. It may ring, buzz or whoosh in one or both ears, constantly or intermittently. There are several possible causes. Arrange an ear and hearing assessment if it persists, gets worse, or affects sleep or concentration, rather than trying to identify the cause yourself.

## Some changes need faster help
Seek an urgent appointment if the sound beats with your pulse. Tinnitus with sudden hearing loss, facial weakness or vertigo, or following a head injury, requires emergency assessment. For ongoing symptoms, gentle background sound and a regular sleep routine may ease the disturbance. Avoid loud headphone masking and do not let coping measures delay assessment.

title.zh: 口腔白斑别自行认定鹅口疮，吸入器护理也重要
title.en: White mouth patches need assessment, not an automatic thrush label

summary.zh: 鹅口疮是真菌感染，口腔不适需要判断原因，含激素吸入器用后应注意口腔护理。
summary.en: Thrush is a fungal infection; mouth symptoms need assessment and steroid inhalers need appropriate aftercare.

body.zh:
## 白色改变不等于同一种病
口腔鹅口疮是真菌感染，可能出现白色斑块、灼热或疼痛、口角裂开、味觉改变，也可能影响进食。单看舌头发白或一张照片不能确诊。口腔持续疼痛或白斑应请医生或口腔专业人员检查，不要自行把所有白色改变都当作鹅口疮并反复用药。

## 把吸入器护理纳入日常
温和清洁牙齿和口腔，并向专业人员说明正在使用的药物。含激素的吸入器可能增加口腔真菌感染风险，使用后按指导用水漱口有助于预防。请药师或护士检查吸入方法和器具护理；持续不适时咨询治疗方案，不要自行改变原有的处方用药。
body.en:
## White patches need a closer look
Oral thrush is a fungal infection. It can cause white patches, burning or soreness, cracked mouth corners and altered taste, sometimes making eating uncomfortable. A white tongue or photograph alone cannot confirm it. Have persistent patches or mouth pain assessed by a clinician or dental professional instead of repeatedly treating every white change as thrush.

## Include inhaler aftercare
Keep teeth and the mouth gently clean, and explain which medicines you use. Inhalers containing a steroid can increase the risk of oral thrush; rinsing with water after use helps prevent it. Ask a pharmacist or nurse to check technique and device care. Discuss ongoing symptoms rather than changing prescribed treatment yourself.

sources.title: Kent Community Health NHS Foundation Trust · Looking after your mouth and oral health (published and edited 18 July 2024)
University Hospitals Sussex NHS Foundation Trust · Inhaler technique: Accuhaler (published October 2021; review due October 2024)

title.zh: 唇疱疹发作时暂停亲吻，尤其别亲婴儿
title.en: Avoid kissing during a cold sore, especially kissing a baby

summary.zh: 唇疱疹与普通口腔溃疡不同，从刺痛开始就可能具有传染性。
summary.en: Cold sores differ from ordinary mouth ulcers and can spread from the first tingling stage.

body.zh:
## 先刺痛，随后可能起疱
唇疱疹由单纯疱疹病毒引起，常先有刺痛、痒或灼热感，随后在嘴唇或面部出现小水疱，再结痂。它不同于普通口腔溃疡。病毒很常见，有些人在儿童时期就已接触，发作不该成为责备或羞辱的理由。

## 从先兆期就减少接触传播
从最初刺痛到完全愈合，都应避免亲吻及口部亲密接触。尤其不要亲吻婴儿，因为新生儿感染可能很严重。不要抠破水疱，触碰后洗手。若十天后仍未开始愈合、病灶很大或很痛，或本人免疫功能较弱，应咨询医生，不必等到反复破溃才求助。
body.en:
## Tingling can come before blisters
Cold sores are caused by herpes simplex virus. Tingling, itching or burning may precede small blisters around the lips or face, which later crust. They differ from ordinary mouth ulcers. The virus is common, and exposure can happen in childhood; an episode is not a reason for blame or shame.

## Reduce contact until fully healed
Cold sores can spread from the first tingling until complete healing. Avoid kissing and oral intimate contact throughout that period. Never kiss a baby while you have a cold sore, because neonatal infection can be serious. Avoid picking and wash hands after touching it. Seek advice for sores not starting to heal within ten days, very large or painful sores, or weakened immunity.

title.zh: 银屑病不会传染，脱屑也不能只靠照片定病因
title.en: Psoriasis is not contagious, and scaling alone is not a diagnosis

summary.zh: 皮损、指甲和关节变化都值得告诉医生，治疗需要结合具体情况。
summary.en: Skin, nail and joint changes all matter when planning individual care.

body.zh:
## 与免疫活动有关的皮肤病
银屑病是可反复发作的长期炎症性皮肤病，与免疫系统过度活跃有关，不会通过日常接触传染。皮肤可出现增厚、脱屑、瘙痒或疼痛，颜色因肤色而不同。其他皮肤问题也可能脱屑，因此不能凭照片把自己或同学的皮疹认定为银屑病。

## 检查不只看一块皮肤
医生会结合皮损形态、分布及相关症状评估。说明它是否影响睡眠、上学或活动，也要报告指甲凹点、翘起，以及关节疼痛、肿胀或晨僵。温和保湿可减少干裂，具体治疗应结合部位和严重程度决定。不要因皮疹相似就借用他人的处方，也不需要因担心传染而回避正常接触。
body.en:
## An inflammatory skin condition
Psoriasis is a long-term condition that can flare and settle, linked to overactivity of the immune system. It is not contagious. Patches may be thickened, scaly, itchy or painful, with colour varying across skin tones. Scaling also occurs in other conditions, so a photograph is not enough to label your own or someone else's rash.

## Look beyond one patch
A clinician considers the appearance, distribution and associated symptoms. Explain effects on sleep, school or activities, and report nail pitting or lifting, joint pain, swelling or morning stiffness. Moisturising can reduce dryness and cracking. Treatment depends on the areas and severity involved; do not borrow another person's prescription because their rash looks similar.

sources.title: British Association of Dermatologists · Psoriasis: an overview (updated August 2023)

credit: Wellcome Library, London / Wikimedia Commons · CC BY 4.0
imageAlt: Historical illustration of a vertical skin section from a longstanding psoriasis patch, shown at 300 diameters in an 1878-1879 medical journal; not a modern micrograph.

title.zh: 风团不一定是食物过敏，呼吸困难却不能等
title.en: Hives are not always a food allergy, but breathing trouble is urgent

summary.zh: 荨麻疹可有多种诱因，嘴唇、舌头或喉咙突然肿胀应立即求助。
summary.en: Hives have several triggers; sudden swelling of the lips, tongue or throat needs emergency help.

body.zh:
## 隆起的痒疹有多种诱因
荨麻疹常表现为隆起、发痒的风团，形状和大小可以不同。食物或药物过敏可能诱发，感染、冷热和皮肤受压等也可能有关。仅凭一次皮疹，不能认定某种食物就是原因，也不要自行大范围忌口。

## 皮疹之外的变化更重要
若反复发作、扩散或持续不缓解，应咨询专业人员；选择止痒药也应先确认是否适合本人。嘴唇、口腔、舌头或喉咙突然肿胀，呼吸或吞咽困难、喉咙发紧，以及晕厥或意识混乱，可能提示严重过敏反应。出现这些情况应立即呼叫当地急救，不要等待皮疹消退，也不要先观察普通止痒药是否起效。
body.en:
## Raised itchy patches have several triggers
Hives, or urticaria, produce raised, itchy patches in different shapes and sizes. Food or medicine allergy can trigger them, but infections, heat, cold and pressure on skin can also be involved. One episode does not identify a particular food as the cause, and is not a reason for broad dietary restrictions.

## Watch for symptoms beyond the skin
Seek advice for recurring, spreading or persistent hives, and check whether any itch medicine is suitable for you. Sudden swelling of the lips, mouth, tongue or throat, breathing or swallowing difficulty, throat tightness, faintness or confusion may signal anaphylaxis. Call local emergency services immediately. Do not wait for the rash to settle or for ordinary itch treatment to work.

sources.title: NHS · Hives (reviewed 26 April 2024)

title.zh: 冻疮发痒别猛烤，手脚要缓慢回暖
title.en: Warm chilblains gradually instead of holding them against a heater

summary.zh: 寒冷后的红紫肿痒与小血管反应有关，保持温暖干燥并保护皮肤。
summary.en: Cold-related itchy swellings involve small blood vessels; keep skin warm, dry and protected.

body.zh:
## 受冷之后的小血管反应
冻疮可表现为手指、脚趾等部位发痒、疼痛和肿起，颜色可能偏红、蓝或紫。它与小血管对温度变化的异常反应有关，身体健康的人也可能出现。它不同于组织真正冻结的冻伤，不应把受冷后的所有皮肤损伤都当成普通冻疮。

## 保暖，也避免突然加热
在寒冷潮湿环境中，用手套、袜子和合适衣物保持温暖干燥。进屋后让手脚逐渐回暖，不要直接靠火炉、暖气或热水猛烫，也不要揉搓、抓挠。皮肤完整时可温和保湿。若皮肤破损、担心感染，或症状反复、令人困扰，应咨询医生；糖尿病或循环不良者尤其需要及时获得建议。
body.en:
## A reaction after cold exposure
Chilblains are itchy or painful swellings, often on fingers or toes, which may look red, blue or purple. They involve an abnormal small-blood-vessel response to temperature changes and can affect otherwise healthy people. They are different from frostbite, where tissue freezes; not every cold-related skin injury should be treated as a routine chilblain.

## Warm gradually and protect the skin
Keep hands and feet warm and dry with suitable gloves, socks and clothing. Rewarm gradually indoors, not against a fire or radiator or in hot water. Avoid rubbing and scratching; gently moisturise intact skin. Ask for advice about broken skin, suspected infection or troublesome recurrence, particularly if you have diabetes or poor circulation.

sources.title: The Dudley Group NHS Foundation Trust · Chilblains, version 1 (originated September 2024)

imageAlt: A black winter glove against snow in Jerusalem; neutral cold-weather clothing context, not visible chilblains or a claim about a brand's protective performance.

title.zh: 受冷后皮肤发硬麻木，要警惕真正的冻伤
title.en: Numb, hard skin after cold exposure may be frostbite

summary.zh: 冻伤涉及组织冻结，需要尽快评估，揉搓和直接加热可能加重损伤。
summary.en: Frostbite involves frozen tissue and needs prompt care; rubbing and direct heat can worsen injury.

body.zh:
## 麻木不代表没有损伤
冻伤是组织冻结造成的损伤，常累及手指、脚趾、鼻子或耳朵。皮肤可能发白或灰黄、摸起来异常坚硬或像蜡，并出现麻木。感觉减弱可能让人忽略问题，并不说明损伤轻。发现可疑变化时应脱离寒冷并尽快就医。

## 保护患处，安排医疗帮助
进入温暖的避风处，避免不必要地用受伤的脚行走。不要用雪揉搓、按摩，也不要使用暖气、火炉或加热垫直接加热，麻木的皮肤容易被烫伤。若医疗帮助暂时无法到达，应联系救援人员指导复温。没有全身失温迹象、且能确保患处不会再次冻结时，可用温而不烫的水帮助复温；复温后再冻结会加重损伤，无法避免时不要贸然开始。复温不能代替专业评估。
body.en:
## Numbness can hide injury
Frostbite is damage caused by tissue freezing, often affecting fingers, toes, the nose or ears. Skin may look white or greyish-yellow, feel unusually firm or waxy, and become numb. Reduced feeling can conceal the injury rather than indicate that it is minor. Leave the cold and seek prompt medical assessment for these signs.

## Protect the area while arranging help
Move into warm shelter and avoid unnecessary walking on affected feet. Do not rub with snow, massage, or apply a radiator, stove or heating pad: numb skin burns easily. If care is delayed, seek rescue guidance. With no hypothermia and no risk of refreezing, warm, not hot, water can help thaw the area. Refreezing worsens injury; do not begin thawing where this cannot be prevented. Rewarming does not replace assessment.

sources.title: CDC · Extreme Cold: A Prevention Guide to Promote Your Personal Health and Safety (2005 archived edition, frostbite section)
Wilderness Medical Society · Clinical practice guidelines for frostbite: 2024 update (5 April 2024)

credit: Jonathan Cutrer / Wikimedia Commons · CC BY 2.0
imageAlt: Snow-dusted winter boots and trouser legs at Ski Apache, New Mexico; neutral winter-outdoor context without any inference of frostbite or measured protection.

title.zh: 上臂粗糙小颗粒，别靠猛搓处理毛周角化
title.en: Rough upper-arm bumps need gentle care, not hard scrubbing

summary.zh: 毛周角化与毛囊口角蛋白堆积有关，不是传染性感染。
summary.en: Keratosis pilaris involves keratin blocking follicles, not a contagious infection.

body.zh:
## 毛囊口的角蛋白堆积
毛周角化常在上臂、大腿或臀部形成细小、粗糙的凸起，摸起来干燥，一般不痛，有时会痒，冬季可能更明显。它与角蛋白堵塞毛囊有关，不是会传染给别人的感染。不过，不能只凭这些描述认定所有小疙瘩都是毛周角化。

## 温和护理比反复摩擦更合适
使用温和、无香味的清洁用品，洗澡水不要过热，并注意保湿。不要挤、抠或用粗糙工具大力搓洗；皮肤受刺激后未必更平滑。不必为了外观一味加强清洁。如果凸起明显发痒、发炎、护理后仍无改善，或让你感到困扰，可请药师或医生确认情况，再讨论适合自己的护理方式。
body.en:
## Keratin blocks the follicles
Keratosis pilaris commonly causes tiny rough bumps on the upper arms, thighs or buttocks. They can feel dry, are usually painless, sometimes itch, and may be more noticeable in winter. Keratin builds up in hair follicles; this is not a contagious infection. However, that description cannot confirm that every small bump has the same cause.

## Keep care gentle
Use mild, unperfumed cleansers, avoid very hot showers and moisturise the skin. Do not pick, squeeze or scrub hard with rough tools; irritation will not reliably make the surface smoother. There is no need to keep intensifying washing for appearance alone. Ask a pharmacist or clinician about itchy, inflamed, persistent or bothersome bumps before choosing further care.

sources.title: NHS · Keratosis pilaris (reviewed 4 July 2024)

imageAlt: A dollop of white moisturizer photographed as a still life, with no visible brand; neutral skin-care context, not proof of keratosis pilaris treatment efficacy.

title.zh: 怕冷又疲倦，需要查甲状腺吗
title.en: Feeling cold and tired may warrant a thyroid check

summary.zh: 甲减的症状并不特异，确诊需要结合病史和检查。
summary.en: Underactive thyroid symptoms overlap with other conditions; assessment needs more than a checklist.

body.zh:
## 身体变慢的线索
甲状腺功能减退，简称甲减，是甲状腺激素不足，可使身体多种功能减慢。疲倦、怕冷、体重增加、便秘和皮肤干燥都可能出现。不过这些表现也有其他原因，不能把几项症状对上号就认定甲减；单凭体重变化也无法判断。

## 先检查，再决定治疗
持续不适时应就医，说明症状、家族病史、正在使用的药物和补充剂。医生会结合病史、查体和甲状腺血液检查判断，必要时进一步寻找病因。若需补充甲状腺激素，应按处方使用并按要求复查，不自行停药或调整。不要把碘片、海带补充剂当作通用的“补甲状腺”办法；过量碘可能使某些自身免疫性甲状腺疾病恶化。
body.en:
## Clues to slower body functions
Hypothyroidism means the thyroid produces too little thyroid hormone, slowing many body functions. Tiredness, feeling cold, weight gain, constipation and dry skin can occur. These symptoms have other possible causes, however. Matching several items on a checklist does not establish a diagnosis, and weight change alone cannot identify thyroid disease.

## Check before choosing treatment
Seek assessment for persistent symptoms. Describe your symptoms, family history, medicines and supplements. Clinicians use history, examination and thyroid blood tests, with further investigation when needed. If thyroid hormone replacement is prescribed, take it as directed and attend monitoring rather than changing or stopping it yourself. Avoid treating yourself with iodine or kelp supplements: excessive iodine can worsen some autoimmune thyroid conditions.

sources.title: NIDDK · Hypothyroidism (last reviewed March 2021)

credit: OpenStax College / Wikimedia Commons · CC BY 3.0
imageAlt: A labelled teaching illustration showing the thyroid gland, larynx, trachea and nearby arteries from the front.

title.zh: 心慌、怕热、体重下降，别只归因于压力
title.en: Palpitations, heat intolerance and weight loss deserve assessment

summary.zh: 甲亢与甲减的激素变化不同，类似症状仍需检查辨别。
summary.en: An overactive thyroid differs from an underactive one, but symptoms alone cannot confirm either.

body.zh:
## 激素过多时的表现
甲状腺功能亢进，简称甲亢，涉及甲状腺激素过多，与激素不足的甲减不同。心跳快或不规则、手抖、怕热、出汗、睡不好，以及食欲增加却体重下降，都可能出现。这些表现也可能来自其他疾病，不能一概归为焦虑，也不能据此自行确诊甲亢。

## 检查也要寻找原因
持续出现上述不适时，应就医说明症状，并带上药物和补充剂清单。医生会结合病史、查体、甲状腺血液检查，必要时安排影像检查。格雷夫斯病、结节或甲状腺炎等原因会影响后续处理，治疗并非人人相同。不要自行服用甲状腺药物，也别用碘或海藻补充剂尝试纠正；额外的碘可能使问题加重。
body.en:
## When thyroid hormone is excessive
Hyperthyroidism involves too much thyroid hormone, unlike the hormone shortage in hypothyroidism. A fast or irregular heartbeat, trembling hands, heat intolerance, sweating, poor sleep and weight loss despite increased appetite can occur. Other illnesses can cause similar symptoms. Neither assuming anxiety nor diagnosing an overactive thyroid from symptoms alone is reliable.

## Establish the cause as well
Seek assessment for persistent symptoms and bring a list of medicines and supplements. Clinicians consider your history, examination, thyroid blood tests and sometimes imaging. Graves' disease, thyroid nodules and thyroid inflammation can require different approaches; treatment is individual. Do not start thyroid medicines yourself or try iodine or seaweed supplements to correct the problem. Extra iodine can make it worse.

sources.title: NIDDK · Hyperthyroidism (last reviewed August 2021)

credit: Governo do Estado de São Paulo / Wikimedia Commons · CC BY 2.0
imageAlt: Rows of capped blood-sample tubes in laboratory racks at Hospital das Clínicas, São Paulo.

title.zh: 手脚麻、走路不稳，也要留意维生素B12缺乏
title.en: Vitamin B12 deficiency can affect sensation and balance

summary.zh: 没有贫血也可能出现神经症状，持续不适应尽早评估。
summary.en: Neurological symptoms can occur without anaemia and deserve prompt assessment.

body.zh:
## 不只是疲倦
维生素B12缺乏可引起疲倦、乏力、舌头红痛，也可能出现手脚麻木、针刺感、肌肉无力，以及平衡或协调困难。神经症状即使没有贫血也可能发生。单靠感觉无法确定病因，相似症状并不都意味着缺维生素。

## 不用补充剂代替评估
若上述症状持续出现，应尽早就医，说明何时开始、是否加重，以及是否影响走路或日常活动。医生可结合症状和血液检查评估是否存在B12缺乏。不要仅凭网上的症状清单给自己下结论，再反复尝试不同维生素而拖延检查。治疗需要专业安排；有些未经治疗的神经问题可能无法完全恢复，早发现、及时处理更有利于减少长期影响。
body.en:
## More than tiredness
Vitamin B12 deficiency can cause tiredness, weakness and a sore, red tongue. It can also cause numbness, pins and needles, muscle weakness, and problems with balance or coordination. Neurological symptoms may develop even without anaemia. These sensations cannot identify the cause by themselves: similar problems do not always mean vitamin deficiency.

## Do not substitute supplements for assessment
Seek prompt medical advice for persistent symptoms. Explain when they began, whether they are worsening and whether walking or daily activities are affected. Clinicians can assess symptoms and blood tests for possible B12 deficiency. Avoid diagnosing yourself from an online checklist and repeatedly trying vitamins instead of seeking care. Treatment needs professional guidance; some untreated neurological problems may become irreversible.

sources.title: NHS · Vitamin B12 or folate deficiency anaemia: symptoms (reviewed 20 February 2023)

imageAlt: A cooked salmon portion served on quinoa and vegetables on a white plate.

title.zh: 头两侧发紧，可能是紧张型头痛吗
title.en: A tightening headache on both sides may be tension-type

summary.zh: 疼痛特点有助于判断类型，但突然剧痛或神经异常不能等待。
summary.en: Pain patterns help assessment, while sudden severe pain or neurological changes need urgent care.

body.zh:
## 感觉像压着或勒着
紧张型头痛通常累及两侧，呈压迫或紧箍感，程度多为轻至中度，日常活动一般不会使它加重。偏头痛更常表现为搏动性疼痛，活动时加重，并可伴恶心或怕光、怕声音。两者不能只凭疼痛位置区分，新出现或反复头痛仍应接受评估。

## 记录变化，别不断加止痛药
记录头痛发生时间、持续多久、严重程度和用药情况，有助于医生判断。频繁使用止痛药本身也可能带来药物过度使用性头痛，反复需要用药时应咨询，而不是不断加药。若突然出现迅速达到高峰的剧烈头痛，或伴说话、走路异常等神经症状，应立即寻求急诊帮助；发热伴颈部僵硬也需紧急评估。
body.en:
## Pressing rather than throbbing
Tension-type headache usually affects both sides, feels pressing or tightening, and is mild or moderate. Routine activity does not usually worsen it. Migraine more often throbs, worsens with activity and brings nausea or sensitivity to light or sound. Location alone cannot distinguish them. New or recurring headaches still need assessment.

## Record changes and medicine use
Keep a diary of timing, duration, severity and medicines taken. Frequent painkiller use can itself contribute to medication-overuse headache; seek advice rather than repeatedly adding medicines. A sudden severe headache that rapidly reaches maximum intensity needs emergency assessment, as do headaches with new speech or walking difficulties. Fever with neck stiffness also requires urgent evaluation.

sources.title: NHS Wales · Headache pathway, version 1.2 (last review April 2019; official disclosure PDF)

imageAlt: An unoccupied desk with a laptop, adjustable lamp, stacks of books and documents.

title.zh: 家人梦游时，先把夜间环境变安全
title.en: Make the night-time environment safer for someone who sleepwalks

summary.zh: 梦游发生在未完全清醒时，需要保护和评估，不应责怪。
summary.en: Sleepwalking happens without full wakefulness and calls for safety, not blame.

body.zh:
## 人在走动，不代表已经清醒
梦游属于非快速眼动睡眠期的异态睡眠，可在从深睡眠部分醒来时发生，常见于夜间较早阶段。此时并未完全清醒，不应把这种行为当作故意捣乱或加以责怪。睡眠不足、作息不规律、压力及其他睡眠问题都可能增加发生机会。

## 减少跌倒和外出的风险
清理地面杂物，移走可能伤人的物品，保护尖锐家具边角，避免使用高床或双层床。若有走出家门的风险，可考虑门窗报警装置。保持充足、规律的睡眠。若夜间行为令人担忧、有受伤风险或影响睡眠，应向医生描述具体经过；医生可能进一步评估其他睡眠问题，并检查药物是否有关，不自行调整处方。
body.en:
## Moving does not mean fully awake
Sleepwalking is a non-REM parasomnia: it can happen when someone partly wakes from deep sleep, often earlier in the night. The person is not fully awake, so do not treat the behaviour as deliberate misbehaviour or blame them. Insufficient sleep, irregular schedules, stress and other sleep disturbances can increase episodes.

## Reduce injury and wandering risks
Clear floor clutter, remove hazardous objects, pad sharp furniture edges and avoid high or bunk beds. Consider door or window alarms if wandering outside is possible. Keep sleep regular and adequate. Discuss concerning episodes, injury risks or disrupted sleep with a clinician. Describe what happens; assessment may include other sleep disorders and a medication review rather than changing prescriptions yourself.

sources.title: American Thoracic Society · Parasomnias and Safety Precautions: A Patient and Family Handout (published 30 January 2024)

imageAlt: An unoccupied bedroom with a made bed, computer desk, windows and a chair.

title.zh: 跨时区后睡不着，是身体的时钟还没跟上
title.en: After crossing time zones, your body clock needs time to adjust

summary.zh: 时差反应与睡眠节律错位有关，抵达后的光照和作息有帮助。
summary.en: Jet lag involves disrupted sleep timing; daylight and local routines can help adjustment.

body.zh:
## 不只是旅途累了
跨时区飞行后，身体原有的睡眠节律与目的地时间可能对不上。到了当地晚上难入睡、早晨难醒，白天疲倦或难以集中注意力，都可能是时差反应，有时还伴消化不适。这与长途旅行的一般疲劳有所区别，通常会在几天内逐渐改善。

## 让作息跟着当地时间走
出发前保证休息，并可逐渐把入睡时间向目的地靠近。飞行途中喝水，避免过多酒精和咖啡因；若对应目的地夜间，可尝试睡觉。抵达后按当地时间安排睡眠，白天接触自然光，避免长时间白天补觉。不要因为第一晚睡不好就自行依赖安眠药；若正在考虑药物，应先咨询医生。
body.en:
## More than a tiring journey
After flying across time zones, your established sleep rhythm may no longer match destination time. Trouble falling asleep at night, difficulty waking, daytime tiredness and poor concentration can follow, sometimes with digestive upset. This timing mismatch differs from ordinary travel fatigue. Jet lag usually improves over a few days.

## Work towards local time
Rest before travelling and gradually move bedtime towards your destination's schedule. During the flight, drink water and avoid excessive alcohol or caffeine; try sleeping if it is night at your destination. After arrival, follow local sleeping hours, spend time outside in daylight and avoid long daytime sleeps. Do not start relying on sleeping tablets after one difficult night; discuss medicines with a clinician first.

sources.title: NHS · Jet lag (reviewed 31 May 2023)

imageAlt: A close view of an airport display listing flight destinations including Detroit and Tokyo.

title.zh: 丙肝可以没有症状，检测有助于及早治疗
title.en: Hepatitis C can be silent, and testing can open the way to treatment

summary.zh: 丙肝主要经血液传播，多数感染可在专业治疗下治愈。
summary.en: Hepatitis C spreads through blood contact, and professional treatment can cure most infections.

body.zh:
## 没有不适也可能感染
丙型肝炎病毒可损伤肝脏，很多感染者没有明显症状。它通过接触感染者的血液传播，例如共用注射器或使用未充分清洁的穿刺工具。握手、拥抱、坐在一起或共用餐具不会传播丙肝，无需因此疏远他人。

## 询问是否需要检测
若曾有可能的血液暴露，应咨询医生是否需要检测，不必等到出现不适。血液检查可帮助区分是否曾接触病毒、目前是否仍有感染，医生会解释结果。多数感染可通过抗病毒治疗治愈，但用药应结合肝脏情况和其他药物专业安排。不要自行购买疗程或借用别人的药；按要求完成治疗和复查，也不要共用针具或可能沾血的剃须刀等物品。
body.en:
## Infection may have no obvious symptoms
Hepatitis C can damage the liver, yet many infected people feel well. The virus spreads through contact with infected blood, including shared injecting equipment or inadequately cleaned piercing instruments. It does not spread through handshakes, hugs, sitting together or sharing eating utensils. Ordinary contact is no reason to exclude someone.

## Ask about testing
Discuss possible blood exposure with a clinician rather than waiting for symptoms. Blood tests help distinguish past exposure from infection that is still present; ask what your results mean. Antiviral treatment can cure most infections, but liver health and other medicines affect professional decisions. Do not buy a course or borrow medicines yourself. Complete advised treatment and follow-up, and avoid sharing needles or blood-contaminated razors.

sources.title: NIDDK · Hepatitis C (last reviewed December 2024)

imageAlt: A close view of a donor's arm with blood-collection needle tubing and a tourniquet.

title.zh: 梅毒的疮或皮疹消退，不等于感染痊愈
title.en: A syphilis sore or rash disappearing does not mean the infection is cured

summary.zh: 无症状阶段仍可能需要治疗，检测和随访比观察外观可靠。
summary.en: Symptom-free infection can still need treatment; testing and follow-up matter more than appearance.

body.zh:
## 症状可以变，也可以暂时没有
梅毒是细菌感染，可出现生殖器、肛周或口腔溃疡，早期溃疡常不痛；之后也可能出现皮疹。溃疡或皮疹消失并不代表病菌已清除，感染可进入没有明显症状的潜伏阶段。不能只凭皮肤恢复或网上照片判断是否感染、是否痊愈。

## 检测与治疗应有连续安排
若怀疑暴露或发现可疑症状，应尽早到医疗机构评估。医生会结合检查与血液检测判断，并安排治疗及复查。不要自行服用剩余抗生素，也别因症状改善就中断照护。性伴侣可能也需要保密的告知、评估和治疗；安全套可降低风险，但未覆盖的感染部位仍可能传播。感染不是道德评价，寻求帮助时应获得尊重和隐私保护。
body.en:
## Symptoms can change or disappear
Syphilis is a bacterial infection that may cause genital, anal or mouth sores, often painless initially, and later a rash. Disappearing sores or rash do not prove the bacteria have cleared: infection can enter a latent stage without obvious symptoms. Neither healed skin nor online photographs can establish infection or cure.

## Arrange testing and continuing care
Seek clinical assessment after suspected exposure or concerning symptoms. Examination and blood tests guide diagnosis, treatment and follow-up. Do not take leftover antibiotics or abandon care when symptoms improve. Partners may need confidential notification, evaluation and treatment too. Condoms reduce risk, but uncovered infected areas can still transmit syphilis. Infection is not a moral judgement; care should respect privacy and dignity.

sources.title: CDC · Sexually Transmitted Infections Treatment Guidelines, 2021: syphilis and prevention (MMWR, 23 July 2021)

credit: CDC / C. W. Hubbard / CDC PHIL; Wikimedia Commons · Public domain
imageAlt: Bright spiral-shaped Treponema pallidum organisms against a dark background in a fluorescent-antibody-treated control specimen.

title.zh: 淋病不一定有症状，不靠自行吃抗生素处理
title.en: Gonorrhoea may have no symptoms and needs more than borrowed antibiotics

summary.zh: 按暴露部位检测、专业治疗和性伴侣照护，有助于减少漏诊和再次感染。
summary.en: Testing relevant exposure sites, professional treatment and partner care help prevent missed infection and reinfection.

body.zh:
## 没有疼痛也不能排除
淋病可累及生殖道、直肠或咽喉。部分感染没有明显症状，咽部感染尤其容易没有不适；有人则出现排尿疼痛或异常分泌物。不能用“没感觉”排除感染。就诊时说明接触方式，有助于医生选择尿液或相应部位的拭子检查，而不是只检查一个部位。

## 耐药使规范治疗更重要
淋病奈瑟菌可能对抗生素耐药，自行服用剩药或借药可能无法治愈，并延误合适治疗。确诊后遵照专业方案，若症状持续应复诊，并按指导完成随访。性伴侣也可能需要评估和治疗；恢复性接触的时间应遵从医生建议。正确、持续使用安全套能降低传播风险，但不能代替有指征时的检测，也不代表风险完全消失。
body.en:
## No discomfort does not exclude infection
Gonorrhoea can affect the genital tract, rectum or throat. Some infections cause no obvious symptoms, especially in the throat; others cause painful urination or unusual discharge. Feeling well cannot exclude infection. Explain sexual exposures so clinicians can select urine tests or swabs from relevant sites rather than testing only one location.

## Resistance makes proper treatment important
Gonorrhoea bacteria can resist antibiotics. Leftover or borrowed medicines may fail and delay appropriate care. Follow professional treatment advice, return if symptoms persist and complete recommended follow-up. Partners may also need evaluation and treatment; follow advice about when sexual contact can resume. Correct, consistent condom use reduces transmission risk but does not replace indicated testing or remove every risk.

sources.title: CDC · Sexually Transmitted Infections Treatment Guidelines, 2021: gonococcal infections and prevention (MMWR, 23 July 2021)

credit: CDC / Joe Miller / CDC PHIL; Wikimedia Commons · Public domain
imageAlt: A photomicrograph showing numerous pink, Gram-negative Neisseria gonorrhoeae diplococci.

title.zh: 结核预防性治疗，用药前要先排除活动性结核病
title.en: Before TB preventive treatment, clinicians must exclude active disease

summary.zh: 预防性治疗旨在降低发病风险，是否适合及如何完成需专业评估。
summary.en: Preventive treatment lowers the risk of TB disease, with eligibility and completion assessed professionally.

body.zh:
## 预防发病也需要先评估
结核潜伏感染的预防性治疗，旨在降低以后发展为结核病的风险。它并不是看到一张阳性结果就自行吃药。开始前，医务人员必须评估并排除活动性结核病；如果实际已有结核病却使用不合适的预防方案，可能造成治疗不足及耐药风险。

## 一起权衡获益和用药风险
是否需要预防性治疗，要结合个人发病风险、药物不良反应及相互作用判断，不能套用别人的方案。告知医生正在使用的所有药物，并讨论如何完成治疗。按约复诊，服药遇到困难或怀疑不良反应时及时联系治疗团队，不自行改药或加倍补服。需要支持时可以说明实际障碍；帮助完成治疗比责怪漏服更有用。
body.en:
## Prevention still needs assessment
Treatment for latent tuberculosis infection aims to reduce the risk of developing TB disease later. A positive test is not an instruction to start medicines yourself. Before preventive treatment, clinicians must assess for and exclude active TB disease. Using an unsuitable preventive approach when active disease is present can mean inadequate treatment and encourage drug resistance.

## Weigh benefits and medicine risks together
The decision considers individual progression risk, adverse effects and drug interactions; another person's plan may not fit. Tell clinicians about all medicines and discuss practical ways to complete treatment. Attend follow-up and contact the team about difficulties or suspected adverse effects rather than changing medicines or doubling missed doses yourself. Support should address barriers without blaming someone for missed treatment.

sources.title: CDC and National Tuberculosis Controllers Association · Guidelines for the Treatment of Latent Tuberculosis Infection (MMWR, 14 February 2020)

imageAlt: A blue seven-compartment pill organizer marked with the days of the week.

title.zh: 天热不只是口渴：怎样减少高温伤害
title.en: Hot weather is more than a thirst problem

summary.zh: 安排好活动时间，留意身体和身边人的状态。
summary.en: Plan around the heat and check on people who may need support.

body.zh:
## 给身体降温的时间
高温会给身体带来压力，老人、婴幼儿、慢性病患者以及户外工作者尤其需要关注。尽量避开一天中最热的时段，在阴凉或凉爽的室内休息，穿轻便衣物并规律补充水分。如果医生要求限制饮水，请遵循个人医疗建议。

## 发现危险信号
头晕、乏力、恶心和大量出汗可能提示身体受到热的影响。及时停止活动，到凉爽处休息并补充水分。若有人意识混乱、昏厥或状况迅速恶化，应立即呼叫急救，同时将其移到阴凉处并帮助降温。
body.en:
## Make room to cool down
Heat puts stress on the body. Older adults, young children, people with chronic conditions and outdoor workers may need particular attention. Avoid the hottest part of the day where possible, rest in a cool or shaded place, wear light clothing and drink water regularly. Follow individual medical advice if your fluid intake is restricted.

## Recognise warning signs
Dizziness, weakness, nausea and heavy sweating can signal heat-related illness. Stop activity, move somewhere cool and drink water. If someone becomes confused, faints or deteriorates rapidly, call emergency services immediately; move them to shade and help cool them while waiting.

sources.title: WHO · Health advice for hot weather (2025)

imageAlt: A hand filling a glass from a tap.
A selection of vegetables

title.zh: 夏天准备食物，生熟分开为什么重要？
title.en: Why raw and cooked foods need separate space

summary.zh: 砧板、餐具和储存方式都可能影响食物安全。
summary.en: Cutting boards, utensils and storage all matter for food safety.

body.zh:
## 别让食物交叉污染
生肉和海鲜可能携带致病微生物。处理后应清洗双手、刀具和台面；生食与熟食尽量使用不同的容器和砧板，避免生肉汁接触可以直接吃的食物。

## 不只看食物闻起来是否正常
食物安全还包括彻底加热、使用安全的水和原料，以及将食物保持在安全温度。容易腐败的食物不宜长时间放在室温下；气味正常也不能保证没有风险。
body.en:
## Prevent cross-contamination
Raw meat and seafood can carry harmful microorganisms. Wash hands, knives and surfaces after handling them. Use separate containers and cutting boards for raw foods and ready-to-eat foods where possible, and keep raw juices away from food that will not be cooked.

## Smell is not a safety test
Safer food also means cooking thoroughly, using safe water and ingredients, and keeping food at safe temperatures. Do not leave perishable food at room temperature for long periods. Food can be unsafe even when it smells normal.

sources.title: WHO · Five keys to safer food

title.zh: 游泳前，先看水域和同行的人
title.en: Before swimming, look at the water and your companions

summary.zh: 学习游泳、持续看护和了解水域风险，可以一起降低溺水风险。
summary.en: Swimming skills, close supervision and awareness of local conditions all help.

body.zh:
## 会游泳也要了解环境
泳池和天然水域的风险不同：水流、水深和能见度都可能变化。选择有安全管理的水域，了解现场规则和救援设备的位置，不要高估自己的体力。

## 看护不能分心
儿童在水中或水边时，需要成年人近距离、持续看护；手机和聊天都可能分散注意力。合适的救生衣能在适用情况下提供额外保护，但不能代替看护和游泳技能。发现危险时尽快寻求救援，不要贸然进入危险水域。
body.en:
## Swimming ability is only one part of safety
Pools and natural waters have different hazards. Currents, depth and visibility can change. Choose a supervised area where possible, learn the local rules and find the rescue equipment. Be realistic about your strength and the conditions.

## Supervision needs attention
Children in or near water need close, constant adult supervision. Phones and conversations can distract the person watching. A properly fitted life jacket can add protection where appropriate, but does not replace supervision or swimming skills. Seek help quickly in an emergency rather than entering dangerous water impulsively.

sources.title: CDC · Summer Swim Safety (2024)

imageAlt: Lane lines beneath the water of a swimming pool.

title.zh: 减少蚊虫叮咬，从衣物和积水做起
title.en: Fewer mosquito bites start with clothing and standing water

summary.zh: 防蚊不只依靠驱蚊产品，也要留意室内外积水。
summary.en: Repellent is one tool; standing water around the home matters too.

body.zh:
## 减少接触
蚊子白天和夜间都可能叮咬。外出时穿长袖长裤，按产品标签使用适合自己的驱蚊产品；如果同时使用防晒霜，先涂防晒霜，再使用驱蚊产品。给儿童使用时尤其要遵循标签上的年龄和用法限制。

## 检查容易积水的地方
花盆托盘、桶和其他容器可能积水，成为蚊子繁殖的场所。定期清理、倒空或遮盖这些容器，并维护门窗纱网。旅行后出现发热等不适时，应就医并说明旅行经历和可能的叮咬情况。
body.en:
## Reduce exposure
Mosquitoes can bite during the day and at night. Wear long sleeves and trousers outdoors and use a suitable repellent according to its label. When using sunscreen too, apply sunscreen first and repellent second. Follow age and application instructions carefully for children.

## Check for standing water
Plant saucers, buckets and other containers can collect water where mosquitoes breed. Empty, clean or cover them regularly, and maintain window screens. If you develop a fever or feel unwell after travel, seek medical advice and mention your travel and possible bites.

sources.title: CDC · How to protect against mosquito bites (2024)
CDC · Preventing Mosquito Bites

imageAlt: A close-up photograph of a Culex mosquito.

title.zh: 防晒不只靠防晒霜：先找阴凉
title.en: Sun protection starts with shade

summary.zh: 紫外线强的时候，衣物、帽子和阴凉处可以一起发挥作用。
summary.en: Shade, clothing and a hat work alongside sunscreen.

body.zh:
## 看紫外线，不只看气温
凉爽或多云的日子也可能有紫外线。户外活动前可以查看当地紫外线指数，强度较高时减少暴露，并在树荫或遮阳棚下休息。

## 多种保护一起用
宽檐帽、覆盖皮肤的衣物和合适的太阳镜能提供帮助。暴露的皮肤可以使用广谱防晒霜，按产品说明补涂；防晒霜不应成为长时间暴晒的理由。
body.en:
## UV exposure is not the same as heat
Ultraviolet radiation can reach you on cool or cloudy days. Check the local UV index before spending time outdoors, reduce exposure when it is high, and take breaks under trees or other shade.

## Combine protections
A broad-brimmed hat, clothing that covers skin, and suitable sunglasses can help. Apply broad-spectrum sunscreen to exposed skin and reapply as directed. Sunscreen is not a reason to stay in strong sun longer.

sources.title: WHO · Protecting against skin cancer (2024)

imageAlt: Beach umbrellas providing shade on a sunny day.

title.zh: 草丛活动后，检查身上有没有蜱
title.en: After time in tall grass, check for ticks

summary.zh: 蜱可藏在草木中，及时发现和正确处理很重要。
summary.en: Ticks can hide in vegetation; finding and removing them promptly matters.

body.zh:
## 出门前后的检查
蜱可能出现在草地、灌木和树林中。尽量走在小径中央，穿覆盖皮肤的衣物，回家后检查身体、衣物和随身物品。驱避产品应按标签使用。

## 发现附着的蜱
用干净的细尖镊子尽量靠近皮肤夹住蜱，平稳向上拉出，不要扭转或用火、油等刺激。清洁伤口和双手。之后几天到几周内若出现发热或皮疹，应就医并告诉医生叮咬时间和地点。
body.en:
## Check before and after going out
Ticks can live in grass, brush and wooded areas. Stay near the centre of trails, wear clothing that covers skin, and check your body, clothing and gear after returning. Follow the label when using repellent.

## If a tick is attached
Use clean fine-tipped tweezers to grasp it close to the skin and pull steadily upward. Do not twist it or use heat or oil. Clean your hands and the bite area. If fever or a rash develops over the following days or weeks, seek care and report when and where the bite happened.

sources.title: CDC · Preventing Tick Bites (2024)
CDC · What to Do After a Tick Bite

imageAlt: A tick on a green leaf.

title.zh: 腹泻时，为什么要留意脱水？
title.en: Why dehydration matters during diarrhoea

summary.zh: 腹泻会带走水分和盐分，儿童尤其需要密切观察。
summary.en: Diarrhoea causes loss of water and salts, especially concerning in children.

body.zh:
## 补充流失的水分
腹泻可能使身体失去水分和盐分。应及时补充液体；口服补液盐可用于补充流失的水分和电解质，按说明配制。婴幼儿更容易脱水，需要更密切的照顾。

## 什么时候求助
尿量明显减少、口干、站立头晕或儿童哭时泪少，都可能是脱水信号。出现明显脱水、便血、持续呕吐或无法喝水时应尽快就医。不要自行给儿童使用止泻或抗生素药物。
body.en:
## Replace lost fluid
Diarrhoea can cause the body to lose water and salts. Drink fluids; oral rehydration salts can replace both water and electrolytes when prepared as instructed. Babies and young children are particularly vulnerable to dehydration.

## When to seek help
Much less urine, a dry mouth, dizziness on standing, or a child crying without tears may indicate dehydration. Seek prompt care for signs of significant dehydration, blood in stool, persistent vomiting or inability to drink. Do not give a child anti-diarrhoeal medicines or antibiotics without medical advice.

sources.title: WHO · Diarrhoeal disease (2024)
CDC · Symptoms of E. coli Infection (2024)

imageAlt: A clear glass containing water.

title.zh: 游泳前，记得取下隐形眼镜
title.en: Take contact lenses out before swimming

summary.zh: 水和隐形眼镜接触可能增加眼部感染风险。
summary.en: Water and contact lenses can make eye infections more likely.

body.zh:
## 水并不是无菌的
泳池、湖水和自来水都可能含有微生物。戴隐形眼镜游泳或洗澡时，水接触镜片会增加眼部感染风险。下水前取下镜片；如果需要视力矫正，可以考虑配有度数的泳镜。

## 遇到不适不要硬撑
接触镜片前洗净并擦干双手，使用推荐的护理液，不用水冲洗或储存镜片。若眼睛疼痛、发红、畏光或视力模糊，取下镜片并尽快联系眼科医生。
body.en:
## Water is not sterile
Pools, lakes and tap water may contain microorganisms. Water touching contact lenses while swimming or showering increases the risk of an eye infection. Remove lenses first; prescription goggles may help if you need vision correction.

## Do not ignore discomfort
Wash and dry hands before handling lenses. Use the recommended lens solution rather than water for cleaning or storage. If you have eye pain, redness, light sensitivity or blurred vision, remove the lenses and contact an eye-care professional promptly.

sources.title: CDC · Keeping Water Away from Contact Lenses (2025)

imageAlt: Several colourful contact lens cases.

title.zh: 怀疑肺结核，为什么可能需要留痰？
title.en: Why a sputum sample may be needed for TB testing

summary.zh: 痰液检测帮助寻找病原，检查结果还要结合症状和其他检查。
summary.en: Sputum tests look for the bacteria alongside other clinical evidence.

body.zh:
## 痰液不是普通口水
当医生怀疑肺结核时，可能需要采集来自呼吸道深处的痰液，检测结核分枝杆菌。分子检测、涂片和培养各有作用，具体检查由医务人员根据情况决定。

## 检查结果需要结合判断
一次检查结果不能由读者自行解读为全部结论。医生还会考虑症状、影像和其他结果，必要时安排进一步检查。等待结果期间应遵循医疗人员的防护建议。
body.en:
## Sputum is not just saliva
When pulmonary TB is suspected, a clinician may request sputum from deep in the respiratory tract to look for TB bacteria. Molecular tests, smears and cultures each have different roles; the care team chooses appropriate tests.

## Results need context
A single result should not be interpreted in isolation. Clinicians also consider symptoms, imaging and other findings, and may arrange further tests. Follow the care team’s precautions while awaiting results.

sources.title: WHO · Tuberculosis (2026)

credit: Daniel Sone / National Cancer Institute / Unsplash
imageAlt: A laboratory researcher preparing samples for PCR; general laboratory context, not a TB test.

title.zh: 烟雾影响空气时，怎样减少吸入？
title.en: Reducing exposure when smoke affects the air

summary.zh: 空气质量差时调整活动安排，对呼吸系统疾病患者尤其重要。
summary.en: Adjusting outdoor activity matters particularly for people with respiratory conditions.

body.zh:
## 先了解空气情况
烟雾中的颗粒物会刺激眼睛和呼吸道，也可能加重心肺疾病。关注当地空气质量信息，污染严重时减少户外活动，尤其是运动和其他费力活动。

## 给敏感人群更多保护
儿童、老年人和患有心肺疾病的人可能更易受影响。尽量待在空气较清洁的室内，并按医嘱管理原有疾病。出现呼吸困难、胸痛等严重症状时，应立即寻求医疗帮助。
body.en:
## Check local air information
Particles in smoke can irritate eyes and airways and worsen heart or lung conditions. Follow local air-quality information and reduce outdoor exposure, especially strenuous activity, when pollution is severe.

## Protect people at greater risk
Children, older adults and people with heart or lung conditions may be more vulnerable. Spend time in cleaner indoor air when possible and follow your existing care plan. Seek immediate medical help for serious symptoms such as difficulty breathing or chest pain.

sources.title: CDC · Wildfire Smoke Tips (2024)

imageAlt: Wildfire smoke hanging over a forest.

title.zh: 作息总是变化，睡眠可以从哪里调整？
title.en: A steadier sleep schedule starts with small changes

summary.zh: 规律起床和白天接触自然光，有助于建立稳定作息。
summary.en: A consistent wake time and daylight can support a steadier routine.

body.zh:
## 规律比一次补觉更重要
睡眠不仅影响第二天的精神，也与长期健康有关。尽量保持规律的睡觉和起床时间，包括周末；白天接触自然光并保持适当活动，有助于建立稳定的日夜节律。

## 持续困难值得咨询
晚间为自己留出放松时间，减少可能干扰睡眠的因素。不同年龄需要的睡眠时长不同。如果长期睡不好、白天困倦明显，或他人发现你睡觉时呼吸异常，应咨询医疗专业人员。
body.en:
## Consistency matters
Sleep affects more than tomorrow’s energy. Try to keep a regular bedtime and wake time, including at weekends. Daylight and appropriate activity during the day can support a stable daily rhythm.

## Persistent problems deserve attention
Allow time to unwind and reduce things that interfere with sleep. Sleep needs differ by age. If poor sleep or pronounced daytime sleepiness persists, or someone notices unusual breathing during sleep, speak to a healthcare professional.

sources.title: CDC · About Sleep (2024)
CDC · Sleep and Heart Health (2024)

imageAlt: A person resting in bed under a blue blanket.
A person running outdoors

title.zh: 运动不一定是训练，走路也算
title.en: Movement does not have to look like a workout

summary.zh: 走路、骑车和家务都可以成为日常身体活动的一部分。
summary.en: Walking, cycling and household tasks can all count as physical activity.

body.zh:
## 从生活里的动作开始
身体活动包括步行、骑行、运动和一些家务，不一定要去健身房。平时活动较少的人可以从少量开始，逐渐增加；有慢性疾病或不确定如何运动时，可先咨询医生。

## 少坐一会儿也有意义
长时间坐着时，找机会起身、走动或伸展。选择自己喜欢、能够持续的活动，并考虑天气和身体状况，循序渐进比突然增加强度更容易坚持。
body.en:
## Start with everyday movement
Physical activity includes walking, cycling, sport and some household tasks; a gym is not essential. If you have been inactive, start with a little and build gradually. Ask a healthcare professional for advice when living with a chronic condition or unsure where to start.

## Break up long periods of sitting
Look for opportunities to stand, walk or stretch. Choose activities you enjoy and can sustain, taking weather and your own health into account. Gradual progress is easier to maintain than a sudden jump in intensity.

sources.title: WHO · Physical activity (2024)

title.zh: 发电机的尾气为什么危险？
title.en: Why generator exhaust is dangerous

summary.zh: 一氧化碳看不见、闻不到，不能靠气味判断是否安全。
summary.en: Carbon monoxide cannot be seen or smelled, so odour is not a warning.

body.zh:
## 开门也不等于安全
发电机尾气可能含一氧化碳，这种气体无色无味。不要在住宅、地下室或车库内使用发电机，即使门窗敞开也不安全；发电机应放在室外并远离门窗和通风口。

## 怀疑中毒立即离开
头痛、头晕、乏力和恶心可能是一氧化碳中毒的表现。如果怀疑暴露，立即到新鲜空气处并寻求急救，不要为了寻找设备或物品而留在危险区域。
body.en:
## An open door is not enough
Generator exhaust can contain carbon monoxide, a colourless, odourless gas. Never use a generator inside a home, basement or garage, even with doors or windows open. Keep it outdoors and away from doors, windows and vents.

## Leave immediately if exposure is suspected
Headache, dizziness, weakness and nausea can be signs of carbon monoxide poisoning. Move to fresh air and seek emergency help immediately. Do not remain in the dangerous area to retrieve equipment or belongings.

sources.title: CDC · Carbon Monoxide Hazard: Using a Generator (2024)

imageAlt: A worker beside a diesel generator in an engine room; not a demonstration of safe generator placement.
Scientist working at a microscope

title.zh: 结核病治疗中遇到困难，可以向谁求助？
title.en: When TB treatment is difficult, ask for support

summary.zh: 药物不适、复诊和生活安排，都值得及时与医疗团队沟通。
summary.en: Discuss side effects, appointments and practical difficulties with your care team.

body.zh:
## 不必独自应对
结核病可以治疗，但治疗需要遵循医疗团队制定的方案和随访安排。药物不适、上学工作安排、交通或费用压力，都可能让坚持治疗变得困难；及时说出来，医务人员才能一起寻找支持。

## 不要自行停药
症状改善不代表可以提前结束治疗。出现疑似药物不良反应时，及时联系医生；严重反应应立即就医。不要自行更改剂量或停药，医生会根据具体情况决定如何处理。
body.en:
## You do not have to manage alone
TB is treatable, but treatment and follow-up need to follow the care team’s plan. Side effects, school or work schedules, transport and costs can make treatment difficult. Tell the team early so you can look for support together.

## Do not stop on your own
Feeling better does not mean treatment can end early. Contact your clinician about possible side effects and seek urgent care for severe reactions. Do not change doses or stop treatment without medical advice; the team can decide what is appropriate.

sources.title: WHO · Tuberculosis (2026)

title.zh: 高温下意识混乱：这不是普通的中暑不适
title.en: Confusion in the heat is an emergency

summary.zh: 热射病可能危及生命，尽快呼救并帮助降温。
summary.en: Heat stroke can be life-threatening; call for help and start cooling.

body.zh:
## 辨认危险信号
在高温环境或剧烈活动后，如果有人出现意识混乱、言语不清、晕厥或抽搐，应警惕热射病。这是医疗急症；即使皮肤仍在出汗，也不能排除危险。

## 等待救援时降温
立即呼叫急救，将人移到阴凉处，去除多余衣物，用凉水、湿布和扇风帮助降温，并陪伴观察。意识不清或吞咽困难时不要喂水。不要等到体温测量完毕才呼救。
body.en:
## Recognise the danger
Confusion, slurred speech, collapse or seizures after heat exposure or strenuous activity may signal heat stroke. It is a medical emergency. Someone can still be sweating and have a dangerous heat illness.

## Cool while waiting for help
Call emergency services immediately. Move the person to shade, remove extra clothing, and cool with water, wet cloths and moving air. Stay with them. Do not give drinks to someone who is confused or cannot swallow safely, and do not delay the call while looking for a thermometer.

sources.title: CDC · Heat-Related Illnesses: What to Look For and What to Do (2017)

imageAlt: A thermometer showing hot weather

title.zh: 孩子腹泻时，怎样留意脱水？
title.en: Watching for dehydration when a child has diarrhoea

summary.zh: 尿量、精神状态和能否喝下液体，比单看排便次数更有帮助。
summary.en: Urine output, alertness and ability to drink matter alongside stool frequency.

body.zh:
## 关注变化
腹泻和呕吐会带走水分与盐分。婴幼儿更容易脱水，尿布明显变少、口干、哭时泪少、异常困倦都需要留意。继续母乳或配方奶喂养；不要为了补水自行稀释配方奶。

## 及时寻求帮助
口服补液盐应按包装说明配制，是否使用可咨询专业人员。如果孩子喝不下或持续吐、出现血便、精神差或脱水迹象，应尽快就医；婴儿出现这些情况尤其不宜等待。
body.en:
## Notice the changes
Diarrhoea and vomiting remove water and salts. Babies and young children can dehydrate quickly: fewer wet nappies, a dry mouth, fewer tears or unusual drowsiness deserve attention. Continue breast or formula feeds; do not dilute formula to provide extra water.

## Ask for help in time
Prepare oral rehydration solution according to its instructions and ask a professional when unsure. Seek prompt care if the child cannot keep fluids down, has blood in the stool, seems unusually unwell or shows signs of dehydration. Do not wait with a baby who is deteriorating.

sources.title: NHS · Food poisoning (reviewed 2024)
NHS · Dehydration

imageAlt: A child drinking water at breakfast

title.zh: 乙肝预防为什么从出生时就开始？
title.en: Why hepatitis B prevention begins at birth

summary.zh: 孕期筛查、新生儿接种和后续随访共同降低母婴传播风险。
summary.en: Pregnancy screening, infant vaccination and follow-up work together.

body.zh:
## 尽早预防传播
乙肝病毒可在出生时由母亲传给婴儿，婴幼儿感染后发展为慢性感染的风险较高。世界卫生组织建议新生儿出生后尽早接种乙肝疫苗，并按免疫程序完成后续剂次。

## 根据家庭情况安排
孕期乙肝筛查结果要告知产科和儿科团队。若母亲感染乙肝或感染状态不明，婴儿可能还需要乙肝免疫球蛋白和专门随访；具体时间与程序应遵循当地免疫规定和医生指导。
body.en:
## Prevent transmission early
Hepatitis B can pass from a mother to her baby around birth. Infection acquired in infancy is more likely to become chronic. WHO recommends hepatitis B vaccination as soon as possible after birth, followed by the remaining doses in the schedule.

## Make a plan with the care team
Share pregnancy screening results with maternity and paediatric providers. When the mother has hepatitis B or her status is unknown, the baby may also need hepatitis B immune globulin and specific follow-up. Follow local immunisation guidance and individual medical advice.

sources.title: WHO · Recommended routine immunization (January 2025)
CDC · Hepatitis B Immunization (2025)

imageAlt: A healthcare professional vaccinating a young child

title.zh: 错过一针疫苗，接种记录还有用吗？
title.en: A missed vaccine dose does not erase the record

summary.zh: 带上接种记录咨询补种，通常不必自行从头开始。
summary.en: Bring vaccination records to a clinician and ask about catch-up.

body.zh:
## 先找接种记录
旅行、搬家或生病可能打乱接种计划。错过一次预约后，先查看接种证或其他记录，联系当地接种门诊，说明年龄、已接种的剂次和时间。

## 补种不是自行安排
很多多剂次疫苗的间隔变长后不必重新开始，但不同疫苗有年龄和间隔要求，规定也会因地区而异。请由接种人员结合当地程序制定补种计划，不要自行推算或重复接种。
body.en:
## Find the record first
Travel, moving or illness can interrupt an immunisation schedule. Check the vaccination record and contact a vaccination clinic with the person’s age, previous doses and dates.

## Catch-up needs an individual plan
Many multi-dose vaccine series do not need restarting when the interval is longer than planned, but age and minimum-interval rules vary by vaccine and country. A vaccination professional can use local guidance to plan missing doses; do not calculate or repeat doses on your own.

sources.title: CDC · 2025 child and adolescent catch-up schedule

imageAlt: A healthcare worker placing a bandage on a child's arm after a flu vaccination

title.zh: 泳池里有氯，为什么腹泻时仍不该下水？
title.en: Why diarrhoea and swimming do not mix

summary.zh: 部分病原体在消毒泳池中也能存活较长时间。
summary.en: Some germs can survive for days even in properly chlorinated pools.

body.zh:
## 氯不能立刻消灭所有病原体
有些引起腹泻的病原体可通过泳池水传播。隐孢子虫对氯的耐受性较强，即使泳池维护正常，也可能存活多日。吞入受污染的水会增加感染机会。

## 保护自己和他人
腹泻时不要游泳，也尽量不要吞咽泳池水。确诊隐孢子虫感染的人，应遵循医生建议；美国疾控中心建议腹泻完全停止后再等待两周再游泳。其他病因的返泳时间以当地规定和医疗建议为准。
body.en:
## Chlorine is not instant protection
Some germs that cause diarrhoea spread through recreational water. Cryptosporidium is particularly resistant to chlorine and can survive for days even in a properly maintained pool. Swallowing contaminated water creates an opportunity for infection.

## Protect everyone in the water
Stay out of the pool while you have diarrhoea and avoid swallowing pool water. For confirmed cryptosporidiosis, CDC advises waiting two weeks after diarrhoea has completely stopped before swimming. For other illnesses, follow local rules and your clinician’s advice.

sources.title: CDC · Clinical Care of Crypto (2024)
CDC · What to Do When There is Poop in the Pool (2024)

imageAlt: Children playing in a swimming pool

title.zh: 食物过敏：为什么共用餐具也要留意？
title.en: Food allergy and the problem of shared utensils

summary.zh: 少量过敏原可能通过餐具、台面或食物接触进入另一道菜。
summary.en: Small amounts of an allergen can transfer through utensils and surfaces.

body.zh:
## 留意交叉接触
食物过敏时，风险不只来自食谱里明显的原料。切过花生的刀、共用的砧板或烹饪器具，都可能把过敏原带到另一份食物中。烹饪并不能可靠地去除过敏原。

## 提前沟通
准备或购买食物前，说明需要避免的具体食物，核对配料与加工信息，并尽可能使用清洁、分开的工具。严重过敏者应遵循个人急救计划；出现呼吸困难、喉舌肿胀或意识改变时立即呼叫急救。
body.en:
## Cross-contact matters
A food allergen can transfer from a knife used for peanuts, a shared board or cooking equipment into another dish. The risk is not limited to ingredients named in a recipe, and cooking does not reliably remove allergens.

## Speak up before eating
Explain the specific food to avoid, check ingredients and processing information, and use clean, separate equipment where possible. People with severe allergies should follow their personal emergency plan. Breathing difficulty, swelling of the tongue or throat, or altered consciousness needs emergency help.

sources.title: CDC · Food Allergy Reactions (2024)

imageAlt: Peanuts in a glass bowl

title.zh: 糖尿病与结核病：为什么医生会同时关注？
title.en: Why diabetes matters in tuberculosis care

summary.zh: 糖尿病会增加感染结核菌后发展为结核病的风险。
summary.en: Diabetes can increase the risk of TB disease after infection.

body.zh:
## 风险增加，不等于一定患病
糖尿病会影响身体应对感染的能力。感染结核菌的人如果同时患糖尿病，发展为结核病的风险可能更高；但这不意味着每个糖尿病患者都有结核病。

## 一起管理两种情况
如果有持续咳嗽、发热、盗汗或体重下降，应就医并告知糖尿病史。结核病和糖尿病的治疗需要医疗团队共同评估，包括血糖监测和药物安排，不要自行停药或改变方案。
body.en:
## Higher risk is not a diagnosis
Diabetes affects how the body responds to infection. A person with diabetes who has TB infection may be more likely to develop TB disease, but diabetes does not mean a person has TB.

## Manage both conditions together
Seek care for a persistent cough, fever, night sweats or weight loss and mention diabetes to the clinician. Managing TB alongside diabetes calls for coordinated care, including glucose monitoring and medication review. Do not stop or change treatment independently.

sources.title: CDC · TB Risk and People with Diabetes
CDC · TB risk factors (2023 report)

imageAlt: A person checking blood glucose

title.zh: 被昆虫蜇伤后，哪些变化需要求助？
title.en: After an insect sting, which changes need help?

summary.zh: 局部不适常可缓解，但呼吸困难和口咽肿胀需要急救。
summary.en: Local discomfort often settles, but breathing problems need emergency care.

body.zh:
## 先处理局部
如果皮肤里留下蜂刺，可用指甲或卡片边缘轻轻侧向刮去，然后用肥皂和水清洗。用布包住冷敷物敷在肿胀处，避免抓挠。局部疼痛、瘙痒和肿胀常会逐渐好转。

## 识别严重反应
嘴唇、舌头或喉咙肿胀，呼吸困难、晕厥或明显意识变化，可能是严重过敏反应，应立即呼叫急救并遵循个人急救计划。口腔、喉咙或眼睛附近被蜇，或症状加重、出现脓液，也需要及时评估。
body.en:
## Start with the local area
If a bee stinger remains, gently scrape it sideways with a fingernail or card edge, then wash with soap and water. Apply a cold pack wrapped in cloth and avoid scratching. Local pain, itching and swelling commonly improve over time.

## Recognise a severe reaction
Swelling of the lips, tongue or throat, breathing difficulty, collapse or altered consciousness may indicate a severe allergic reaction. Call emergency services and follow the person’s emergency plan. A sting in the mouth or throat, near the eye, or worsening symptoms and pus also need prompt assessment.

sources.title: NHS Cornwall · Insect bites and stings (2024)

imageAlt: A bee on a flower

title.zh: 防晒霜上的 SPF 和广谱是什么意思？
title.en: What SPF and broad spectrum mean on sunscreen

summary.zh: SPF 主要反映 UVB 防护，广谱还关注 UVA。
summary.en: SPF describes UVB protection; broad spectrum also covers UVA.

body.zh:
## 看懂两个标识
SPF 反映防晒产品对导致晒伤的 UVB 辐射的防护程度，并不单独说明 UVA 防护。标有广谱的产品则强调同时防护 UVA 和 UVB。选择时结合产品说明、肤质和活动情况。

## 不是涂一次就万无一失
在暴露部位足量使用，并按标签说明、游泳或出汗情况补涂。阴凉处、遮盖皮肤的衣物、帽子和太阳镜同样重要；防晒霜不能让长时间暴晒变得安全。
body.en:
## Two different labels
SPF describes protection against sunburn-causing UVB radiation; it does not by itself describe UVA protection. A broad-spectrum product is designed to protect against both UVA and UVB. Choose with the product instructions, your skin and planned activity in mind.

## Reapply and combine protection
Apply enough to exposed skin and reapply as directed, especially after swimming or sweating. Shade, covering clothing, a hat and sunglasses also matter. Sunscreen does not make prolonged exposure to strong sun risk-free.

sources.title: WHO · Protecting against skin cancer (2024)

imageAlt: Sunscreen and sandals on a beach

title.zh: 旧油漆和灰尘：为什么要关注儿童铅暴露？
title.en: Old paint, dust and the risk of lead exposure

summary.zh: 铅可能损害儿童发育，怀疑含铅材料时不要自行打磨。
summary.en: Lead can harm child development; suspected lead paint needs expert handling.

body.zh:
## 儿童更容易受到伤害
铅是一种有毒物质，会影响多个身体系统，儿童正在发育的神经系统尤其脆弱。含铅油漆和受污染的灰尘只是可能来源之一，不能通过外观判断材料是否含铅。

## 不要自行打磨可疑材料
翻修旧建筑或家具前，如怀疑油漆含铅，应咨询当地专业人员，避免自行打磨或刮除而扬起粉尘。怀疑儿童接触铅时，请向医疗人员说明接触情况，是否检测由专业人员判断。
body.en:
## Children are especially vulnerable
Lead is toxic and can affect several body systems. Children’s developing nervous systems are particularly vulnerable. Lead paint and contaminated dust are possible sources, but appearance alone cannot show whether a material contains lead.

## Do not sand suspected paint yourself
Before renovating an older building or furniture, seek local expert advice if lead paint is possible. Scraping or sanding can spread dust. If a child may have been exposed, tell a healthcare professional what happened; they can determine whether testing is appropriate.

sources.title: WHO · Global call to action on lead poisoning prevention (2024)
WHO · Chemical safety: Lead poisoning

imageAlt: Peeling paint on an old wall

title.zh: 肉看起来熟了，就一定安全吗？
title.en: Does cooked-looking meat guarantee safety?

summary.zh: 颜色不能可靠反映食物内部温度，食物温度计可以帮助检查。
summary.en: Colour alone does not reliably show the internal cooking temperature.

body.zh:
## 外观不是可靠的温度计
肉类表面的颜色或汁液颜色不能可靠说明内部是否达到安全温度。食物温度计可以帮助检查最厚部位，尤其是鸡肉、肉馅和较厚的肉块。

## 同时注意操作卫生
根据当地权威食品安全建议确认不同食物的安全温度，清洗探针，并避免让熟食接触盛过生肉的器具。冷藏、彻底加热和生熟分开需要一起做到。
body.en:
## Appearance is not a thermometer
The colour of meat or its juices does not reliably show whether the centre reached a safe temperature. A food thermometer can check the thickest part, particularly for poultry, ground meat and thick cuts.

## Keep handling safe too
Use local authoritative guidance for the appropriate temperature for each food. Clean the probe and keep cooked food away from utensils that held raw meat. Chilling, thorough cooking and separation all matter.

sources.title: CDC · Always Use a Food Thermometer (2024)
WHO · Five keys to safer food

imageAlt: A barbecue thermometer

title.zh: 接触结核病后检测阴性，为什么还要复查？
title.en: Why a negative TB test may need a repeat

summary.zh: 感染后的免疫反应需要时间，初次检测的时间点很重要。
summary.en: The immune response takes time, so the timing of the first test matters.

body.zh:
## 检测有一个窗口期
接触有传染性的肺结核患者后，身体可能需要数周才能对结核感染检测产生可测出的免疫反应。接触结束不久就得到阴性结果，不能单凭这次结果排除近期感染。

## 跟随当地的复查安排
美国疾控中心建议，部分接触者在最后一次接触后的八至十周复测。具体时间和措施应以当地防疫人员及医生的评估为准。出现持续咳嗽、发热或体重下降等症状时，应及时就医，不必等到复查日期。
body.en:
## There is a window period
After exposure to someone with infectious pulmonary TB, it can take weeks for the immune response to become detectable. A negative test soon after the last exposure cannot by itself exclude a recent infection.

## Follow the local review plan
CDC guidance recommends repeat testing for some contacts eight to ten weeks after their last exposure. The timing and next steps should be agreed with local public health professionals or a clinician. Seek care promptly for symptoms such as persistent cough, fever or weight loss rather than waiting for the repeat test.

sources.title: CDC · Contact investigation guidelines
